jobs.title: Parts Room Clerk
jobs.description:
Pay: $28.00/hr

Shift: Monday - Friday 7am -5pm

Location: Pen Argyl, PA

Position:

The Parts Room Clerk will be responsible for keeping the parts room organized and making sure all inventory is correctly put away. This individual must be capable of using a computer, comfortable speaking with vendors and have experience with doing cycle counts.

Duties/Responsibilities:

• Receive and verify the content of materials received from vendors
• Create purchase requisitions within ERP system
• Enter various transactions in EPR system
• Receive materials in the ERP system
• Unpack materials into the company stockroom
• Stock materials on the storeroom shelves
• Transact part numbers and quantities into the inventory database
• Receive material requests and issue parts and materials as requested
• Maintain accurate record of all issued parts and materials
• Monitor and maintain inventory accuracy through physical inventories and cycle counts
• Schedule vendors for services, i.e. forklift maintenance
• Research parts, tools, supplies, etc for purchase based on company needs

Planning;

• Work with Maintenance Manager and Production Management to optimize maintenance and production schedules and efficiencies
• Organize resources in order to optimize productivity
• Inform maintenance of repair needs

Communication:

• Constant communication with the Maintenance Manager, Maintenance Department employees, Production Supervisors, Production employees, etc. to help ensure the most productive and cost effective plan is obtained.
• Be able to read and comprehend simple instructions, correspondence
• Be able to write simple correspondence and/or memos
• Display exceptional communication and customer service skills internally and with outside vendors
• Actively participates in meetings and share relevant information with the team

• Must be able to operate a computer
• Knowledge of word processing software; spreadsheet software; internet software; database software
• Be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily
• Have the knowledge, skill, and ability to operate a forklift
• Must have a valid driver’s license and a good driving record
• Be able to add, subtract, multiply and divide American money, weight measurement, volume and distance
• Be able to reason and apply common sense
• Be able to handle problems, situations effectively
• Be able to answer questions and resolve problems in a timely manner with team involvement
• Experience in Microsoft D365 preferred

Why Work at Techo-Bloc?

We offer competitive pay, strong benefits, and a workplace where people genuinely take pride in what they do.

Perks & Benefits:

✅ Weekly Pay

✅ Vacation + Sick Time

✅ Medical / Dental / Vision

✅ 401(k) + Company Match

✅ Life Insurance + Disability Coverage

✅ Employee Discount on Products

✅ Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

✅ Uniform Provided After 3 Months

✅ Boot Reimbursement Program

✅ Training & Career Development

The Team & Culture

Our crew is hardworking, motivated, and proud of the products we make. We thrive in a fast-moving environment, support one another when challenges come up, and value a “can-do” attitude. If you’re eager to learn and want a stable job with a company that’s growing — we’d love to meet you.

Ready to Join Us?

Apply today and build something you can be proud of — with a team that works hard and wins together.

Physical Requirements:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 50 pounds and occasionally up to 80 pounds. Must be able to closely inspect and continually monitor all machines in the production process.  While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to move throughout the facility. The employee is frequently required to reach with hands and arms talk or hear and smell. The employee is occasionally required to remain stationary; ascend and descend steps and ladders; and position self in tight spaces.

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

jobs.title: Nursing Faculty - Sacramento - $10,000 Sign-on Bonus
jobs.description:
Shape the Future of Nursing Education

In this role, you’ll help shape the next generation of healthcare providers through high‑quality nursing education delivered in classroom and clinical settings. You’ll play a vital role in teaching, mentoring, evaluating, and supporting students while contributing to the broader academic and professional community in alignment with Chamberlain’s mission.

What You’ll Do

• Teach assigned nursing courses across classroom, online, clinical, lab, and simulation environments using engaging, evidence‑based, and technology‑enabled methods.
• Contribute to curriculum development and implement approved course content and teaching materials.
• Put students first—build meaningful relationships, understand individual needs, and foster an inclusive learning environment that supports success.
• Evaluate student performance and provide timely, constructive feedback and remediation as needed.
• Lead or support clinical, lab, and simulation experiences, connecting theory to practice and promoting safe, ethical, and professional nursing practice.
• Support student and new faculty success through guidance, coaching, and mentoring.
• Participate in professional service activities such as committees, graduation, and program evaluation.
• Engage in scholarship related to teaching and nursing practice by researching, applying, and sharing new knowledge.
• Maintain subject‑matter expertise and teaching effectiveness through ongoing professional development.
• Apply and uphold academic and student‑related policies, including exams, attendance, and grading standards, staying current with updates.
• Perform other duties as assigned and comply with all policies and standards.

How You’ll Succeed

• Anticipate and respond to student needs while helping remove barriers to success.
• Align daily work with Chamberlain’s vision and strategic priorities.
• Seek feedback, implement new initiatives, and use data to continuously improve student outcomes.
• Collaborate effectively with internal and external partners in a matrixed environment.
• Demonstrate ethical practice, accountability, and a commitment to shared success.

What Success Looks Like

• Students achieve strong outcomes, including NCLEX, KAM, and other program metrics.
• High levels of student engagement and satisfaction reflected in evaluations and NPS feedback.
• All academic work meets licensure and regulatory requirements.
• Grading and feedback are accurate, rubric‑aligned, timely, and high quality.
• Effective use of technology, data, and AI tools to enhance teaching and learning.
• Ongoing faculty contributions to service, scholarship, and a positive academic culture aligned with Chamberlain’s values.

Required Qualifications

• Master’s degree in nursing.
• At least 2 years of professional experience in a field related to the teaching discipline.
• Active, unencumbered licensure or certification required to practice professionally in the discipline, as applicable to assignment.
• Education and experience that align with state, regulatory, and licensure requirements for assigned courses.
• Demonstrated ability to effectively teach assigned courses based on education, experience, and professional preparation.

Preferred Qualifications

• Doctorate degree in nursing.

Teaching & Professional Skills

• Excellent communication skills, sound judgment, and a high level of initiative.
• Proven ability to create engaging, inclusive learning environments and manage conflict effectively.
• Strong emotional and social intelligence, with the ability to recognize student needs and respond with empathy.
• Experience collaborating with faculty, Extended Service Teams, and clinical partners to support student outcomes.

Technology & Innovation

• Proficiency with learning management systems, simulation equipment, and online teaching platforms.
• Growing ability to leverage technology, data, and AI tools to enhance teaching and learning effectiveness.

Scholarship & Professional Development

Demonstrates scholarship appropriate to academic rank, including at least one example in one of the following areas:

• Scholarship of Discovery
• Scholarship of Integration
• Scholarship of Practice/Application
• Scholarship of Teaching and Learning
• Scholarship activities must be public, peer‑reviewable, and accessible for use by others, as outlined in the faculty handbook.

Compliance & Credentialing

• Maintains current regulatory, licensure, and practice credentials as required by assignment.
• For faculty working in clinical settings, meets all additional compliance requirements outlined in the Faculty Compliance Packet.
• Additional state‑specific requirements may apply; refer to the Online Faculty Licensure Requirements Document for details related to your designated specialty.

jobs.title: Cyber Security Manager (Governance, Risk and Compliance)
jobs.description:
Remote Approved - Must be in USA.

We are seeking an experienced Security Manager to lead the governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) pillar of our Enterprise Cybersecurity program. This people-leadership role owns the cybersecurity governance operating rhythm, executive and board-level reporting, third-party security risk management, data security program management, security awareness, and cybersecurity policy and compliance activities. The Security Manager is accountable for the cadence, quality, and continuity of these programs — turning security metrics, risk data, and regulatory requirements into clear, actionable insight for leadership and the Board.

The ideal candidate combines strong program and people management with a solid understanding of security frameworks (such as NIST CSF and CMMC), risk management, and stakeholder engagement across IT, Legal, business units, and external partners. This role reports to the Sr. Dir, Enterprise Cyber Security and directly manages analysts supporting governance, risk, and awareness functions.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Cybersecurity Governance & Reporting

• Own the cybersecurity governance program, including the Monthly Cybersecurity Metrics Report and Quarterly Board Dashboard measures.

• Define and maintain cybersecurity metrics, KPIs, and KRIs; track program maturity against the NIST CSF; and drive strategic initiatives, risks, and governance commitments to closure.

• Coordinate identity governance activities, including monthly AD account reviews, access certifications, and IAM metrics reporting.

• Coordinate cybersecurity inputs for the annual cyber insurance renewal and annual Incident Response Plan update and Management tabletop exercise.

Data Security Program Management

• Lead data discovery and classification governance across IT, Legal, and business stakeholders, tracking data risk reduction and reporting progress through program metrics.

Third-Party & Supplier Cyber Risk Management

• Manage the third-party cyber risk assessment program, including new third-party service reviews, periodic reassessments, critical-supplier (direct and indirect) assessments, and FBIN questionnaires.

• Track and drive remediation of third-party and supplier risks and integrate cyber-risk data into governance reporting.

Security Vendor Administration & Operational Oversight

• Provide governance administration for cybersecurity vendors (PO creation, invoice processing, DocuSign workflows, renewal tracking) and support legal/contract activities such as NDA/MNDA reviews and security questionnaire responses.

Cybersecurity Policies, Standards & Compliance

• Maintain cybersecurity governance documentation, coordinating annual policy and standard updates, approvals, publication and archive.

• Support compliance initiatives including SOX controls, CMMC readiness, NIST CSF maturity reporting, SOC 2 assurance, and audit evidence collection and manage governance repositories and control attestations.

Security Awareness Program

• Administer the enterprise security awareness program, including annual training, new hire training, National Cybersecurity Awareness Month, quarterly phishing simulations and ad hoc awareness articles on the FBIN intranet.

Leadership & Continuous Improvement

• Manage, mentor, and develop analysts supporting governance, risk, and awareness functions.

• Partner with cross-functional teams: IT, Legal, connected product, and business units to embed security best practices and continuously improve the maturity, efficiency, and clarity of processes and reporting.

KEY COMPETENCIES

• Collaborate: Build partnerships and work collaboratively with others to meet shared objectives.

• Communicate Effectively: Develop and deliver multi-mode communications that convey a clear understanding of the unique needs of different audiences.

• Instill Trust: Gain the confidence and trust of others through honesty, integrity, and authenticity.

• Builds Effective Teams: Attract, develop, and retain talent to meet current and future organizational needs.

• Drives Results: Consistently achieve results, even under challenging circumstances.

• Decision Quality: Make sound and timely decisions that keep the organization moving forward.

• Plans and Aligns: Plan and prioritize work to meet commitments aligned with organizational goals.

• Ensures Accountability: Hold self and others accountable to meet commitments.

• Bachelor's degree in Information Security, Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

• Minimum of 7+ years of overall technology experience, with at least 5+ years in an information security, cybersecurity, or GRC role.

• Demonstrated experience owning cybersecurity governance, risk, or compliance programs and producing executive- or board-level reporting.

• Working knowledge of security frameworks such as NIST CSF and CMMC, and of enterprise risk and third-party risk management practices.

• Experience coordinating security awareness, data security, or identity governance programs across cross-functional stakeholders.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex security topics for technical and non-technical audiences, including leadership.

• Strong analytical, organizational, and program-management skills.

PREFERRED:

• Prior people-leadership or team-management experience.

• Relevant certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CRISC, CISA, or CompTIA Security+.

• Experience with GRC and risk platforms and data security tooling.

• Familiarity with SOC 2, cyber insurance renewal processes, and audit/assurance coordination.

• Experience supporting incident response governance and tabletop exercises.

jobs.title: ANALISTA SHE (SEGURIDAD INDUSTRIAL)
jobs.description:
Vacante tercerizada

Apoyar en campo y en la gestión administrativa el cumplimiento de las normas, políticas y procedimientos de Seguridad, Salud y Medio Ambiente (SHE) en la bodega de Comayagua, la bodega de Dos Caminos y la planta de trillado de Villanueva, contribuyendo a prevenir accidentes, enfermedades profesionales e impactos ambientales. Asimismo, mantener ordenados y actualizados los registros y la evidencia documental que respaldan el cumplimiento legal y el Sistema de Gestión Integrado de SHE.

Principio fundamental del puesto: no se limita a llenar registros. Cada recorrido, entrega de equipo o charla debe ejecutarse con presencia en campo, observando las condiciones reales de trabajo y reportando de inmediato al Coordinador SHE cualquier condición o acto inseguro.

Apoyo de seguridad en campo

•  Realizar recorridos diarios de seguridad en la bodega de Comayagua, la bodega de Dos Caminos y la planta de trillado de Villanueva, observando y reportando el cumplimiento de las políticas y procedimientos de SHE.

•  Apoyar las inspecciones periódicas de instalaciones, equipos y áreas de trabajo, registrando hallazgos y actualizando el estado de su cierre.

•  Revisar que los trabajos de alto riesgo cuenten con su permiso de trabajo y reportar cualquier desviación.

•  Reportar de inmediato al Coordinador SHE cualquier condición o acto inseguro y solicitar la suspensión de la tarea cuando exista peligro inminente.

•  Entregar y registrar la dotación de equipo de protección personal e insumos de higiene y seguridad, y revisar su uso correcto.

•  Revisar y registrar el estado de extintores, botiquines, señalización y equipos de emergencia.

Investigación de accidentes e incidentes

•  Apoyar en la recopilación de información, fotografías y testimonios para la investigación de accidentes e incidentes.

•  Registrar los reportes de incidentes, actos y condiciones inseguras.

•  Actualizar el seguimiento de las acciones correctivas y preventivas.

Gestión de riesgos

•  Apoyar en la actualización de las matrices de riesgo de los tres sitios.

•  Apoyar el seguimiento de las recomendaciones de los estudios de riesgo.

•  Acompañar en campo los trabajos de contratistas y los proyectos de CAPEX, reportando desviaciones de seguridad.

Cumplimiento legal y Sistema de Gestión

•  Archivar y mantener ordenada la información documental y la evidencia de cumplimiento legal y del Sistema de Gestión de SHE.

•  Apoyar en la actualización de los procedimientos e instructivos del Sistema de Gestión Integrado de SHE.

•  Mantener actualizados los registros, controles e indicadores del área.

Higiene industrial, salud ocupacional y medio ambiente

•  Apoyar en la ejecución del programa de higiene industrial y ambiental, incluyendo las mediciones de material particulado.

•  Coordinar la logística y el registro de los exámenes ocupacionales del personal.

Capacitación y cultura de seguridad

•  Apoyar la logística y llevar el registro de asistencia del programa de charlas, capacitaciones y certificación del personal.

•  Apoyar en las inducciones de seguridad e impartir charlas cortas de seguridad al personal.

Experiencia Laboral

• 6 meses a 1 año en seguridad industrial o en operaciones industriales o agroindustriales (deseable).

Conocimientos Técnicos

Conocimientos y/o certificaciones en:

• Seguridad industrial y medio ambiente.
• Básicos de cumplimiento legal: Reglamento General de Medidas Preventivas de Accidentes de Trabajo y Enfermedades Profesionales.

jobs.title: Clinical Operations Coordinator RN- Canning Thoracic Institute Full time
jobs.description:
This role will oversee pulmonary, sleep and thoracic surgery

The Clinical Operations Coordinator, RN reflects the mission, vision, and values of NM, adheres to the organization’s Code of Ethics and Corporate Compliance Program, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and all other regulatory and accreditation standards.

• The Clinical Operations Coordinator, RN is responsible for supervising the daily clinical operations of practice sites, supervising clinical support staff, coordinating clinical staff and provider schedules, and performing service recovery as necessary. The operations Coordinator is the clinical lead and subject matter expert at the local level to ensure staff knowledge, competence and processes align with evidence based high quality patient care. Under the clinical direction of the Director, Clinical Practice and the administrative direction of the Clinical/Practice Administrator, the Operations Coordinator participates in the planning, leading, and organizing of activities relating to quality patient care in the practice. Direct clinical patient care would be provided less than twenty percent of the time in this role. The Operations Coordinator may oversee multiple sites or departments within RMG.

Responsibilities:

• Supervise and direct the office’s clinical support staff, manage workload distribution and prioritization of tasks.
• Participate in interviewing, hiring, training, progressive discipline, dismissals, and performance appraisals.
• Oversee and direct day to day office clinical operations within budget guidelines.
• Assist with managing providers schedule templates and optimize patient care hours to enhance productivity.
• Schedule staff and allocate resources across hours of operation to maximize patient access and satisfaction, provider productivity and efficiency, and staff productivity.
• Responsible for front-line communication with staff to receive and provide feedback regarding clinical workflow, quality and productivity.
• Ensure that service excellence is delivered and perform service recovery whenever necessary.
• Manage medical surgical supplies within budget.
• Ensure accuracy of all data collection and data entry by site staff through training and compliance monitoring and facilitate and oversee flow of information to and from central administrative offices.
• Conduct office staff meetings on a regular basis in coordination with practice leadership.
• Attend and actively participate in leadership meetings.
• Ensure that patient dignity and confidentiality are always maintained.

Additional Functions

jobs.title: Senior Engineer, Global Technology - Enterprise Core Platform
jobs.description:
Why This Role Matters

As a Senior Engineer, you will help shape the future of the Enterprise Core Platform (ECP), the internal developer platform on Azure that every engineering team at Expeditors builds on. We are turning ECP from shared infrastructure into a platform engineering organization that runs like a product: self-service, declarative, and built for both engineers and the AI agents they work with. This role will help build where the platform is going next.

Team and Technology

You will join the Enterprise Core Platform engineering team, working in a small team using Kanban and monthly backlog planning. Each domain is led by a TPM and an engineering lead who act as cofounders, with autonomy to build and decide in their area and accountability for the result. The platform spans Azure Kubernetes Service, GitOps, infrastructure as code, identity, secrets, policy as code, and a new control plane written in Go. The team also builds AI-native capabilities including MCP servers, agent skills, spec-driven workflows, and the guardrails around them.

What Success Looks Like

• First 30 days: run the control plane locally, ship a reviewed change within the first two weeks, and shadow the on-call rotation.
• First 90 days: own one capability end to end (design note, implementation, tests, rollout to a dev environment), and ship one agent-facing capability, such as an MCP tool, skill, or golden path, that another team uses.
• First year: lead a stage of the control plane roadmap, carry a platform domain through a migration, and raise how the rest of the team builds with agents.

Key Areas of Impact

Technical Depth and Delivery

• Build and operate the Go control plane and its providers across identity, source control, GitOps, secrets management, templates, and the path to production.
• Own capabilities end to end through design, implementation, testing, reviewed pull requests, rollout, and operational support.

Architectural Scale

• Modernize Azure Kubernetes Service, GitOps, infrastructure as code, identity, secrets, and policy as code, leading migrations and helping define platform ownership.
• Help evolve ECP from pipeline-based provisioning to a declarative control plane that reconciles state, corrects drift, and enables safe AI-native workflows.

Team Collaboration Scale

• Partner within a small team where TPM and engineering leads share ownership, autonomy, technical decisions, and accountability for results.
• Build with coordinated agents using implementation, adversarial review, and independent verification while remaining accountable for every line you merge.

Influence and Advocacy

• Use reviewed pull requests, design notes, and architecture decision records (ADRs) to communicate technical decisions and help raise engineering practices across the team.
• Help shape what the platform owns, how teams use agent-facing capabilities, and how engineers build safely and effectively with AI agents.

Scope of Vision

• Lead a stage of the control plane roadmap and carry a platform domain through migration as ECP evolves into a self-service, declarative platform.
• Help define the future of ECP across the control plane, AI-native developer experience, and core platform domains.

Scale of Business Understanding and Impact

• Connect ECP’s technical priorities and decisions to Expeditors’ broader business and technology strategy, improving the platform experience for engineering teams through reliable, scalable, self-service capabilities.
• Reduce developer friction by building golden paths and agent-facing capabilities that other teams can adopt and use safely.

This position is on-site and will reside in the greater Seattle, WA. area at one of the following locations depending on availability. Candidates must be local or willing to relocate. Relocation assistance is not offered for this position.

• Downtown Seattle
• Federal Way
• Lynnwood
• Bellevue (Factoria)

Qualifications for Success

Required

• Senior-level software engineering experience, preferably 5+ years, building systems other engineers depend on in production.
• Depth in one or more object-oriented programming languages. Go preferred; Python, Java, or TypeScript also fit, with willingness to work across them.
• Kubernetes and infrastructure as code at depth. Azure preferred; AWS or GCP is acceptable if the concepts transfer.
• Clear technical writing, including design notes, ADRs, and runbooks others can follow.
• Experience building with AI coding agents daily with the ability to demonstrate an agent workflow, MCP server, skill, or automation and how its output is verified.

Preferred

• Control planes, Kubernetes operators, or reconciliation-based systems.
• API and resource model design that outlives its first consumer.
• GitOps with Argo CD, Kustomize, and Helm; CI/CD with GitHub Actions.
• Identity and secrets experience including OIDC, OAuth2, Entra ID, workload identity, and HashiCorp Vault.
• Agent safety, observability, policy as code, software supply chain security, schema design, and platform-as-a-product experience.
• Experience with Agentic AI development processes and practices.

Applicants are required to be eligible to lawfully work in the U.S. immediately; employer will not transfer or sponsor applicants for U.S. work authorization (such as an H-1B visa) for this opportunity.

Compensation and Benefits

Base Salary: $142,000 - $214,000

Benefits: Expeditors offers competitive benefits to all full-time employees including:

jobs.title: Store Manager
jobs.description:
What to expect when you work here

As a Store Manager (SM), you will be responsible for managing the store’s team members and the overall success of the store. You will partner with your Assistant Store Manager to hold your team accountable for meeting sales goals by ensuring that they provide friendly, enthusiastic customer service. You will be expected to maintain a strong sense of product knowledge, and to provide customers and team members with in-depth information on product features and benefits. You will also be responsible for managing all store operations, including opening and closing procedures, administering returns/store credit, managing schedules, performance metrics and standards, and dividing tasks amongst your team.

You can expect our 5 Core Values to drive everything we do.

Aim For The Podium:

• We provide an outstanding shopping experience and deliver exceptional customer service. The SM is an essential sales driver, coach, and communicator, providing training, leading by example, and communicating sales goals
• Ensure that merchandising is completed according to MAPP, and that the store aesthetic is clean, stocked, and organized
• Stay up-to-date with our brand and product knowledge, company information, sales and company-wide events, truly becoming a resource to your team and our customer base
• Hustle, improve, win, and don’t fear change. Take victory laps, and celebrate wins big and small
• Build and retain a winning team by partnering with Talent Acquisition and actively recruiting in-store and in your local community

Take Risks; Wear a Helmet:

• It never hurts to try something new. We are always looking to grow and progress and want to hear all your new ideas.
• Little wins can make a big difference - when you try something new, and it works, feed the idea up, so it can be shared. The best new ideas come from the teams in our stores!
• Don't be afraid to fail; no one is right all the time, but you can always be well-prepared.

Share The Road:

• We take the health, safety, and wellness of our employees seriously. Our Wellness program and safety committee offers workshops, classes, resources, etc. to all of our team members
• Our Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion council and employee resource groups promote open and honest communication, remove barriers, and champion policies to build a more equitable environment
• Do the right thing, and lead by example with a friendly and upbeat personality
• Set a tone of friendly competition, so that your team works together when selling, and everyone understands when to step back and when to step up and offer help

Keep It Real:

• You'll earn an hourly base rate, plus you'll have a chance to earn commission on a tiered system, based on meeting your sales goal, with additional incentives available, such as SPIFFS and monthly bonus potential
• Full Time benefits include Medical/Dental/Vision/Life/Accident, Paid Time Off, 401K, and a generous employee discount
• Because a whole lot of life happens between paychecks, Comoto also offers a voluntary benefit to all team members called DailyPay which allows for secure, instant transfers of earned pay before payday. This benefit is available to all team members immediately upon hire
• We strongly value training and development - with that, your first fiscal month of employment will be base pay only, so you may focus on learning
• Deliver honest feedback in a way that motivates your team members to push for their best

Fuel Your Passion:

• Work in an industry that you are passionate about!
• We are a growing company, and we promote from within - career opportunities!
• Represent Cycle Gear at special events, such as annual sales meetings, Bike Nights, local motorcycle venues and mechanic schools, etc.
• We have the best customers! Riders are passionate, friendly, charitable, community-minded people, and we get to interact with them every day!

Our next Store Manager has:

• Sales management, product sales, and/or customer service experience, ideally in a specialty retail environment
• Demonstrated the ability to lead a team that delivers results
• A proven track record of teaching, motivating and holding a team accountable
• Experience with computers (MS Excel) and POS systems (RetailPro)
• A self-starter mentality that consistently delivers an outstanding, personalized retail experience
• An open mind, and is eager to learn and be a part of the riding community
• Motorcycle riding, knowledge, or interest (strongly desired, but not a requirement)

jobs.description:
About the Role

As a Sales Advisor, you'll be responsible for providing excellent customer service, welcoming & guiding customers through your store to actively sell our products and providing customers with support & guidance. You'll use your fashion and product knowledge to provide our customers with all the relevant information they need for the best experience. You'll also work on garment refill & care, presentation and contribute to a clean and tidy sales floor and back of house, working closely with the rest of your store team to deliver an excellent customer experience.

A Day in the Life

Working at H&M means no two days are ever the same, but a typical day will include the following responsibilities*

Customer Sales & Profit

• Provide excellent customer service: welcoming & guiding customers through the store & OMNI experience where available, supporting them with direct customer service
• Willingness to engage and have conversations with customers to provide excellent service
• Guide customers through our fashion trends, stories & products in all areas of the store
• Ability to effectively promote and sell our products to customers
• Actively promote our Customer Loyalty App (Hello Member) & in-store sustainability initiatives
• Representing yourself and the H&M brand positively during all customer interactions
• Support with commercial or operational actions to reach sales targets with store management team

General Information

Fashion & Trend Awareness

• Keep up-to-date with fashion scene, trends, tendencies, styles, brands, products, competitors, and relevant influencers, etc.
• Use your product & fashion knowledge to share relevant information to customers

Team & Development

• Retain and share your service, fashion and store operations knowledge and skills with colleagues
• Follow all procedures, routines, and legal requirements in all areas of the store
• Give & receive feedback with your colleagues to learn, develop & support each other
• Participate in relevant available Onboarding, introduction processes & trainings and courses relevant for your role & future development

Retail Operations/ Visual & Commercial Execution

• Complete full garment cycle from unpacking and refill to steaming and ensure good garment care
• Operate fitting room and checkout areas according to best practice & processes
• Contribute to a clean and tidy sales floor and back of house (including stockrooms)
• Support with garment presentation, execution and maintain attractive merchandise displays, clear trends & stories according to visual & commercial guidelines
• Ensure good stock levels with replenishment routines on sales floor
• Upkeep & follow best practice for any in-store OMNI Services & in-store tech services/tools, etc (Instore Care App, Click & Collect, Smart Store etc)
• Support with opening and closing of the store
• Following all H&S guidelines and legal requirements applicable to role and responsibilities

Who You Are

• As a Sales Advisor, you'll be passionate about fashion and everything we create in-store.
• Motivated by giving customers a great experience.
• You should also be communicative, creative and curious, motivated, flexible, decisive, and action-oriented.
• You should also enjoy working in a collaborative and dynamic environment.
• You have sales experience working in a dynamic and collaborative environment that you can apply to your role
• Experience working with customer service in fashion, retail or other service-related industries

Why You'll Love Working at H&M

• We value diverse backgrounds, including but not limited to race, ethnicity, gender, age, religion, sexual orientation, and disability
• We pride ourselves on being a values-driven organization, guided by our 7 unique values that have been part of our success story for over 75 years
• You'll have access to our Colleague Resource Groups (CRGs) to find community and networking opportunities among colleagues
• We are an inclusive company where you're encouraged to be yourself at work
• You will have access to a large global talent community, where career growth and aspirations have no limits
• We believe in supporting your overall wellbeing and offer comprehensive benefits inclusive of health insurance, wellness and family support programs, company match retirement plan, paid leave programs, and paid time off, including a community day to serve your local community
• You'll be able to express your personal style with our employee discount at H&M, & Other Stories, and COS

Job Status: Hourly, Non-Exempt

EEOC Code: SLS

Compensation: Sales Associates Pay Rate $17.50 per hour**

*This job posting highlights the most critical responsibilities and requirements of the job and is not all-inclusive. There may be additional duties, and responsibilities assigned for this job at the company's discretion.

**H&M, in good faith, has assessed this posted range of compensation as the accurate range for this role and location at the time of this posting. H&M may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range depending on candidate qualifications. This range may be modified in the future.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations for applicants with disabilities. If you require assistance or accommodation during the application or interview process, please contact us at https://hm.ethicspoint.com, and use Ask a Question.

Benefits:

We offer all our employees at H&M Group attractive benefits with extensive development opportunities around the globe. All our employees receive a staff discount card, usable on all our H&M Group brands in stores and online. Brands covered by the discount are H&M (Beauty and Move included), COS, Weekday, Monki, H&M HOME, & Other Stories, ARKET, Afound. In addition to our staff discount, all our employees are included in our H&M Incentive Program – HIP. You can read more about our H&M Incentive Program here.

In addition to our global benefits, all our local markets offer different competitive perks and benefits. Please note that they may differ between employment type and countries.

Inclusion & Diversity:

H&M is a part of H&M Group. At H&M Group, we’re determined to create and maintain inclusive, diverse and equitable workplaces throughout our organization. Our teams should consist of a variety of people that share and combine their knowledge, experience and ideas. Having a diverse workforce leads to a positive impact on how we address challenges, on what we perceive possible and on how we choose to relate to our colleagues and customers all over the world. Hence, all diversity dimensions are considered in our recruitment process.

We strive to have a fair and equal process and therefore kindly ask you not to attach a cover letter in your application as they often contain information that easily can trigger unintentional biases.

Company Description:

H&M is a fashion brand that offers the latest styles and inspiration, from fashion pieces and unique designer collaborations to affordable wardrobe essentials. Our business idea is fashion & quality at the best price in a sustainable way. Learn more about H&M here.

H&M Fashion USA, Inc. – Maki Assessment Tool:

We use an online assessment tool called Maki for skills-based selection of applicants for sales advisor positions within some of our stores. Maki is not an automated decision-making tool. Rather, it is a tool that uses an AI-created avatar to present to you a set of multiple-choice questions. These questions are prepared by the H&M hiring team to assess candidates’ ability to perform the duties of the position for which they are applying. The assessment calculates your total score based on predefined point values provided by our H&M team. The hiring team will review your whole application, including your assessment score, to decide whether to advance each candidate to the next stage. Doing the assessment is optional. If you choose to complete the assessment, your score will be one factor that the hiring team considers.

If you have any difficulties or concerns with the online assessment method, you can request an alternative method of assessment by contacting recruitment_support@hm.com. Choosing an alternative method will not affect your chances of being considered for the position, nor does any assessment method provide an advantage or disadvantage in the selection process. You will have the opportunity to provide optional feedback immediately after the assessment and you may always ask questions.

When you take the assessment, we collect your responses and use this information to evaluate your suitability for the role to which you have applied. The answers are saved in your applicant profile. We do not sell the information captured in the questionnaire and do not use any personal information to train any AI models. Our applicant tracking system provider has access to this information but is contractually prohibited from using it for any other purpose.

During this process, we may collect information from you through cookies, with your consent. This may include details such as your electronic network activity information (IP address, timestamps, and device identifiers). This information is accessible to our hiring team but is otherwise kept confidential. For more information, please refer to our Cookie Notice.

We retain this information for 3 years in your applicant file and use it as set forth in our Applicant Privacy Notice. For more information on how your personal data is processed by us, please refer to our Applicant Privacy Notice.

The Phlebotomist reflects the mission, vision, and values of NM, adheres to the organization’s Code of Ethics and Corporate Compliance Program, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and all other regulatory and accreditation standards.

The Phlebotomist provides expert phlebotomy services and must demonstrate excellent customer service and communication skills. The phlebotomist must have the ability to function as part of a highly effective team that consistently puts “Patients First”.

The Phlebotomist is responsible for venipuncture collection and specimen processing. Other responsibilities include but are not limited to order entry in multiple systems, verification of test result receipt, patient information retrieval and lab reception/clerical duties and functions

Responsibilities:

· Performs phlebotomy and other lab specimen collections per age related standards and in accordance with departmental policies, protocols and procedures.

· Demonstrates AIDET model and optimizes patient safety to reduce the likelihood of medical/health care errors.

· Receives and reviews physician orders; ensures that all necessary information is included for appropriate lab services. Enters accurate orders for lab tests in accordance with department policies, protocols and procedures.

· Patient communication model and provides appropriate post-phlebotomy patient care.

· Processes specimens in a timely manner to ensure stability and integrity of samples including labeling, centrifuging, aliquoting, freezing and packaging specimens for transport in accordance with established protocols and policies.

· Reviews/Records refrigerator temperature(s) and QC/QA records. Areas of concern are recorded through the Corrective Action Log and reported to maintenance for repair. Findings are reported to supervisor or manager.

· Understands the operation and maintenance of equipment pertinent to the job. Follows up with all outstanding orders on manifest log, and communicates all timed, completed or uncompleted draws/charges/results as appropriate

· Communicates and notifies Laboratory and/or Physician of problems with specimen procurement for optimal care

· Maintains a safe work environment, holds self-accountable for safe work practices; including adhering to biohazard waste procedures and ensuring proper storage and timely pickup of biohazardous waste.

· Performs lab-related clerical duties include but not limited to order entry, verification of test result receipt, patient information retrieval as well as utilization of email, medical record systems, handheld and desktop devices, ordering and maintaining supply inventory, filing and sanitizing equipment as necessary

· Uses department’s resources efficiently; participates in efforts to reduce costs and streamline work processes.

· Adheres to continuing education expectations; completes and signs-off on competency assessments

· Demonstrates the value of teamwork on a consistent basis; interacts with and assists others in a professional manner

· Applies critical thinking, sound decision making and judgment to investigate and resolve challenging situations

· Complies with all organizational policies regarding ethical business practices.

· Performs other duties as assigned

Minimum Requirements:

Education:

• High School diploma or equivalent.

Certification:

• ·Phlebotomy certification through a nationally recognized organization or training from a phlebotomy school or medical institution or one or more years of phlebotomy experience in a healthcare setting or CMA certification.

Preferred:

· Experience performing phlebotomy on a broad range of patient’s types.

· Experience with processing lab specimens, transferring specimens, and handling a centrifuge.

jobs.title: Senior Product Designer
jobs.description:
The Senior Product Designer owns the end-to-end user experience of Acumatica applications, shapes workflows, and aligns them with the product vision. As an active member of the discovery team, they collaborate with the Product Manager, Business Analyst, Engineering Lead, and backend developers to translate business requirements into validated, scalable solutions. This role includes building working prototypes for Business Analysts to specify from and for backend developers to connect services to, modeling system behavior, writing clear behavioral specifications for engineers and AI agents, and ensuring AI-generated output meets quality and accessibility standards. The Senior Product Designer also mentors team members, leads cross-functional design sprints, and links design work to measurable business outcomes.

MAJOR ROLES & RESPONSIBILITIES

Discovery & Validation: Understanding Users and Problems

• Conduct and synthesize user research and competitive analysis, including emerging UX patterns and AI capabilities, to inform design direction

• Validate early concepts with users through working prototypes before committing to full design or engineering effort

• Lead usability and UX acceptance testing to ensure the experience functions as designed. Define success metrics such as task completion, error rate, CSAT, and adoption with product managers. Identify and raise UX defects before release.

Interactive Systems Design: Designing Behavior, Not Just Screens

• Own end-to-end UX for assigned epics, including AI-surfaced and headless experiences. Partner with the Engineering Lead to assess feasibility and trade-offs.

• Model user flows, screen and component states, and transitions, defining how the UI responds to user input, validation, system events, and API responses

• Design for non-deterministic AI output by defining fallback, recovery, and human-in-the-loop behavior when results are incomplete, incorrect, or low confidence

Prototype & Behavioral Specification: Building the Working Reference

• Build working code prototypes in the component library to serve as reference artifacts. These prototypes help Business Analysts write functional and business specifications and enable backend developers to connect real services.

• Structure prototypes to be plug-in ready, with defined mock data structures and clear data shapes. Keep the UI separate from data logic to prevent backend rework.

• Write behavioral specifications that AI coding agents can interpret clearly, covering interaction rules, states, edge cases, and UI acceptance criteria.

• Define UI-level guardrails for AI-surfaced features, such as how uncertainty is displayed, when human confirmation is required, and how users can override. Partner with the Product Manager and Business Analyst to establish the supporting business rules.

• Annotate prototypes with known business rules and open questions to surface rules that do not appear on screen, such as permissions, validation logic, and calculations, early in the process.

• Build reusable specification templates, prompt templates, and context files to ensure AI-generated output remains consistent with the design system.

Design Systems & Versioning: Keeping Design and Code in Sync

• Work directly in BitBucket repositories: create branches, commit changes, open and review pull requests, and resolve basic merge conflicts

• Store and edit design tokens in the code repository, keeping Figma variables and coded tokens aligned

• Treat the coded component library as the source of truth, moving beyond Figma-only handoff. Structure the system so AI agents can use it reliably.

AI-Assisted Workflows & Design QA: Building Fast, Shipping Right

• Use AI tools (e.g., Cursor, Claude Code, Figma Make) to build working prototypes in hours rather than days

• Coordinate AI agents for research synthesis, specification drafting, prototyping, and documentation, while maintaining responsibility for final design decisions.

• Audit AI-generated code and UI for design system compliance, interaction accuracy, and accessibility before it reaches engineering or users

• 5+ years of product design experience, with demonstrated impact on shipped products and business outcomes

• Portfolio showing end-to-end ownership of complex B2B or enterprise workflows, including state models, edge cases, and system behavior

• Demonstrate the ability to build working code prototypes with AI-assisted tools that Business Analysts can specify from and backend developers can connect services to, using defined mock data and UI separated from data logic.

• Demonstrate strong accessibility awareness by applying WCAG standards and understanding assistive technologies to ensure all users can engage with the product effectively.

• Demonstrate fluency in designing screen- and flow-level patterns for AI-surfaced and agentic experiences, including confidence indicators, override affordances, and human-in-the-loop controls, across both visual and headless interfaces.

• Apply AI-augmented design strategy by setting cross-feature principles for how AI appears in the product (trust, transparency, user control, and communicating uncertainty), partnering with Data and AI teams, and guiding how AI is used across the design workflow

• Connect design decisions to business goals, contributing to and constructively challenging product direction from a design perspective.

• Apply systems thinking by designing for scale and long-term impact and understanding how individual features integrate into the overall product ecosystem.

• Communicate design rationale confidently to team members, contribute actively to cross-functional meetings, and build strong relationships across functions.

• Demonstrate facilitation skills by leading workshops and cross-functional sessions, knowing when to guide, when to step back, and how to move a group from divergence to decision.

• Exhibit sound judgment and leadership when navigating ambiguity without clear precedent, taking ownership of outcomes rather than just outputs.

jobs.title: Senior Transportation Engineer
jobs.description:
AECOM is seeking a Senior Transportation Engineer to join our Surface Transportation team in Novi, Michigan. This position offers an opportunity to play a key role in the delivery and growth of transportation projects throughout Michigan, with a focus on roadway and highway design, client service, technical leadership, and business development.

The successful candidate will bring strong transportation engineering experience along with established relationships with the Michigan Department of Transportation (MDOT) and local transportation agencies, municipalities, counties, and other public-sector clients. This individual will serve as a trusted technical advisor to clients, help identify and pursue new opportunities, and strengthen AECOM’s position as a preferred transportation partner throughout the region.

In addition to leading and supporting roadway design projects, you will collaborate with project managers, technical staff, and business development leaders to develop client strategies, identify upcoming opportunities, support pursuits, and maintain long-term client relationships. This is an excellent opportunity for a transportation professional who enjoys combining technical engineering with client engagement, strategic growth, and team leadership.

Key Responsibilities

• Lead and perform transportation engineering and roadway design activities for urban and rural roadways, interstate highways, interchanges, and other transportation infrastructure projects.
• Develop transportation design solutions in accordance with MDOT, local agency, and applicable industry standards.
• Serve as a senior technical resource for roadway design, including horizontal and vertical alignments, roadway modeling, plans, specifications, estimates, design reports, and technical memorandums.
• Coordinate with clients, public agencies, municipalities, utilities, permitting agencies, and other project stakeholders to advance projects from planning through final design and construction.
• Establish and maintain strong working relationships with MDOT and local transportation agencies throughout Michigan, serving as a trusted advisor and technical point of contact on assigned projects.
• Participate in business development activities, including client meetings, relationship-building activities, opportunity identification, pursuit strategy, proposal development, interviews, and presentations.
• Support the development and execution of client account strategies designed to strengthen existing relationships and expand AECOM’s transportation portfolio throughout Michigan.
• Develop and maintain an understanding of client priorities, capital programs, procurement strategies, and upcoming transportation needs to position AECOM for future opportunities.
• Support project managers and business development leaders in developing capture strategies, scopes of work, fee estimates, and proposals for MDOT and municipal transportation clients.
• Provide technical leadership and mentorship to engineers and other transportation staff.
• Perform quality control reviews of roadway plans, calculations, specifications, reports, and other project deliverables.
• Develop construction cost estimates and provide input into project budgets, schedules, and technical approaches.
• Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams and subconsultants to deliver high-quality transportation projects.

Minimum Requirements

• BA/BS + 6 years of relevant experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education

Preferred Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering or related engineering discipline.
• 10+ years of transportation engineering experience with a strong background in roadway design and delivery of transportation infrastructure projects.

• Established relationships with MDOT and/or Michigan municipal, county, regional, or other transportation agency clients.

• Strong communication and presentation skills with the ability to interact effectively with public-sector clients, technical teams, and project stakeholders.

Resolve complications and complaints by conducting thorough research of the situation and the most effective solutions. jobs.description:

We are seeking an experienced Process Engineer to provide technical support for our manufacturing facilities. This role leads process improvements through engineering methods and data analysis, manages capital projects and equipment upgrades, and supports manufacturing operations. Responsibilities include coordinating work with vendors, contractors, and internal stakeholders and serving as the technical lead for process equipment and operations. The ideal candidate has strong technical skills, experience in heavy industrial or process environments, and proficiency in basic engineering design calculations. This position offers opportunities to expand your professional skills while seeing the real-world impact of your work.

Responsibilities

• Evaluate existing coil coating and metal processing lines to reduce downtime, minimize waste, and maximize productivity.

• Study and recommend methods to improve existing equipment and processes.

• Provide technical support for process lines by identifying improvement opportunities, troubleshooting equipment, and responding to operator inquiries.

• Help manage the company’s combustion systems by assisting maintenance managers with tuning and troubleshooting natural-gas-fired industrial burners, thermal oxidizers (recuperative and RTO), and combustion-air delivery systems to ensure safe gas firing and complete destruction of volatile organic compounds (VOCs).

• Diagnose the root causes of refractory degradation, hot spots, thermal cracking, and material failure.

• Use process historians, including Rockwell/OSIsoft PI and ibaAnalyzer, to capture real-time operating data, trace system anomalies, and support root cause analysis (RCA).

• Coordinate design and installation activities with other departments.

• Perform basic heat-transfer calculations and thermodynamic modeling to improve the energy efficiency of the company’s thermal systems, including water heating and cooling systems and fluid-based chemical process systems. Apply a working knowledge of combustion systems, curing ovens, thermal oxidizers, heat exchangers, and refractory and insulation linings.

• Complete engineering calculations to validate new equipment or process implementations.

• Requisition materials and equipment for capital projects.

• Plan, schedule, and supervise construction activities, and participate in the startup and evaluation of new equipment.

• Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering or related engineering degree.

• 5+ years experience in process or industrial environment.

• Process knowledge and strong troubleshooting skills.

• Excellent computer hardware and software applications knowledge

• Data driven decision making; Effective use of process automation tools.

Must be able to travel up to 30% and work within one of the plant facilities.

jobs.title: Associate Director, Program Management
jobs.description:
Natera’s mission is to transform the diagnosis and management of genetic disease by making personalized genetic testing and diagnostics standard of care. Natera’s focus is on reproductive health, cancer, and organ transplantation.

The Patient Experience (PX) team ensures we are providing the best care for our patients. We do so with a combination of state-of-the-art patient support technologies and a team of 800+ support staff, specialized in every step of the patient journey, including pre-test estimates, blood sample collection, and billing support.

A key pillar of the PX team’s success is continuously improving how we operate. We don’t accept the status quo. We are obsessed with identifying improvement opportunities and quickly delivering and iterating on solutions. This includes implementing business review mechanisms, developing insightful and actionable metrics, and leading large-scale initiatives.

About the role

As Associate Director, Program Management, you will lead high-impact, cross-functional programs across Patient Experience. Depending on business priorities, this could span areas such as phlebotomy scheduling and operations, billing support, and patient support technology. You will shape where programs go, not just how they get delivered. You’ll partner with VP-level leaders to define the problems worth solving, drive decisions with significant cost and patient experience stakes, and build the mechanisms that help the organization see what’s happening and act on it.

This is a senior individual contributor role. You will lead through expertise, influence, and judgment rather than direct reports.

What you’ll do

• Own a portfolio of strategic programs spanning multiple PX teams or business units, with a focus on improving patient experience, operational efficiency, and cost-to-serve.

• Define program scope and boundaries with limited guidance. Partner with business unit leaders to co-create strategy and set portfolio priorities.

• Lead through significant ambiguity. Help stakeholders define the problem before solving it, and bring a clear, defensible point of view to decisions.

• Build and evolve business review mechanisms and metrics. Turn data into a clear narrative of what is happening, what we are learning, and what we are doing about it.

• Anticipate risks across the portfolio before they surface. Arrive with mitigation options and make scope, time, and cost trade-off recommendations.

• Drive decisions that require cross-functional VP-level commitment. Present at steering committees and SVP-level forums, and manage a broad stakeholder map, including skeptics.

• Rigorously pressure-test analyses, vendor claims, and technology choices, especially on high-stakes, hard-to-reverse decisions.

• Own strategic governance of vendor and partner relationships within your portfolio, using performance data to inform investment and resource recommendations.

• Scale your impact by designing repeatable delivery models and using AI tools and mechanisms, not personal effort.

Basic qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience

• PMP or equivalent program management certification

• Proven track record of driving decisions with VP- and SVP-level stakeholders and presenting to senior leadership

• Demonstrated ability to independently frame and solve ambiguous, novel problems, using first-principles thinking

• Track record of delivering measurable business outcomes, such as cost reduction, revenue enablement, or cycle time improvement

• Experience building business review mechanisms and metrics that drive decisions

• Strong analytical skills, with the judgment to validate data and methodology, not just report it

• Excellent written and oral communication skills, including turning complex data into clear narratives for executive audiences

• Experience working with global teams across multiple time zones

• 7+ years of program management experience, including ownership of cross-functional portfolios spanning multiple teams or business units

Preferred qualifications

• Advanced degree (MBA or similar)

• Experience in healthcare, diagnostics, or patient-facing operations

• Experience with contact centers, field or mobile healthcare services, or other large-scale service operations

• Experience governing BPO or outsourced service partners

• Experience leading AI, automation, or technology-enabled operational change

• Familiarity with healthcare billing and reimbursement

The pay range is listed and actual compensation packages are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, years & depth of experience, certifications and specific office location. This may differ in other locations due to cost of labor considerations.

Remote USA

$148,400—$185,500 USD

OUR OPPORTUNITY

Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives.

The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. When you join Natera, you’ll work hard and grow quickly. Working alongside the elite of the industry, you’ll be stretched and challenged, and take pride in being part of a company that is changing the landscape of genetic disease management.

WHAT WE OFFER

Competitive Benefits - Employee benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life and disability plans for eligible employees and their dependents. Additionally, Natera employees and their immediate families receive free testing in addition to fertility care benefits. Other benefits include pregnancy and baby bonding leave, 401k benefits, commuter benefits and much more. We also offer a generous employee referral program!

Essential Functions

Description

• Plans and leads the briefing of innovative, opinion-leading, commercial and brand-enhancing global product lines designed for global and regional fans that deliver revenue, MSRP, margin, profitability, productivity, color/material guidance, construction, lifecycle targets, channel segmentation plans and other metrics as required. Provides input on seasonal global and regional analysis to inform the global briefing process. Synthesizes findings and inputs including but not limited to: product performance, assortmentperformance by channel/tier/key account/DTC, competitor analysis, trend reports, fan insights, market research data, retail visits, brand strength, trade publications and analysts, the executive team, and regional and global business units.

• Works cross-functionally throughout the seasonal product process with the Lifestyle and Performance business units to bring a cohesive, cross- merchandised, fan-focused line with compelling stories each season delivered on-time and completely.

• Executes against long-term and in-season strategic initiatives via the global product line plan and seasonal briefing as determined by senior management and merchandising analytics. Supports continuous improvement on style/sku efficiency, margins, regional alignment and other key metrics as required.

• Supports regional fan and channel needs with specific inline and regionally driven styles as required by the business (SMU’s, limited editions, collaborations, exclusive product).

Most employment attorneys have spent their careers on one side of the table or the other.

Some have represented employers navigating difficult workplace disputes. Others have advocated directly for employees whose careers, reputations, and livelihoods were suddenly at risk.

Regardless of where you've practiced, chances are you've encountered a case that stayed with you long after it ended:

• The workers endured harassment because they feared retaliation.

Success here requires more than legal knowledge. It requires judgment, empathy, strategic thinking and the ability to connect with clients whose lives may have been turned upside down and the skill to effectively advocate on their behalf.

Our attorneys handle sophisticated matters, work alongside accomplished colleagues, and advocate for individuals facing some of the most consequential moments of their professional lives. The attorneys who thrive on our team are intellectually curious, highly motivated, collaborative, and deeply committed to achieving exceptional outcomes for their clients.

At Morgan & Morgan, we are interested in speaking with employment attorneys from a broad range of backgrounds and at every stage of their careers. jobs.title: Contract Associate Director, Media Buying
jobs.description:
What to know

Lead and execute game-changing advertising strategies that help mission-driven organizations grow. As a contract Associate Director, you'll manage digital advertising campaigns across clients ranging from leading nonprofits to political and advocacy groups to major brands (and everything in between).

This may be the right role for you if you’re equally strategic, creative, and analytical. You can switch seamlessly from delivering an insightful analysis of campaign performance to launching new creative to proposing platform pivots. You’re used to spending most of your day speaking in acronyms — terms like DSP, CPA, IVT, ROAS, and AVOC are major parts of your vocabulary — and you know how to explain them to clients and teammates.

You will use your depth of paid media experience to inform your work but also tap into your digital curiosity and passion for innovation to bring new ideas and thinking to the team.

The company

Blue State is a purpose-driven agency. We partner with leading causes, brands, and campaigns and create real change. From AARP and Doctors Without Borders to Amnesty International and Oxfam, we transform how brands and causes raise money, influence policy, build platforms, and grow communities of supporters. Led by the most creative and analytical minds from the political, nonprofit, and brand worlds, Blue State is an independent agency in the US and London.

A day in the life

• Build, manage, monitor, and optimize media campaigns across multiple platforms, primarily using Meta Business Manager, Google and Bing Ads, Google Campaign Manager 360, and the Yahoo DSP. (Other digital channel expertise is a plus.)

• Translate clients’ strategic visions into media objectives and KPIs to accomplish a wide range of client objectives including direct response (lead gen and fundraising), awareness, persuasion, and advocacy.

• Have a strong POV on measurement, attribution, and conversion tracking, and apply that knowledge to recommendations and ongoing campaign management, including planning around targeting and other strategies that align with client KPIs.

• Oversee other media buyers and work with media planners, strategists, and analysts, as well as external vendors, to develop audience recommendations and execute media campaigns.

• Work collaboratively with other internal or external teams, including account directors, creative directors, designers, and copywriters, to produce campaigns, creative ideas, and experimental designs.

• Analyze ongoing and historical performance data to generate reports, insights, and opportunities for optimization.

• Lead client-facing interactions — you’ll be the subject-matter expert for the platforms you manage.

• Serve as a subject-matter expert in the field by keeping up with industry trends, researching media publishers and ad tech partners, and developing vendor relationships.

The team

As part of the Paid Media team, you’ll work closely with a cross-disciplinary group of Blue State employees who are passionate, geeky, and care about their clients and causes. Blue State fosters an environment where everyone has an opportunity to shape new approaches, grow and learn from their colleagues, and take advantage of a personal development fund to stretch their skills even further. You’ll have the opportunity to work with some of the most inspiring charities, ambitious brands, and passionate advocacy and social change campaigns.

Some things we’re looking for

• 6+ years' experience in a hands-on paid media buying role using a mix of digital channels (Social, Search, Display, Video, Native, OOH, etc.) — with preference for experience in executing, managing, and reporting on media campaigns with a mix of objectives/goals.

• A passion for progressive causes.

• Demonstrated experience meeting or exceeding campaign objectives and specific KPIs.

• Ability to effectively manage multiple clients and projects on time, within budget, and meet performance goals.

• High proficiency with digital advertising platforms — you want to continually deepen your expertise in paid social, paid search, and/or programmatic trading — as well as Google Analytics and other measurement platforms.

• Exceptional attention to detail, especially regarding campaign setup and trafficking, QA, and reporting.

• Clear communicator with internal teams, vendors, and clients.

• Ability to adapt to new situations, solve problems on the fly, and communicate with those around you. Teamwork and scrappiness required.

• A shared passion and curiosity for delivering change. This includes comfort with ambiguity, a restlessness that resists the status quo, and a commitment to quality that ensures progress.

• A testing evangelist — no result is ever a problem as long as we can learn and improve in the future.

• Humble in victory, constructive in defeat. We champion and expect empathy, communication, collaboration, and respect.

The salary range for this position is $65-$85 per hour; compensation will be commensurate with experience.

At Blue State, diversity is a necessity, not a nice-to-have. We encourage those from underrepresented communities — women, people of color, LGBTQIA+, immigrants, those with disabilities and people at all the intersections in between — to apply. Even if you don’t think your current skill set checks every box below, but this role seems to align with your strengths, we want to hear from you.

Blue State is committed to creating an inclusive and accessible application and interview process. If you would like to request a reasonable accommodation for a disability, including the use of AI tools throughout the hiring process, please contact us at recruiting@bluestate.co with the subject line: Accommodation Request to get started.

Summary:

The Sales and Operations Development Program offers a 12-month Accelerated Commercial Experience (ACE) that provides associates with a fast-tracked opportunity, early in their career, to gain broad exposure within the Electrical Distribution industry. This rotational program provides hands-on exposure to the people, products, customers, and operations that power Rexel’s business. Through meaningful assignments, cross-functional projects, structured training, and mentorship, ACE Trainees develop the commercial, operational, and leadership skills needed to make an impact from day one. Participants gain broad experience across the business while exploring career paths aligned with their strengths and interests. Upon successful completion of the program, ACE Trainees may pursue opportunities in sales, operations, project management, procurement, marketing, future leadership, and other key areas of the organization.

You will work alongside experienced Rexel leaders and team members, contribute to real business priorities, and develop relationships across functions

Rotations Include:

• Warehouse & Logistics: Learn the full-cycle supply chain processes behind storing and moving materials, including order fulfillment, receiving, stocking, staging, and shipping
• Sales: Gain experience in counter, inside, and outside sales. Build customer service, product knowledge, selling, and digital tool skills
• Operations: Understand the business drivers that influence safety, profitability, facility maintenance, inventory, working capital, and customer service. Use available data and tools to support sound business decisions
• Project Management: Manage customer, sales, and vendor relationships; place orders; track shipments; coordinate billing; and maintain clear, timely communication throughout the project. Learn to review bid packages and prepare project quotations

Elective Rotations:

Toward the end of the program, ACE Trainees can tailor their experience through elective rotations based on individual interests, career goals, and local business opportunities. Elective opportunities may include:

• Returning to a previous rotation for deeper experience.
• Product Specialist rotations in areas such as Automation, Lighting, Gear, Datacom, or Services.
• A customized rotation developed with local leadership

• 4 Year / Bachelor's Degree - Preferred
• Bachelor’s degree in Industrial Distribution, Supply Chain, Business, or related degree preferred

At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise. To usher in this new era, we seek AI-native thinkers across every function who are energized by the opportunity to reinvent how they work. You don’t just use tools; you possess an innate curiosity, treating AI as a high-trust collaborator that is core to how you solve problems and accelerate your impact. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done.

The Elastic Global Services (EGS) team builds the highly available, scalable, multi-tenant Cloud Services platform that underpins Snowflake services. Our work includes autoscaling cloud virtual machines, managing compute-cluster topologies and lifecycles, and orchestrating workloads.

Our infrastructure runs on Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud. We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to lead complex distributed systems projects and improve the reliability, performance, and efficiency of our platform as customer demand grows.

Learn more in our ACM Symposium on Cloud Computing talk https://acmsocc.org/2022/assets/slides/99.pdf.




AS A SENIOR SOFTWARE ENGINEER, YOU WILL

 - Design and implement scalable, fault-tolerant distributed systems for our Cloud Services platform.

 - Independently deliver projects from design through production rollout, collaborating with partner teams as needed.

 - Develop expertise in an EGS component and resolve reliability and performance issues.

 - Make informed trade-offs among availability, consistency, performance, and infrastructure cost.

 - Ensure operational readiness and meet customer commitments for availability and performance.

 - Contribute thoughtful design and code reviews, and mentor junior engineers.




OUR IDEAL SENIOR SOFTWARE ENGINEER WILL HAVE

 - 5+ years  experience designing, building, and supporting large-scale distributed fault tolerant infrastructure in production.

 - Experience independently designing and delivering distributed systems projects in production.

 - Strong coding and debugging skills, with a track record of delivering maintainable, well-tested software.

 - Excellent understanding of operating systems concepts, including multithreading, memory management, networking, storage, and performance.

 - Clear technical communication, sound engineering judgment, and a collaborative approach to problem-solving.

 - BS / MS in Computer Science or related fields.

 - Clear technical communication and effective collaboration within and across teams.


WHY JOIN EGS AT SNOWFLAKE?

Build core infrastructure for an industry-leading cloud data platform. Solve challenging problems in distributed systems and resource management alongside experienced engineers, with direct ownership and impact on customer reliability and performance.

Snowflake is growing fast, and we’re scaling our team to help enable and accelerate our growth. We are looking for people who share our values, challenge ordinary thinking, and push the pace of innovation while building a future for themselves and Snowflake.

How do you want to make your impact?

At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.

Your Impact:

As an Axon Justice Account Executive, you will own and drive the strategic growth of large, high-impact state and local judicial customers across a defined territory. This is a quota-carrying, external field role with broad autonomy and responsibility for developing and executing territory strategy aligned to Axon’s broader business objectives.

You will lead complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles, navigate judicial procurement processes, and build trusted executive-level relationships across customer branches.
