jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer
jobs.description:
About Chamber

Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of death in America. At Chamber, we’re rebuilding the system for cardiology, creating a world where outcomes, not volume, define success. We partner with independent cardiologists to help them lead population health efforts in their communities, equipping them with technology, data, and operational tools that turn complex insights into better care for patients.

Our model blends clinical expertise, thoughtful design, and a modern operating platform that supports physicians, patients, and payers alike. We believe innovation and empathy go hand in hand, and by combining cutting-edge AI tools with a relentless focus on human care, we can transform heart health at scale.

Role Overview

The Staff Software Engineer will play a central role in designing and building Chamber’s core application platform. This is a hands-on role for someone who thrives in a startup environment, enjoys solving complex product and data challenges, and is excited to build systems that make a difference in healthcare.

This role will help design and build the applications that power Chamber’s operational tools for care teams & healthcare providers, along with our patient-facing mobile app. These applications support real-time cardiology insights and value-based care workflows, combining clinical data, analytics, and AI-assisted features.

The role will work across web and mobile — from modern web interfaces and API integrations to a React Native app —partnering closely with product, data, and infrastructure engineers to deliver reliable, high-impact software. This role will have a meaningful influence on application architecture, engineering practices, and the evolution of Chamber’s product platform.

Key Responsibilities

 - Design and build Chamber’s core applications. Develop and evolve the full-stack systems that power Chamber’s operational tools for care teams, providers, and patients. Build scalable application components that support complex healthcare workflows and large volumes of clinical and operational FHIR-based data.

 - Build modern, high-quality web interfaces. Design and implement intuitive user experiences using React, Next.js, and Tailwind. Translate complex workflows and analytics into usable and reliable tools for clinicians and care operations teams.

 - Develop backend services and application logic. Build and maintain Node.js and AWS lambda services that power application workflows, APIs, and integrations. Implement business logic and application services that interact with Chamber’s healthcare data systems, including FHIR-based platforms.

 - Build and ship the mobile app. Develop patient-facing features in React Native and TypeScript. Deliver a reliable, accessible experience on iOS and Android.

 - Integrate data and AI-powered capabilities. Collaborate with others to integrate analytics and AI-powered features into the application layer. Apply LLM-powered functionality where it meaningfully improves workflows and insights for care teams and patients.

 - Collaborate across engineering disciplines. Work closely with fellow engineers to deliver reliable and scalable systems. Contribute to architectural decisions, engineering standards, and shared development practices.

Requirements

 - 7+ years of experience in software engineering with significant full-stack development experience

 - Experience working with healthcare data platforms or healthcare technology systems

 - Proven experience designing and building production web and mobile applications

 - Strong experience with React, Next.js, and TypeScript

 - Experience building and shipping production mobile apps with React Native.

 - Experience building backend services using Node.js or similar platforms

 - Experience designing APIs and implementing application business logic

 - Experience working with cloud-based systems (AWS preferred)

 - Experience building applications that interact with external APIs or data platforms

 - Strong communication and collaboration skills

 - Comfortable with ambiguity and working in a fast-paced startup environment

Chamber Values

Our values guide how we lead, collaborate, and care:

jobs.title: 2027 Industrial Equipment Maintenance Intern
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril’s Manufacturing Maintenance team ensures maximum equipment uptime, builds world-class preventive and predictive maintenance programs, and supports the commissioning and ramp of new production lines. As we stand up and expand facilities (including Arsenal-1), the team is responsible for the reliability of manufacturing equipment that enables rapid, software-defined production of autonomous systems.

ABOUT THE JOB

The Industrial Equipment Maintenance Intern will support the reliable operation of production equipment used to build Anduril’s autonomous systems. This is a hands-on role working alongside experienced maintenance specialists, technicians, and engineers. You will gain practical experience with industrial equipment, preventive maintenance systems, troubleshooting, and the unique challenges of high-rate manufacturing for defense applications.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Assist maintenance specialists with preventive and corrective maintenance on manufacturing equipment (assembly systems, automation/robotics, torque tools, machining/fabrication equipment, conveyors, material handling systems, and facility support equipment).

• Support equipment inspections, basic troubleshooting, and recovery of production equipment to minimize downtime.

• Help execute and document work orders in the CMMS; update equipment histories and contribute to PM schedule accuracy.

• Participate in equipment commissioning, startup, and maintainability reviews for new or expanding production lines.

• Support spare parts identification, basic inventory tasks, and vendor coordination under supervision.

• Observe and contribute to reliability activities, including basic root-cause analysis and continuous improvement ideas.

• Read and interpret mechanical drawings, electrical schematics, and equipment manuals with guidance.

• Maintain a clean, organized work area and strictly follow all safety, quality, and environmental procedures.

• Collaborate with production, manufacturing engineering, and quality teams on equipment-related issues.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Must be pursuing a bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Industrial/Mechanical Engineering Technology, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Maintenance, Mechatronics, or a related field.

• Must be returning to school at the end of the internship to continue academic studies for at least one quarter or semester.

• Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export-controlled information or facilities; U.S. clearance eligibility may be required depending on program.

• Ability to complete an in-person 12-week internship in one of our offices in summer 2027.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Strong mechanical aptitude and genuine interest in hands-on equipment work and manufacturing reliability.

• Ability to follow procedures, communicate clearly (verbal and written), and work effectively in a team environment.

• Willing to work a standard manufacturing schedule (typically on-site, full-time during the internship term); occasional overtime or shift flexibility may be needed.

• Prior coursework, projects, or experience with industrial equipment, automation, robotics, PLCs, hydraulics, pneumatics, or manufacturing processes.

• Familiarity with CMMS systems, Lean/Six Sigma concepts, or basic reliability practices.

• Hands-on experience with tools, mechanical assembly, or electromechanical systems.

• Interest in defense technology, autonomous systems, or advanced manufacturing.

• Ability to stand, walk, climb, bend, and work in a manufacturing environment for extended periods.

• Lift and carry up to 40–50 lbs; work around automation, noise, and industrial equipment while wearing required PPE (safety glasses, hearing protection, steel-toe shoes, etc.).

• Comfortable working in typical plant conditions (varying temperatures, dust, etc.).

WHAT YOU’LL GAIN

• Direct exposure to hyperscale manufacturing of advanced autonomous defense systems at facilities such as Arsenal-1.

• Hands-on experience with modern industrial equipment, automation, and reliability practices in a fast-moving environment.

• Mentorship from maintenance leaders building programs from the ground up.

• Opportunity to contribute meaningfully to equipment uptime and production scale-up.

• Competitive pay, networking across engineering and operations teams, and potential pathways into full-time roles.

US Hourly Range

$28—$40 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

• No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

• Please always verify communications: Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address. Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

• Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

• What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.

By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

jobs.title: Product Engineering Lead
jobs.description:
JOIN THE TEAM BRINGING AUTONOMY TO THE BUILT WORLD


At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs.

In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic

In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Autonomy in the real world is never fully hands-off. Our machines work alongside expert operators who support them from anywhere, and the tools those operators use are a core part of the product. As a tech lead you'll be the bridge between the people supporting our fleet and the engineers building it. You'll architect, build, and own the software that connects people to our machines when it matters most.



You'll spend real time with the people using these tools, in the operations center and on job sites, and partner with our product team to shape the vision and requirements. From there, you'll own the technical design and implementation, leading the build with frontend, backend, and autonomy engineers, and scale it as the fleet grows. This is where great product engineering meets steel-toed boots.



Also, you get to drive 100,000 lb excavators.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Serve as technical lead for Remote Assistance, setting architecture, roadmap, and engineering standards for the product area

 - Spend regular time with operators, in the operations center and on job sites, to understand their workflows and where the tools slow them down

 - Turn user feedback into fast, measurable iteration, from UI and interaction design through to the services and data behind it

 - Build and ship across the stack: real-time, operator-facing applications and the backend services, APIs, and data pipelines that power them

 - Partner closely with autonomy, backend, and infrastructure engineers to define how people and machines work together, and what the system needs from each

 - Design for reliability, low latency, and clarity under pressure, in tools where getting it right matters

 - Scale the program as the fleet grows: improve operator efficiency, build the metrics that show it, and help hire and grow the team around you




WHAT YOU BRING

 - 8+ years building and shipping production software, including technical leadership of a product area or team

 - A track record of building products by working directly with their users: you've sat next to them, watched them work, and changed the product because of it

 - Strong engineering fundamentals and comfort across the stack; you can build a polished, responsive UI and reason clearly about the services, data models, and APIs underneath it

 - Experience with real-time or mission-critical systems where latency, reliability, and clear information under pressure matter

 - Ability to set technical direction, write it down, and bring frontend, backend, and adjacent teams along with it

 - Comfort with ambiguity and building 0-to-1, plus the judgment to know when to harden and scale what works




NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience building operator, dispatcher, or human-in-the-loop tools for robotics, autonomous vehicles, drones, or other physical systems

 - Background with live video, sensor, or 3D/geospatial data visualization in the browser

 - Experience with streaming and low-latency networking (e.g. WebRTC, WebSockets, gRPC)

 - Work on internal tools or operations platforms used by a dedicated team under real time pressure

 - Experience with TypeScript/React, Go or Python, and AWS



If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.

jobs.title: Senior Thermofluids Analyst II
jobs.description:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

NEUTRON

Neutron is a medium lift launch vehicle capable of delivering the mega constellations of tomorrow, high assurance payloads, and human spaceflight. As a highly reusable launch platform, Neutron will deliver a highly cost-effective and reliable launch solution leveraging Rocket Lab’s proven execution history with the Electron program. If you’re interested in joining a high performing team, pushing the boundaries with a clean sheet development of re-usable liquid launch vehicle, this is your opportunity!

SENIOR THERMOFLUIDS ANALYST II

Based out of Rocket Lab's our headquarters in Long Beach, CA the Senior Thermo-fluids Analyst will be directly contributing to the design and qualification of the Archimedes engine. You will be responsible for thermo-fluids modeling and analysis of components and engine systems, partnering with designers to ensure the engine and its subsystems achieve exceptional performance and meet requirements. In this role, you will utilize your understanding of fluid dynamics and thermodynamics to conduct CFD and thermo-fluid simulations, analyze modeling and testing results, and advise on technical matters related to your experience in thermo-fluids modeling and analysis. You will support the Neutron and Archimedes teams, with deliverables required for internal leadership, board of directors, and investors.

WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO:

• Use commercial tools and develop specialized tools to solve difficult thermo-fluid analysis problems in Propulsion hardware

• Work with designers, development engineers, and the manufacturing group to define and analyze hardware designs that meet heat transfer and fluid dynamics requirements while being manufacturable and reliable.

• Create system, subassemblies, and individual parts analytical models.

• Perform steady state and transient thermo-fluids and conjugate heat transfer analysis of heat exchange systems to predict fluid and structural temperatures, as well as heat and flow rates.

• Develop standard practices for thermo-fluids analysis and common hand calculations to expedite hardware development.

• Generate and maintain clear documentation of all performed analyses, including inputs, methods, and results to ensure proper communication during hardware reviews and qualification.

• Support stage, engine and sub-system testing through data review and provide recommendations based on data and analysis.

• Provide continued direction to the engineering team on highest value analysis and results deliverable schedule as the program evolves.

YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS AS A SENIOR THERMOFLUIDS ANALYST II:

• Bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline or equivalent

• 8+ years of performing thermal and mass transfer analyses for aerospace hardware.

• A good foundation on heat transfer, thermodynamics, and fluid mechanics analysis best practices.

• Fundamental understanding of fluids design principles.

• Familiarity with one or both of following tools: STAR-CCM+, ANSYS CFX or equivalent.

• Prior experience in thermal/fluid hardware instrumentation and testing.

THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE:

• Graduate degree

• Professional experience with NX, and ANSYS mechanical.

• Experience with best practices for design, qualification and production

• Experience with a scrappy development environment

• Experience with supporting failure investigations.

• Proficient with the following tools: Thermal Desktop, GFSSP, and/or SINDA/FLUENT.

• Prior experience analyzing rocket engine combustion devices and turbo pump components.

• Fundamental understanding of mechanical design principles.

• Familiar with performing CFD analysis on parallel computing systems.

• Familiarity with one or more of the following topic areas: CHT, FSI, Multiphase, or Reacting Flow.

• Familiarity with liquid engine qualification and certification using NASA-STDs 5012.

This position may require prolonged periods of sitting, standing, walking, computer work, and occasional exposure to moderate levels of noise, dust, and fumes in production areas

Anticipated annual equity grant value is designed around function, level, experience, and other factors; realized value depends on vesting and stock-price performance.

Join one of the world's fastest-growing space companies and own a piece of it. In addition to competitive base pay, you'll receive company stock as part of your total compensation package, giving you a direct stake in our success. As we expand to new launch sites, groundbreaking missions, and global markets, your ownership has the opportunity to grow alongside the company.

jobs.title: Senior Thermofluids Analyst I
jobs.description:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

NEUTRON

Neutron is a medium lift launch vehicle capable of delivering the mega constellations of tomorrow, high assurance payloads, and human spaceflight. As a highly reusable launch platform, Neutron will deliver a highly cost-effective and reliable launch solution leveraging Rocket Lab’s proven execution history with the Electron program. If you’re interested in joining a high performing team, pushing the boundaries with a clean sheet development of re-usable liquid launch vehicle, this is your opportunity!

SENIOR THERMOFLUIDS ANALYST I

Based out of Rocket Lab's our headquarters in Long Beach, CA the Senior Thermo-fluids Analyst will be directly contributing to the design and qualification of the Archimedes engine. You will be responsible for thermo-fluids modeling and analysis of components and engine systems, partnering with designers to ensure the engine and its subsystems achieve exceptional performance and meet requirements. In this role, you will utilize your understanding of fluid dynamics and thermodynamics to conduct CFD and thermo-fluid simulations, analyze modeling and testing results, and advise on technical matters related to your experience in thermo-fluids modeling and analysis. You will support the Neutron and Archimedes teams, with deliverables required for internal leadership, board of directors, and investors.

WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO:

• Use commercial tools and develop specialized tools to solve difficult thermo-fluid analysis problems in Propulsion hardware

• Work with designers, development engineers, and the manufacturing group to define and analyze hardware designs that meet heat transfer and fluid dynamics requirements while being manufacturable and reliable.

• Create system, subassemblies, and individual parts analytical models.

• Perform steady state and transient thermo-fluids and conjugate heat transfer analysis of heat exchange systems to predict fluid and structural temperatures, as well as heat and flow rates.

• Develop standard practices for thermo-fluids analysis and common hand calculations to expedite hardware development.

• Generate and maintain clear documentation of all performed analyses, including inputs, methods, and results to ensure proper communication during hardware reviews and qualification.

• Support stage, engine and sub-system testing through data review and provide recommendations based on data and analysis.

• Provide continued direction to the engineering team on highest value analysis and results deliverable schedule as the program evolves.

YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS AS A SENIOR THERMOFLUIDS ANALYST I:

• Bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline or equivalent

• 5+ years of performing thermal and mass transfer analyses for aerospace hardware.

• A good foundation on heat transfer, thermodynamics, and fluid mechanics analysis best practices.

• Fundamental understanding of fluids design principles.

• Familiarity with one or both of following tools: STAR-CCM+, ANSYS CFX or equivalent.

• Prior experience in thermal/fluid hardware instrumentation and testing.

THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE:

• Graduate degree

• Professional experience with NX, and ANSYS mechanical.

• Experience with best practices for design, qualification and production

• Experience with a scrappy development environment

• Experience with supporting failure investigations.

• Proficient with the following tools: Thermal Desktop, GFSSP, and/or SINDA/FLUENT.

• Prior experience analyzing rocket engine combustion devices and turbo pump components.

• Fundamental understanding of mechanical design principles.

• Familiar with performing CFD analysis on parallel computing systems.

• Familiarity with one or more of the following topic areas: CHT, FSI, Multiphase, or Reacting Flow.

• Familiarity with liquid engine qualification and certification using NASA-STDs 5012.

This position may require prolonged periods of sitting, standing, walking, computer work, and occasional exposure to moderate levels of noise, dust, and fumes in production areas

jobs.title: Sr. Director, Corporate Legal Counsel
jobs.description:
About GenScript

Founded in 2002 in New Jersey, GenScript Biotech Corporation accelerates innovation in biotech and healthcare by providing researchers and companies with the building blocks needed to develop groundbreaking treatments and products. Guided by its mission to Make People and Nature Healthier Through Biotechnology, and its role as a well-recognized biotechnology company, GenScript has a team of approximately 6,165 employees and has served more than 200,000 customers across over 100 countries and regions.

Position Summary

The Senior Director of Legal will serve as a senior member of Legal Team I within the GenScript Legal Department. Legal Team I is responsible for legal, regulatory, and compliance matters across the Americas, including the U.S. and Canada, Europe, and the UK, and serves as a strategic legal partner to executive leadership, commercial teams, and R&D functions.

Under the direction of the Team Leader, this role will provide senior-level legal leadership and strategic counsel on complex commercial, regulatory, compliance, governance, transactional, and dispute-related matters. The role will also collaborate closely with legal colleagues in China, Asia Pacific, and ProBio, the CDMO subsidiary of GenScript Biotech, to support cross-border business initiatives and manage legal risk across jurisdictions.

Please note that this role is based in New Jersey and will require regular onsite time at our US headquarters in Piscataway, NJ. The estimated compensation is $300,000 base and can be flexible based on experience level.

Core Responsibilities

Strategic Legal Leadership

• Serve as a senior legal advisor for matters across the Americas, Europe, and the UK, providing practical, risk-based legal guidance to business and functional leaders.

• Partner with executive leadership, commercial teams, R&D functions, business development, manufacturing, compliance, finance, HR, regulatory, and operations teams on strategic legal matters.

• Provide senior-level legal input on business strategy, transaction structuring, risk tolerance, governance, regulatory considerations, and operational execution.

• Anticipate and assess legal, regulatory, and compliance risks affecting life sciences, biotech, pharmaceutical, CDMO, research, manufacturing, and commercialization activities.

• Lead legal workstreams for high-impact business initiatives and ensure legal support is aligned with business priorities and global legal department standards.

Commercial, Transactional & Corporate Support

• Lead the drafting, review, negotiation, and management of complex commercial and strategic agreements.

• Support corporate development and strategic business initiatives, including financing transactions, capital markets matters, strategic investments, mergers and acquisitions, and post-transaction integration matters.

• Advise business stakeholders on transaction strategy, deal structure, negotiation approach, contractual risk allocation, approval requirements, and post-execution obligations.

• Drive consistency in contracting standards, negotiation positions, governance processes, and risk mitigation practices across regions.

Regulatory, Compliance & Risk Management

• Provide strategic legal guidance on regulatory and compliance matters across the Americas, Europe, and the UK, including export control, anti-bribery and anti-corruption, FCPA, data security, privacy-related considerations, HR and immigration legal issues, and tax-related transaction matters.

• Advise on legal and compliance risks related to product development, clinical or research activities, manufacturing, commercialization, supply chain, product launch readiness, and international operations.

• Support legal matters involving life sciences regulatory frameworks, FDA-related considerations, EU and UK regulatory issues, and cross-border compliance requirements.

• Provide guidance on Hong Kong Stock Exchange-related compliance, disclosure, governance, or regulatory matters, as applicable.

• Partner with cross-functional teams to design and implement practical legal risk mitigation strategies that support business objectives while protecting the organization.

Governance, Disputes & Outside Counsel Management

• Support corporate governance matters, including entity governance, internal approvals, board or committee materials, delegations of authority, and regulatory authority interactions.

• Lead or oversee litigation, disputes, internal investigations, enforcement-related matters, and pre-dispute risk assessments.

• Manage outside counsel in litigation, investigation, regulatory, transactional, and specialty advisory matters across multiple jurisdictions.

• Direct information gathering, internal investigation processes, document collection, matter strategy, settlement evaluation, and regulatory response activities.

• Advise senior management on material legal exposures, recommended courses of action, escalation requirements, and business implications.

• Direct improvement of current legal processes, templates, playbooks, escalation protocols, and governance practices to increase consistency, efficiency, and risk visibility.

Cross-Functional & Regional Collaboration

• Act as a key legal interface between Legal Team I and legal colleagues in China, Asia Pacific, and ProBio.

• Support global alignment on legal strategy, contracting standards, compliance expectations, dispute management, and governance practices.

Leadership Expectations

• Leads and develops a regional legal team across the Americas, Europe, and the UK.

• Provides strategic, commercially practical advice to senior stakeholders.

• Demonstrates sound judgment in balancing legal risk and business objectives.

• Builds trusted relationships across legal, commercial, R&D, regulatory, compliance, finance, HR, manufacturing, and operations teams.

• Contributes to the continuous improvement of legal processes, governance practices, and risk management frameworks.

Qualifications

• Juris Doctor degree from an accredited law school.

• Active bar admission in at least one U.S. jurisdiction.

• Requires 10+ years of legal experience, including a combination of top-tier law firm training and significant in-house legal experience.

• Significant experience advising companies in the life sciences, biotechnology, pharmaceutical, CDMO, manufacturing, healthcare, or related sectors.

• Demonstrated experience leading complex commercial transactions, licensing arrangements, strategic collaborations, co-development agreements, manufacturing agreements, supply agreements, and cross-border contracting matters.

• Experience supporting M&A, financing transactions, capital markets matters, corporate governance, strategic investments, or public-company governance matters.

• Strong working knowledge of life sciences regulatory frameworks, commercial contracting, intellectual property considerations, anti-bribery and anti-corruption, FCPA, export control, data security, privacy, and cross-border compliance issues.

• Experience managing litigation, disputes, internal investigations, regulatory interactions, and outside counsel across multiple jurisdictions.

• Ability to advise senior business leaders and executive stakeholders with sound judgment, business orientation, and practical risk assessment.

• Experience supporting legal matters across the Americas, Europe, and the UK strongly preferred.

• Experience working with China, Asia Pacific, Hong Kong-listed, or cross-border business environments preferred.

• Familiarity with FDA, EU, UK, and other international regulatory frameworks preferred.

• Chinese language capability is not required but would be a plus.

#GS

#LI-EB1

Benefits:

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision insurance as well as a 401(k) retirement plan with a company match that vests fully on day one. We offer paid parental leave after just three (3) months of employment, and a paid time off policy that includes vacation time, personal time, sick time, floating holidays, and company holidays. jobs.title: Deal Operations, AMER
jobs.description:
About the Role

OpenAI is seeking a senior individual contributor to support revenue growth across the Americas (AMER) by helping sales teams structure and close commercially sound deals. You will balance speed and responsiveness with pricing discipline, consistent processes, and appropriate financial and commercial controls.

In this role, you will be the day-to-day Deal Operations partner for AMER account teams, reviewing pricing, discounts, and commercial terms across new business, renewals, and expansions. You will guide sellers through deal requirements, evaluate non-standard requests, and coordinate the approvals needed to move opportunities through contracting and closure.

You will also develop scalable workflows, guidance, and tools that improve deal turnaround times, documentation quality, and consistency across the region.

This role partners closely with Sales, Finance, Legal, Pricing, and Revenue Operations, with Product and other teams engaged as needed, to resolve deal issues and support accurate execution from quote through contract and booking.

In this role, you will:

 - Serve as the primary Deal Operations contact for AMER account teams, managing deal intake, prioritizing requests, and guiding sellers through pricing, review, and approval processes.

 - Review quotes and proposed commercial terms, including discounts, payment schedules, contract duration, and customer commitments, for accuracy and alignment with pricing guidelines and commercial policies.

 - Build financial analyses and deal models to assess revenue, margin, discount impact, and profitability, and explain the tradeoffs of proposed deal structures to decision-makers.

 - Partner with Sales to structure deals that meet customer needs and OpenAI’s commercial objectives, recommending alternatives when proposed terms fall outside established guidelines.

 - Coordinate deal reviews and required approvals across Finance, Legal, Pricing, and Revenue Operations. Prepare clear recommendations, document decisions, and escalate exceptions to the appropriate stakeholders.

 - Identify risks in non-standard terms and work with Legal and Finance to resolve contractual, billing, and revenue recognition considerations before execution.

 - Maintain complete deal records and approval documentation in CRM, CPQ, and contract management systems, and partner with Revenue Operations to align approved terms, executed agreements, and booking information.

 - Help develop and maintain deal approval policies, escalation paths, pricing guidance, and standardized templates. Improve workflows to reduce bottlenecks while maintaining appropriate controls.

 - Equip sellers with practical guidance and training on deal requirements and approval processes. Apply AI and automation to improve deal intake, knowledge retrieval, and self-service support.

 - Track Deal Desk metrics such as turnaround time, approval bottlenecks, exception trends, and quote accuracy. Use recurring deal patterns to recommend improvements to commercial policies, processes, and tools.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You Have:

 - 8+ years of experience in Deal Desk, commercial finance, pricing, sales operations, or a related function, preferably in a high-growth technology environment.

 - Hands-on experience reviewing and structuring complex enterprise deals and supporting quoting, commercial approvals, and contracting processes.

 - Strong financial modeling and analytical skills, including experience assessing pricing, discounts, revenue, margins, and deal profitability.

 - Knowledge of enterprise software commercial terms and subscription or consumption-based business models, with the judgment to identify issues that require Legal or Finance review.

 - Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to explain commercial tradeoffs, make clear recommendations, and coordinate timely decisions across teams.

 - Experience with CRM systems, configure-price-quote (CPQ) tools, and contract management platforms, along with strong spreadsheet skills.

 - Attention to detail and a track record of improving approval workflows, documentation, and operational processes as a business scales.

 - Sound commercial judgment and the ability to manage competing priorities and tight deadlines while maintaining accuracy and appropriate controls.

 - A collaborative, hands-on approach to supporting sales teams and familiarity with using AI and automation to improve deal workflows and productivity.

jobs.title: Deployment Strategist
jobs.description:
About Us

Herald is transforming how commercial insurance gets sold. We combine modern API infrastructure with industry-specific AI that can read emails, extract data, generate quotes, and guide brokers through submission workflows end-to-end. The result: faster placement, cleaner operations, and meaningful revenue growth. The market is huge, the need is obvious, and the product we’re building doesn’t exist yet. If you want to help shape the operating system for modern insurance, we’d love to work with you.

We’re a team of insurtech veterans with experience at At-Bay, Kin,  and Insurify. We’ve raised our Series A funding from top-tier VCs (Lightspeed, Brewer Lane,  Afore, Underscore) along with a panel of insurtech founders (At-Bay, Marble), insurance executives (CRC), and early employees of other successful API infrastructure companies (Plaid, Alloy).

Deployment Strategist

About the Role

Herald is looking for a Deployment Strategist to own the end-to-end success of our enterprise customers, from initial implementation through ongoing adoption and expansion.

As a Deployment Strategist, you'll work at the intersection of customer strategy, product, and technology. You'll partner directly with enterprise customers to understand their business objectives, design workflows, deploy Herald's platform, and ensure they're realizing measurable value.

This is a highly cross-functional, hands-on role. You'll be the primary point of contact for your customers, working closely with our Product, Engineering, and Sales teams to solve problems, improve workflows, and identify opportunities to scale Herald across their organizations.

We're looking for someone who can think strategically about enterprise relationships while also diving into the details of a technical issue, implementation challenge, or adoption problem.

What You'll Do

• Own Enterprise Customer Strategy Own relationships with enterprise customers, serving as their primary strategic and operational partner following contract signature. Deeply understand customers' business objectives, existing workflows, and operational challenges to identify where Herald can deliver the greatest impact. Develop and execute customer roadmaps aligned with business priorities, adoption goals, and opportunities for expansion. Build relationships with stakeholders ranging from individual users to executive leadership.

• Lead Deployments & Workflow Transformation Lead end-to-end enterprise deployments, from workflow discovery and requirements gathering through configuration, testing, onboarding, and rollout. Work directly with customer teams to understand how they operate, identify inefficiencies, and design improved workflows using Herald's platform. Coordinate cross-functional teams to deliver successful implementations and expand Herald across additional teams, business units, and workflows. Navigate complex organizational structures, competing priorities, and technical constraints to move deployments forward.

• Solve Complex Problems & Shape the Product Investigate customer challenges by analyzing data, troubleshooting platform workflows, and independently resolving configuration-level issues when possible. Partner closely with Product and Engineering to translate customer problems into actionable technical requirements and potential solutions. Synthesize customer feedback, usage patterns, and business impact to help inform product priorities. Coordinate customer-facing communication, testing, and rollout of product improvements and technical solutions.

• Drive Adoption & Measurable Customer Outcomes Own customer success beyond the initial deployment, ensuring Herald becomes embedded in customers' day-to-day operations. Proactively identify adoption barriers and develop strategies to increase platform usage and engagement. Use product data and customer insights to measure outcomes, identify opportunities, and continuously improve deployments. Lead training, enablement, and feedback sessions to ensure customers realize lasting value.

What We're Looking For

• Ability to take ownership of ambiguous problems, structure solutions, and drive execution with minimal oversight.

• A proactive mindset, intellectual curiosity, and willingness to dive into the details.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate complex problems, work with data, and develop practical solutions.

• Technical curiosity and aptitude, with the ability to understand software workflows, troubleshoot issues, and collaborate effectively with engineers.

• Strong business judgment, with the ability to understand customer objectives and translate them into actionable plans.

• Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, including comfort working with both technical teams and enterprise executives.

• Comfort operating in a fast-paced startup environment where processes and responsibilities are continuously evolving.

Nice to Have

• Experience at an early-stage B2B SaaS or AI company.

• Experience deploying enterprise software across complex organizations.

• Experience partnering directly with Product and Engineering teams.

• Experience in insurance, financial services, or other complex enterprise industries.

Additional information

Diversity, equity, and inclusion are featured prominently in our company's values which you can read about below. Please reach out if you would benefit from any assistance throughout the application or have suggestions about how we can make our process more accessible and inclusive to all people.

One more note: We want to build an incredible team. As a result, we make a point of being open to surprising candidates who are the right person even though their experience doesn't exactly match up to our job description. Our job descriptions are gestures, not strict criteria. If you think you would be a great addition to our team, but might not fit the criteria perfectly, we still encourage you to apply! We recognize there are many transferable skills and traits that we may not have captured in this description and welcome all interested candidates to apply.

Life at Herald

We're just getting started and building our culture with purpose every day. One of the joys of joining a small company early is that you get to build that culture too. Come join us and help us make Herald an (even more) amazing place to work!

Actions we value

There are many actions that we hope for and even demand from members of our team: communicating honestly, working hard, behaving with integrity. These are expectations. But we value these five actions above and beyond the level of "baseline expectation." We believe that if we excel at these, our business will thrive. We’re betting the company on it.

Build trust

We always lead with empathy. We publicly own and learn from our mistakes just as we are confident and transparent in explaining our decisions. And we help get the work done because we recognize that no job is too small.

Create a shared reality

We each articulate the facts, assumptions, questions, and fears we hold about our business. We listen to and learn from others. We create a shared set of information before making decisions.

Get better every day.

We constantly seek ways to improve ourselves. We provide each other candid feedback coupled with support to elevate those around us. We refine how we work together to become more effective as a team.

Build a diverse, equitable, and inclusive community.

We thrive when our team has a variety of lived experiences, values each other for their unique perspectives, and shares equitably in our mutual success. We invest in building an inclusive community for people who are oppressed because of their race, ethnicity, age, religion, gender expression, sexual orientation, physical ability, or socio-economic class.

(Remember that) we make the rules.

We once created the ways we work and therefore can change them. We do not default to momentum. We challenge ourselves to deconstruct the status quo and create a better future.

jobs.title: Principal Data Scientist I
jobs.description:
As Principal Data Scientist I, you are a technical leader and lead data scientist who design, build, and oversee bioinformatics platforms and data systems that streamline, integrate, and standardize scientific workflows across R&D. In this role, you will develop a deep understanding of how scientists work and what they need, then translate that into systems and data solutions with the business partner organizations they support. You will lead the development of multi-omics bioinformatics platforms and oversee the data pipelines and data operations that bring scientific data into them, managing a team of developers and bioinformaticians. You will serve as the site lead for the Cambridge satellite sites and Waltham, acting as the single point of contact to leadership and coordinating requests from site leadership to the appropriate internal teams. You will work and collaborate with teams in Neuroscience, Immunology, Quantitative Medicine and Genomics, Personalized Medicine, and Biologics and Genetic Medicine.

Responsibilities

• Workflow analysis and system design. Work with scientists and business partner organizations to understand scientific workflows and requirements, then design systems that streamline, integrate, and standardize them. Ensure solutions are scalable, reproducible, and adopted by the scientists who rely on them.
• Multi-omics platform leadership. Own the design and delivery of bioinformatics platforms supporting multi-omics modalities, with accountability for quality, usability, and maintainability across therapeutic areas.
• Data pipelines and data operations. Oversee the pipelines and data operations that move scientific data into these systems, including ingestion, processing, validation, and monitoring. Ensures data is reliable, traceable, and fit for downstream analysis.
• Team management. Manage and develop a team of software developers and bioinformaticians. Set priorities, guide and evaluate performance, and accountable for the team’s output and quality.
• Site leadership. Serve as the single point of contact and communication channel to leadership for the two Cambridge satellite sites and the Waltham site. Collect and prioritize requests from site leadership, route them to the appropriate internal teams, and communicate status and outcomes back to the sites. This is a coordination role without line authority over site staff.
• Engineering excellence. Provide hands-on technical direction across data integration, data warehousing, pipeline and software development, statistics, machine learning, and data visualization. Set standards for code quality, testing, and operational reliability.
• Cross-functional partnership. Collaborate with Neuroscience, Immunology, Quantitative Medicine and Genomics, Personalized Medicine, and Biologics and Genetic Medicine to align platform priorities with scientific needs and business goals.
• Technology evaluation. Evaluate emerging scientific and technological advances and methods and integrate those with clear value into platforms and workflows.
• Innovation and efficiency. Apply creative problem solving to difficult technical challenges and champion new approaches that deliver measurable gains in productivity and efficiency across multiple business areas.
• Compliance and security. Adhere to corporate and divisional policies, including code of conduct, safety, GxP compliance, and data security.

Required:

• Bachelor’s Degree with 8 years of experience; Master’s Degree with 7 years of experience; PhD with 3 years of experience in life science, computational, or technology field.
• Demonstrated experience designing systems that integrate and standardize scientific workflows and data, based on a strong understanding of how scientists work.
• Experience developing bioinformatics platforms or pipelines for multi-omics data (e.g., genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, single-cell, or spatial modalities).
• Experience overseeing scientific data pipelines and data operations, including data quality, lineage, and monitoring.
• Strong software engineering skills, with a record of building and deploying production-quality data and analysis applications.
• Experience managing or leading a team of developers and bioinformaticians, including setting priorities, and evaluating performance.
• Proven ability to influence and coordinate without direct authority, including prioritizing and routing competing requests from multiple groups or sites.
• Creative problem solving and a record of championing new technologies to achieve project goals.
• Excellent written and oral communication skills, including the ability to present technical work to scientific and leadership audiences.

Preferred:

• Pharmaceutical or life sciences industry experience preferred.
• Experience in Neuroscience, Immunology, personalized medicine, or biologics and genetic medicine data, and in a GxP-regulated environment.

We’re a people-centric firm, so it’s no surprise our greatest asset is our people. The impact this creates is an environment that encourages our people to grow and be creative with their talents. This approach builds a culture that is uniquely Olsson. It allows us to grow our people as we grow our business. This, in turn, creates a lasting impact on the world around us.

As a Survey Party Chief, you will take ownership of field surveying activities on a wide range of projects, including construction staking, boundary surveys, topographic surveys, and ALTA/NSPS land title surveys. Working alongside a collaborative team of survey professionals, you will leverage modern survey technology and established field practices to collect accurate data and deliver high-quality results for our clients.

One Medical is a primary care solution challenging the industry status quo by making quality care more affordable, accessible and enjoyable. But this isn’t your average doctor’s office. We’re on a mission to transform healthcare, which means improving the experience for everyone involved - from patients and providers to employers and health networks. Our seamless in-office and 24/7 virtual care services, on-site labs, and programs for preventive care, chronic care management, common illnesses and mental health concerns have been delighting people for the past fifteen years.

In February 2023 we marked a milestone when One Medical joined Amazon. Together, we look to deliver exceptional health care to more consumers, employers, care team members, and health networks to achieve better health outcomes. As we continue to grow and seek to impact more lives, we’re building a diverse, driven and empathetic team, while working hard to cultivate an environment where everyone can thrive.

The Opportunity

As a Member Support Specialist you will be an ambassador for patients in office, with a mastery of human connection and a strong drive for service. You will remove barriers to care, resulting in a truly exceptional in-office patient experience. You are the steward of the space and ensure the look and feel of the office lobby are on brand with the One Medical experience. You will be the first point of contact for patient feedback, as well as provide any other support as requested by the Practice Coordinator, Operations Manager, or in office providers.

You are a strong team player and use your innovative problem solving skills to tackle various tasks and challenges. You have a strong grasp of verbal and written communication. You are able to identify opportunities and deliver on customer-centric solutions while using empathy, focus, and compassion in all interactions with patients and teammates. You bring self-awareness to your daily work to utilize your strengths and develop your areas of opportunity. You thrive in cultures that focus on feedback and growth and are nimble in their approach to respond to the needs of the patients and team. You have an unwavering drive to help and serve others and create amazing moments for our members and teammates. If this sounds like you, we would love to connect.

• Use impeccable C-I-CARE (a framework containing the key elements of a great interaction and effective communication that we use with patients and each other) in all patient interactions and ensure a fluid and positive in-office experience through patient intake, same day schedule management, appropriate follow up scheduling, strong knowledge of billing and insurance, monitoring patient feedback and assisting with outreach as necessary

• All front of house duties including check in/check out, insurance verification, printing/paperwork tasks, prepping tests, tasking to service level expectations etc..

• At least 1 year of experience in high touch customer or patient facing roles

• Strong written and verbal communication skills

• Experience working on collaborative, diverse and feedback-driven multi-disciplinary teams

• A proven track record of persisting through change, demonstrating a forward thinking perspective when under pressure, and consistently stepping up to take action on challenges

• Proficiency in computer technology such as typing, navigating the internet and using multiple software systems simultaneously

Competitive salary: the base pay for this position is $22.00 per hour based on a full time schedule.

This is a full-time, in-person role (40 hours per week, 8 hours a day, Monday through Friday, 7:30am-5:30pm) based at our Beverly Hills office located at 9725 Wilshire Blvd, Beverly Hills, CA 90212. Office type: Pediatrics, Expanded Care. As a mandatory requirement of this role, when colleagues are out sick or on vacation, you may be asked to cover at any of our LA-area clinics, including: Century City, Culver City, El Segundo, Long Beach, Santa Monica, West LA, and Woodland Hills.

Physical Demands:  Mostly sedentary work duties require exerting up to ten pounds of force occasionally and/or small amounts of force frequently. Sedentary work typically involves sitting most of the time, but may involve walking or standing for brief periods.

One Medical offers a robust benefits package designed to aid your health and wellness.  All regular team members working 24+ hours per week and their dependents are eligible for benefits starting on the team member's date of hire:

jobs.description:
Join Axon and be a Force for Good.

At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.

Your Impact:

As Assistant General Counsel, Corporate and M&A, you are a dynamic individual contributor who brings elite transactional training — from Cravath, Kirkland & Ellis, Wachtell, Sullivan & Cromwell, or a comparable white shoe firm — and significant experience advising public companies on complex M&A, acquisitions, joint ventures, capital markets, and other strategic transactions, as well as securities reporting and corporate governance requirements. Reporting directly to the Chief Legal Officer (CLO), you will assist the CLO in managing outside counsel, personally overseeing certain key corporate initiatives, and ensuring all M&A activities align with legal requirements and support the company's strategic objectives. You will advise and collaborate with Axon's Board of Directors, C-Suite, Corporate Development Team, and SEC & Financial Reporting Team.

Critically, you should bring a passion for technology, public safety and Axon’s mission to Protect Life.

What You’ll Do:

Location: Boston or NYC
Reports to: Chief Legal Officer
Responsibilities:

• Help develop and implement the legal strategy for M&A activities in alignment with the company’s overall business and legal objectives.

• Advise the company on Securities laws and reporting requirements.

• Drive best-in-class corporate governance in partnership with the CLO, including direct engagement with Axon's Board of Directors and its committees.

• Help lead and coordinate comprehensive due diligence processes for potential M&A and capital markets transactions.

• Help manage external legal counsel.

• Partner with the Strategy & Corporate Development team to advise the business and undertake complex M&A work.

• Prepare and present legal analyses and updates on M&A activities to the executive team and board of directors.

• Draft, review, and negotiate transaction documents — including purchase agreements, term sheets, NDAs, and ancillary instruments — ensuring legal compliance and robust protection of Axon’s interests.

• Advise on and ensure compliance with securities laws.

• Liaise with regulatory authorities and manage necessary filings or approvals.

• Provide post-merger integration legal support for contract assignments, employee transitions, and regulatory compliance. resolving any legal issues during integration.

• Other duties as assigned.

What You Bring:

• J.D. from an accredited institution with outstanding academic credentials

• Admission to a State Bar within the United States

• Minimum 5-7 years’ experience working for a top tier law firm. In-house experience is a plus.

• Demonstrated legal expertise in M&A, securities law and corporate governance.

• Extensive experience in managing complex M&A transactions, preferably within the technology or financial services sector.

• Excellent writing, analytical, negotiation, communication, strategic thinking, and presentation skills

• Strong understanding of corporate and securities laws, regulations, and industry standards.

• Strong leadership, attention to detail, problem solving abilities and organization/prioritization skills.

• Demonstrated ability to successfully work with a team and in a fast paced, dynamic team environment.

Work Location

This role is based out of our NYC or Boston location and follows a hybrid schedule. We rely on in-person collaboration and ask that team members work onsite Tuesdays through Fridays, with the flexibility to work remotely on Mondays, unless there is an approved workplace accommodation. We believe that connection fuels innovation, and our in-office culture is designed to foster meaningful teamwork, mentorship, and shared success.

Benefits that Benefit You

• Competitive salary and 401k with employer match

• Discretionary paid time off

• Paid parental leave for all

• Medical, Dental, Vision plans

• Fitness Programs

• Emotional & Mental Wellness support

• Learning & Development programs

• Employee Resource Groups (ERGs)

• And yes, we have snacks in our offices

Benefits listed herein may vary depending on the nature of your employment and the location where you work.

Axon is a total compensation company, meaning compensation is made up of base pay, bonus, and stock awards. The actual base pay is dependent upon many factors, such as: level, function, training, transferable skills, work experience, business needs, geographic market, and often a combination of all these factors. Our benefits offer an array of options to help support you physically, financially and emotionally through the big milestones and in your everyday life. To see more details on our benefits offerings please visit https://www.axon.com/careers.

Base Pay Range

$205,380—$360,000 USD

Don’t meet every single requirement? That's ok. At Axon, we Aim Far. We think big with a long-term view because we want to reinvent the world to be a safer, better place. We are also committed to building diverse teams that reflect the communities we serve.

Studies have shown that women and people of color are less likely to apply to jobs unless they check every box in the job description. If you’re excited about this role and our mission to Protect Life but your experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification listed here, we encourage you to apply anyways. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

Important Notes

The above job description is not intended as, nor should it be construed as, exhaustive of all duties, responsibilities, skills, efforts, or working conditions associated with this job. The job description may change or be supplemented at any time in accordance with business needs and conditions.

Some roles may also require legal eligibility to work in a firearms environment.

We collect personal information from applicants to evaluate candidates for employment. You may request access, deletion, or exercise other CCPA rights at axongreenhousesupport@axon.com or via our Axon Privacy Web Form. For more information, please see the Your California Privacy Rights section of our Applicant and Candidate Privacy Notice.

Axon’s mission is to Protect Life and is committed to the well-being and safety of its employees as well as Axon’s impact on the environment. All Axon employees must be aware of and committed to the appropriate environmental, health, and safety regulations, policies, and procedures. Axon employees are empowered to report safety concerns as they arise and activities potentially impacting the environment.

We are an equal opportunity employer that promotes justice, advances equity, values diversity and fosters inclusion. We’re committed to hiring the best talent — regardless of race, creed, color, ancestry, religion, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship status, marital status, disability, gender identity, genetic information, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances — and empowering all of our employees so they can do their best work. If you have a disability or special need that requires assistance or accommodation during the application or the recruiting process, please email recruitingops@axon.com.  Please note that this email address is for accommodation purposes only. Axon will not respond to inquiries for other purposes.

Phishing alert:  Axon will never ask you to pay for any part of the hiring process, including training, equipment, or background checks. We do not make job offers via text message, WhatsApp, or instant messaging platforms without a formal interview process.  All legitimate job openings are listed on our official careers page at https://www.axon.com/careers.  If you receive a suspicious offer or outreach from an email address that is not @axon.com, or if you are asked for sensitive personal information (bank details, Social Security Number) prematurely, please ignore the message and report it to recruitingops@axon.com.

jobs.title: Manager, Reductions & Payor Performance
jobs.description:
We're Scan.com http://Scan.com.  We're building America's national imaging network: the infrastructure that connects patients, providers, and payers to faster, better-value diagnostic imaging.  Thousands of patients move through our platform every day, and each is a real person waiting for an answer to a healthcare concern. We exist to get them that answer faster.



We manage the medical imaging pathway end-to-end.  Providers order through a single point of entry, and from there, we run the entire medical diagnostic pathway.  Managing the full pathway, rather than brokering pieces of it, is what lets us deliver imaging faster, at higher quality, and at a lower cost than the fragmented status quo.



We're looking for a Manager, Reductions & Payor Performance at an exciting time. We've raised over $200m in funding to date, reached profitability, and are growing 100% year on year.

Millions of people wait too long for a diagnosis. Come help us fix that.




WHAT YOU WILL ACHIEVE IN THIS ROLE

As the Manager, Reductions & Payor Performance, you will lead the Reductions team within Revenue Cycle Management, reporting to the Head of RCM and own the financial results and external relationships tied to our receivables. The Reductions team works with external customers, primarily law firms, after a case is completed to ensure financial information is accurate, the right parties receive their balances and discounts, and payment arrives in due course.

This role blends three disciplines: people leadership, strategic account management, and financial analysis. You will coach and develop a team of Reductions Specialists and Team Leads, act as the senior relationship owner for our key law firm and payor partners, and review the reporting that tells us how each firm, payor, brand, and market is performing. You will turn that data into decisions that improve collections, reduce time to pay, and protect partner relationships.

As a scale-up business, you can expect your role to develop over time. Here are some of the types of things you could be getting involved in:

 - Lead, coach, and develop Reductions Specialists and Team Leads through 1:1s, goal setting, performance reviews, and structured 30/60/90-day onboarding

 - Manage workload and coverage, including market assignments and caseload balancing, and own service levels across phones, voicemails, emails, and reduction requests with clear escalation cadences for unresponsive, high-balance, or at-risk accounts

 - Set and maintain reduction guidelines, negotiation authority, and approval thresholds, and review and approve high-value or out-of-policy reduction requests

 - Own the relationship portfolio for strategic law firms and payor partners, with tiered account plans based on volume, balance, and risk, and serve as the escalation point for remediation and virtual meetings

 - Run recurring business reviews with key accounts covering outstanding balances, aging, reduction trends, payment timing, and open issues

 - Negotiate firm-level payment arrangements and agreements in line with company goals, lien and letter-of-protection terms, state lien statutes, and maintain firm-level relationship history so decisions are consistent and documented

 - Create, own, and review recurring reports on reduction percentage, collection rate, time to pay, AR aging, and payments by firm, payor, brand, market, and case type, and build rep- and team-level scorecards while flagging data-quality gaps

 - Present findings and recommendations to RCM and executive leadership, turning insights into clear actions, owners, and timelines, and recommend changes to policy, pricing, or workflow based on the data

 - Partner with Sales, Case Operations, Finance, and Product to contribute to the RCM roadmap, OKRs, and system requirements, and build the SOPs, process flows, and training materials that drive standardization and continuous improvement




WHAT YOU MIGHT BRING TO THE TABLE

You don't need to tick all the boxes to apply for this role. Whether it's your first role or your fifth role, we believe everyone can add value, learn, and grow. However, these might be some of the ways you are currently adding value:

 - Experience in revenue cycle management, medical billing, collections, or a related field

 - Experience leading, coaching, and developing individual contributors and/or team leads

 - Account management experience, including managing external partner relationships and resolving escalations

 - Strong financial acumen: pricing multiples, discount percentages, weighted averages, and the impact of negotiation decisions on revenue

 - Working knowledge of HIPAA and other medical insurance regulations and terminology, and a careful approach to handling patient information

 - Strong written and verbal communication in English, and the willingness to hold difficult, high-stakes conversations with the goal of a win-win for all parties

 - Bonus: experience in personal injury, the medical field, or medical billing, including lien-based and letter-of-protection receivables; familiarity with no-fault/PIP and workers' compensation billing rules and fee schedules; or prior law firm experience with legal terminology and state lien statutes

 - Bonus: experience building dashboards or reports in a BI tool (e.g., Tableau, Power BI, Looker) or with SQL




AI REQUIREMENTS

At Scan.com http://Scan.com, AI isn't a side project; it's how we work. We expect everyone to use AI to think faster, remove drudgery, and multiply their output. What we care about is judgment: knowing when AI makes you sharper, when it doesn't, and how to use it responsibly around patient data. You don't need to be an engineer. You need to be someone who reaches for the best tool and gets more done as a result.

Tier 2 — AI-Amplified

For this role, the expectation is that you are AI-Amplified. AI is part of your daily workflow for drafting, analysis, and research, and you know how to check its output and use it responsibly with sensitive data.

 - AI is part of your daily default. You use it to draft, analyse, research, and pressure-test your own thinking.

 - You can show concrete examples where AI made your work meaningfully faster or better.

 - You know its failure modes: you check its work, and you don't paste sensitive data into public tools.

Assessment: we'll ask you to walk through how you'd use AI to tackle a real task from the role.

One assessment principle across all tiers: we're testing judgment and adaptability, not whether you've memorized today's tools. Tools change quarterly; the ability to learn and apply them is what compounds.



 


A VIEW ON OUR CULTURE

We're building something that matters. Every scan we speed up is a real person waiting on an answer, and that urgency runs through everything we do. We move fast, we own outcomes, and take pride in our output. If you like ambiguity, working with ambitious people, and want your work to visibly move the needle, you'll feel at home here.



 


HOW WE WILL INTERVIEW YOU

We keep our interview process short and sweet. Here are the stages you can expect, but we might switch up the order depending on team availability:

 1. 30-minute introductory phone call with our Senior Talent Partner.

 2. If it feels like there is an initial fit for all, we will invite you to a 45-minute video call with the hiring manager. This is a more structured interview that will deep-dive into the role and technical needs.

 3. 'Scan Standard' interview, where our panel screens for values alignment and the success factors that matter at Scan.com http://Scan.com. You will also be assessed on your AI fluency at the stage and depth relevant to this role (see AI Requirements above).

 4. Meet the founders and/or other team members. Again, the length varies depending on how many people are involved and whether in person or via video call.

 5. Offer!




WHAT WE OFFER

We go beyond the basics with our benefits package. We believe great work starts with supporting our people. Here's what you can expect from us:

 - Salary range of $110,000 - $120,000

 - Flexible remote or hybrid work options

 - Dedicated personal development budget

 - Medical, vision, and dental coverage

 - 28+ days of paid time off across PTO and wellbeing days, so you can show up at your best

 - Paid parental leave

 - 401k retirement plan

 - All the equipment you need to do your best work

 - Inclusive, people-first policies designed by our team, for our team

 - Atlanta office perks: Complimentary team lunch every Wednesday, on-site gym access, roof terrace, and on-site lunch options




DIVERSITY AT SCAN.COM http://Scan.com

Scan.com http://Scan.com is committed to eliminating discrimination and encouraging diversity within our team. We strive to provide equality and fairness for all job applicants and employees and never discriminate on the basis of gender, marital status, age, race, ethnicity, religion, or physical differences.

We are opposed to all forms of unlawful treatment and discrimination.

Our ambition is for our team to be representative of society's diversity, and for every employee to feel respected and able to bring their best selves to work.

If you need an accommodation to apply or interview, contact us at people@scan.com.

We look forward to receiving your application!

jobs.title: Automated Driving Advanced Development Intern, Machine Learning Research (Cambridge)
jobs.description:
At Toyota Research Institute (TRI), we’re on a mission to improve the quality of human life. We’re developing new tools and capabilities to amplify the human experience. To lead this transformative shift in mobility, we’ve built a world-class team advancing the state of the art in AI, robotics, driving, and material sciences.
This is a paid 12-week internship opportunity and is a hybrid, in-office role.
Here’s a glimpse into the Internship experience from some of our TRI interns!


The Team
The Automated Driving Advanced Development division bridges TRI research and Toyota products. In partnership with Woven by Toyota, the team is researching and developing an end-to-end learned driving stack that maps sensor inputs directly to planned trajectories.
The Internship
We’re seeking a research intern to investigate how driving policies post-trained in fast, low-fidelity simulation can transfer to higher-fidelity simulation and real-world driving. This is an open research problem: differences in sensor inputs, vehicle dynamics, and other agents can limit transfer, and policies may learn simulator-specific behavior or forget previously learned skills.
You’ll lead an independent research project exploring approaches to sim-to-sim and sim-to-real transfer for sensor-based driving models. You’ll work with Toyota driving data, generative base models, and closed-loop simulation infrastructure, with the goal of producing work suitable for a conference or workshop submission.
The Opportunity
As a research intern on AD2, you will own a standalone research project in sim-to-sim and sim-to-real domain mapping, with the opportunity to:
Drive your own research: Shape the approach, run experiments, and analyze results, with the independence to set your own direction.
Publish your findings: The project is designed to produce results suitable for a conference or workshop publication.
Shape a real autonomy model: The tools and insights you create will help the team post-train our autonomy model more effectively, with the potential to influence the autonomy stack eventually deployed in Toyota vehicles.
Collaborate with experienced researchers: Work closely with a small team of industry-leading researchers with deep experience in robotics and autonomous driving.
Work at scale: Use the same large-scale Toyota driving data, base models, and simulation infrastructure the team uses every day.
You can learn more about our work on the Automated Driving Advanced Development team page.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills

• Experience working in a CRO and/or pharmaceutical/biotech environment

Preferred Qualifications

• Prior interaction with regulatory agencies

The Application Process

ClinChoice is a global full-service CRO specializing in clinical development and functional solutions for pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, and consumer health companies. Our mission drives our culture: to contribute to a healthier and safer world by accelerating the development and commercialization of innovative drugs and devices.
