jobs.title: GTM Strategy & Operations - Strategic Planning
jobs.location: New York City, NY; San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic's go-to-market organization is growing quickly, and every territory and account assignment has to land correctly for the field to do its best work. The Strategic Planning team sits at the center of that. We work across field Strategy & Operations, Finance, Systems, Data, Incentives and People to help leadership decide where to invest, turn those decisions into a plan, and keep the plan working all year.

This role owns the account side of GTM planning, who covers what: territories, the data enrichment and system requirements behind them, rules of engagement (RoEs), and the account moves that follow during the year.

You'll join a small, high-leverage team and take end-to-end ownership of that scope. That starts with understanding the plan: how coverage, territories and account data fit together, what assumptions sit underneath them, and what happens downstream when one changes. From there you'll plan your area during the cycle, run it through the year as the business moves, and build the tools that make it easier. When something keeps breaking, we expect you to find out why and fix it at the source.

Key responsibilities

• Build and maintain the territory models and methods behind the plan

• Partner on segmentation definitions and strategy, and turn them into the account rules and criteria that territories are built on

• Carry territories from design through validation with the business, QA and go-live

• Own data enrichment and system requirements for territories and accounts, working with Systems and Data

• Run account moves and RoEs through the year, and turn one-off requests into a clear process with rules, templates and turnaround times

• Spot patterns in what breaks after a plan ships and feed them into the next plan's design

• Build tools and automations with Claude that remove manual work for the Strategy & Operations business partner community

You may be a good fit if you

• Deep alignment to Anthropic’s mission

• Direct experience with territory design

• Hands-on experience in sales planning, GTM strategy, revenue operations or a similar analytical role

• Advanced spreadsheet modeling, including building models that others can follow, audit and reuse

• Experience working with CRM data such as Salesforce, including accounts, ownership and hierarchies

• Ability to identify which assumptions matter most in a model and explain the downstream effects of changing them

• Experience running a process with many stakeholders to a fixed deadline

• Ability to earn the trust of field leaders and partner teams, and get work done through them without direct authority

• Track record of moving work forward through teams you don't manage

• Clear written and verbal communication with both field and leadership audiences

• Hands-on use of AI tools such as Claude to speed up analysis or remove manual work

Strong candidates may also

• Experience with planning at a company that was scaling its field team quickly

• Experience enriching CRM data or writing requirements for a systems team

• Experience with AI/ML companies and consumption business models

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:

$190,000—$270,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

jobs.title: Clinical Pharmacist Float, Full-time Rotating
jobs.description:
The Clinical Pharmacist reflects the mission, vision, and values of NM, adheres to the organization’s Code of Ethics and Corporate Compliance Program, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and all other regulatory and accreditation standards.

The Clinical Pharmacist is responsible for identifying, preventing, and/or resolving medication related problems; for providing authoritative information to other health care professionals, patients, and the public; and for assuring that the informational, clinical, and drug distribution components of pharmacy services function as an integrated system to provide patient centered care to the patients and staff of Northwestern Medicine.

The mission of the Department of Pharmacy is to deliver the safest, highest quality, most effective and efficient patient care while developing the best people, advancing research, and integrating pharmacy services to successfully coordinate care across the Northwestern Medicine enterprise.

The vision of the Department of Pharmacy is to be a recognized as a national leader in advancing the pharmacy enterprise through excellence, innovation, education and research.

Responsibilities:

• Interprets medication orders to ensure safety and proper use of medications and is alert to compatibilities, incompatibilities, medication duplication, medication allergies, and potential medication administration errors. Coordinates the solving of medication related problems between pharmacy, nursing, and prescribers, demonstrating initiative and sound judgment.
• Monitors medication therapy for significant drug-drug, drug-diet, or drug-laboratory test interactions. Intervenes in circumstances of significant interactions, therapeutic duplications, and other occasions where pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic expertise is warranted.
• Evaluates and documents that the medication(s) selected are appropriate for achieving the desired therapeutic outcome. Communicates potential problems and likely solutions to the prescriber.
• Acts as a consultant in the areas of pharmacokinetics and adverse reactions to physicians, nurses and other healthcare professionals. Participates in all therapeutic drug monitoring or intervention programs; adjusting therapy as indicated by patient condition and laboratory results.
• Processes all medication order information into the Electronic Health Record to ensure accuracy of records regarding past, current and future dispensing and charging.
• Maintains a comprehensive pharmacy patient profile. The profile should include age, maturation, weight, allergies, diagnosis, estimated and actual pharmacokinetic parameters, and pertinent information which may affect medication therapy decisions.
• Oversees the packaging labeling, and distribution of medications for all patients and employees according to established policies, procedures, and guidelines. Monitors the use of scheduled medications on the nursing units and maintains controlled inventories of medication in the dispensing areas.
• Compounds and dispenses pharmaceuticals including sterile products, chemotherapy and parenteral nutrition products.
• Verifies medication orders before delivery to patient care areas and ensures accuracy and completeness. Resolves discrepancies as necessary.
• Reviews all laboratory data for appropriateness of medication use and recommends changes when needed. Including microbial culture and sensitivity data, toxicology, therapeutic drug monitoring, etc.
• Develops and presents orientation, education and training programs for medical, nursing, hospital and pharmacy staff, as well as assisting in the educating of pharmacy students, residents, and fellows.
• Educates patients and their families about specific medications.
• Responds to emergency situations to assist with medication management (e.g. response to cardiac arrests)
• Provides accurate and timely medication information and or teaching to healthcare professionals or patients.
• Maintains the hospital formulary and acts to limit medication usage to formulary items when appropriate
• Documents all clinical activities and interventions performed. Collects data, maintains logs, records and other documentation as required by the department
• Communicates professional knowledge effectively in both oral and written forms to patients and other health professionals.
• Participates in quality improvement and medication use review activities of the department.
• Organizes, prioritizes, and plans workload within given time constraints. Works cooperatively with fellow pharmacists to oversee and direct the activities of the work area, to assign work to technicians, and to assure that the established department objectives are accomplished
• Reviews restocking automated dispensing cabinets (ADCs) throughout the hospital and resolves any problems.
• Ensures compliance with hazardous waste collection and disposal procedures.
• Maintains proficiency and expertise in area/s of practice through continuous professional development.
• All other job duties as assigned.

Minimum Requirements:

Education:

• Bachelor’s Degree in Pharmacy or a Doctor of Pharmacy Degree

Licensure:

• Active Clinical Pharmacist license in the state of Illinois (IDFPR)

Preferred:

• Training and knowledge of specialty areas (neonatology, critical care, oncology, etc.)
• Completion of a pharmacy residency program or equivalent hospital pharmacy experience

Northwestern Medicine is an equal opportunity employer (disability, VETS) and does not discriminate in hiring or employment on the basis of age, sex, race, color, religion, national origin, gender identity, veteran status, disability, sexual orientation or any other protected status.

Background Check

Northwestern Medicine conducts a background check that includes criminal history on newly hired team members and, at times, internal transfers. If you are offered a position with us, you will be required to complete an authorization and disclosure form that gives Northwestern Medicine permission to run the background check.  Results are evaluated on a case-by-case basis, and we follow all local, state, and federal laws, including the Illinois Health Care Worker Background Check Act.

Artificial Intelligence Disclosure

Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools may be used in some portions of the candidate review process for this position, however, all employment decisions will be made by a person.

Benefits

We offer a wide range of benefits that provide employees with tools and resources to improve their physical, emotional, and financial well-being while providing protection for unexpected life events.

Click on or copy and paste URL to your browser to view detailed benefits information https://jobs.nm.org/benefits

Please refer to the Benefits Eligibility by Employment Classification to determine benefits eligibility for job postings.

If sign-on bonus is included in a job posting eligibility is as followed: Internal employees and rehires who left Northwestern Medicine within 1 year are not eligible for the sign-on bonus. Exception: New graduate internal employees seeking their first licensed clinical position as a Registered Nurse at NM may be eligible.

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
Job Opportunity: Executive Director with Make-A-Day in Columbus, OH

Are you a mission-driven leader passionate about making a meaningful impact in your community? Do you have experience leading nonprofit programs, fundraising efforts, and high-performing teams? If you answered yes, then we want to speak with you!

As the Executive Director, you will provide strategic and operational leadership to advance Make-A-Day’s mission of empowering Central Ohio neighbors facing homelessness and economic instability. You will partner closely with the Board of Directors, lead programs and community outreach, strengthen fundraising efforts, oversee financial and organizational operations, and develop relationships that expand MAD’s impact throughout the community.

Salary range: $80,000 - $85,000, commensurate with experience.

Key Responsibilities:

• Execute the Board’s strategic direction and lead multi-year and annual planning, setting priorities as organizational and community needs evolve.

• Oversee MAD’s Stabilize, Restore, and Advance service model, including outreach events, Move the Box, housing and legal navigation, and food truck operations.

• Develop and manage the volunteer program, including recruitment, training, scheduling, recognition, and partner follow-up.

• Lead fundraising efforts across government and foundation grants, corporate sponsorships, individual giving, and special events, including grant compliance and reporting.

• Cultivate and maintain relationships with donors, funders, sponsors, public agencies, and community partners.

• Develop and manage the annual budget, cash flow, financial reporting, internal controls, and 501(c)(3) compliance.

• Hire, supervise, and develop staff while fostering a respectful, trauma-informed workplace and supporting AmeriCorps VISTA members.

• Establish performance measures and KPI dashboards, using data and community feedback to strengthen programs and report results to the Board, funders, and public.

• Represent MAD in community coalitions, policy discussions, and media engagement related to housing, homelessness, encampments, and justice involvement.

• Create meaningful leadership and service opportunities for individuals with lived experience.

Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s degree in social work, public administration, nonprofit leadership, or a related field.

• 5+ years of experience in social services, housing, health, or a related human services field.

• 5+ years of staff supervision experience, including managing other people managers.

• Experience with budgeting, financial reporting, grant compliance, fundraising, and grant writing.

• Strong leadership, management, and communication skills with the ability to lead diverse teams and build trusted relationships.

• Knowledge of housing, health, behavioral health, and justice systems in Franklin County.

• Experience managing volunteer programs, community partnerships, data collection, and outcomes measurement.

• Comfortable working in nontraditional environments, including streets, parks, and encampments.

• Valid driver’s license, reliable transportation, and flexibility to work early mornings, evenings, or weekends as needed.

• Graduate degree such as an MPA, MSW, or related credential is preferred.

• Knowledge of human services public policy, Medicaid, criminal justice, mental health, substance use services, overdose prevention, or trauma-informed practices is a plus.

• Lived experience or experience serving individuals facing homelessness or other marginalized communities is preferred.

Why Join Make-A-Day?

Because this is more than an executive leadership role. It’s an opportunity to help strengthen an organization making a direct impact in the lives of Central Ohio neighbors facing homelessness and economic instability. Make-A-Day’s work is centered on helping people Stabilize, Restore, and Advance through outreach, advocacy, community partnerships, and essential services. You’ll have the opportunity to lead a dedicated team, strengthen community relationships, grow programs and resources, and help shape the organization’s future impact.

Make-A-Day also offers medical, dental, and vision insurance with 50% of the employee premium covered; a 401(k) with automatic 3% enrollment; unlimited vacation; 13 paid holidays; a semi-flexible schedule; hybrid work; and training and development opportunities.

Apply online today to join a great team and help Make-A-Day continue making a meaningful difference throughout Central Ohio!

Reports To: Branch Manager

Do you have an interest in becoming an experienced electrical or mechanical technician? Are you able and capable of working at extreme heights?  Konecranes has many opportunities open across the united states that we are looking to fill with mechanically inclined individuals. At Konecranes, service technicians are the heart of our industry. Our technicians work in a safety first type of environment and don’t mind heights or working on mechanical parts. As a service technician, you will be working with 480 3 phase motors, troubleshooting issues with our cranes, and working with clients and facility directors to ensure that our clients are properly being taken care of.  Our service technicians are provided with a company vehicle for their travels, and have the opportunity to experience new and challenging situations with each job

Principal Responsibilities:

• Perform mechanical maintenance and inspections on Rubber Tyred Gantry (RTG’s), Ship to Shore (STS), Rail Mounted Gantry (RMG), Automated Stacking Cranes (ASC), Straddle Carriers, Munck Loader, Goliath Gantry, Level Luffing cranes at customer locations.
• Conduct extensive on site mechanical troubleshooting to determine cause for equipment malfunction and establish the necessary repairs utilizing visual inspection, test procedures and appropriate test equipment.
• Perform on site repairs on customer’s cranes in conjunction with planned repairs as part of customer’s maintenance contract, in response to a service call or on an emergency call due to an equipment breakdown.
• Responsible for a basic understanding and working knowledge or all OSHA, ANSI, CMAA, and other codes or regulations pertaining to our industry. Must be able to get specific regulations if requested.
• Responsible for completing all daily paperwork required accurately and completely.
• Document and log any quotations you provide customers (either verbal or written) and generate a document or copy of your quote for use as a follow-up sheet.
• Review with the customer all repairs you performed and get their signature on the daily service report indicating their acceptance of proper and completed work.
• Responsible for maintaining a professional appearance and image at all times.
• Maintain all company equipment and assets in proper working order and neat or clean.
• Maintain a stock of the appropriate forms and literature on the service vehicle and be capable of utilizing the proper documentation and forms used by the service department.
• Responsible for keeping a proper stock level of inventory and line stock items on the service vehicle.
• Accountable for all the company issued tools, ladders, and inventory levels assigned to you.
• Responsible for generating sales and service leads during service calls and identifying the proper Konecranes personnel of the customer’s need and level of interest.
• Must develop a thorough working knowledge of our service literature, service policies and labor rates.
• Must provide customers with a “Safety Summary” on any safety items noticed during service visits and bring back a signed copy of the document as evidence of our notice to the customer. (This is a basic professional courtesy required at all times. It also may protect Konecranes from any liability if the crane is used.)
• Must maintain regular communication with the local office and/or call in a minimum of once per day to the service supervisor.
• Responsible for understanding the procurement of basic parts on service jobs, completing the proper purchase orders and developing a good working knowledge of local vendors and vendor stocked parts. If the job permits or the situation warrants, all the ordering of parts for jobs should be done by the technician servicing the account and this time should be billed to the project.
• Responsible for working a “fair share” of any 24 hour call and overtime necessary. This will be divided as equally as possible by the service supervisor.
• Responsible for completing a “Safety Audit” on the limit switches and proper general operation of any crane you have worked on or inspected prior to leaving the customer’s premises.

Education: Prefer two-year associate degree in Industrial Electrical/Mechanical Technology or related field or equivalent vocational/technical training and experience.

Experience: Minimum one (1) years’ experience involving mechanical and/or industrial troubleshooting and repair.

Company Vehicle: Our Service Technicians get a work truck and a gas card to be used for business purposes. Candidates must pass a Motor Vehicle Record (MVR) check.

Benefits: Medical Plan (You can reduce your deductible by participating in our Wellness Program for 2024. Employees will then have the option to potentially get their medical benefits at no cost in 2025. Ask us for details!) Dental, Vision, 401k plan with a match from day one, profit sharing, identity theft protection, accident insurance, travel insurance and so much more!

Other Requirements: Must have good mechanical aptitude. Must have and maintain a good driving record, including a valid driver’s license. Must be willing and able to work off the ground. Must be willing and able to work overtime and out of town as necessary. Must be willing and able to work in demanding work environments.

Must be able to frequently lift up to 25 lbs. Must be able to lift up to 50 lbs. on a daily basis. Must be able to lift up to 75 lbs. although not on a daily basis. Must be able to lift 100 lbs. on a rare basis. This position requires frequent climbing, balancing, stooping/crouching, and overhead reaching. This position requires occasional pushing, pulling, kneeling, and crawling. You will be inside approximately 90% of the time and outside approximately 10% of the time. You will be frequently exposed to heat, cold, noise and heights.

• This is a safety sensitive position.

What we offer:

Benefits: Medical Plan, Dental, Vision, 401k plan with a match from day one, profit sharing, identity theft protection, accident insurance, travel insurance and so much more!

Vacation: 2 weeks of vacation per year (pro-rated for the first year depending on start date). 5-12 years of service, 3 weeks. 13+ years of service, 4 weeks.

Sick Leave: 5 days of Sick Leave per year. Pro-rated the first year after 90 days of service

Holidays: 10 paid holidays per year

The CSS serves as the primary day-to-day client contact, working closely with the Client Service Manager to ensure operational excellence, consistent service quality, and a professional client experience.

Operations and Service Delivery

jobs.title: Strategic Supply Chain Manager
jobs.description:
Antora Energy delivers affordable, reliable energy to industry, data centers, and the grid. Our thermal batteries turn low-cost electricity into always-on heat and power, without supply-constrained critical minerals or multi-year construction timelines.

We are growing our company with people who put team and mission first, value connection through laughter and joy, and work with humility and openness. We are committed to building a diverse, passionate, and creative team dedicated to a future powered by abundant, clean, low-cost energy.

Position Summary

• Antora Energy is electrifying heavy industry with zero-carbon heat and power. We make it possible and profitable for industrial processes to run entirely on renewable energy. We are now deploying commercial-scale systems and scaling to volume. The Strategic Supply Chain Manager creates and carries out Antora’s sourcing strategy to deliver the lowest cost of stored energy. In this role you don’t wait for problems to be handed to you. You spot them first, reframe them, and change the outcome, with numbers to show for it. You will build process, tools and data where none exist, without adding bureaucracy, and you will own outcomes from start to finish. You’ll use AI every day to move faster and see further than a traditional supply chain team can. This is a full-time, site-based position.

Roles & Responsibilities

• Shape designs, not just source them. Work with Engineering before design freeze. Challenge specs that add cost without adding function, and bring supplier capability and DFM input early.

• Build sourcing strategy from first principles. Develop and maintain should-cost models (material, labor, overhead, margin) for key components, and use them to drive design, build-vs-buy and sourcing decisions.

• Develop and scale suppliers. Identify strategic suppliers for pilot and commercial systems based on quality, capacity and cost. Take immature suppliers from prototype to volume using FAI, process controls and PPAP/APQP-style gates. Plan capacity ahead of demand, and know when to invest in a supplier and when to walk away.

• Get ahead of supply risk. Map risk across the BOM down to sub-tier suppliers. Track supplier financial health, tariffs, geopolitics and domestic-content requirements, and mitigate risks before they turn into disruptions.

• Negotiate from data and leverage. Negotiate supply agreements and BOM cost. Trade terms for value, such as volume for price or payment terms for reserved capacity. Know which clauses carry real risk (LDs, warranty, IP, liability caps, capacity commitments).

• Create structure in ambiguity. Make sound calls on partial information, separate stable work from moving work, and keep suppliers and internal teams steady through design and schedule churn.

• Drive decisions across functions. Work with Engineering, Finance, Ops and Legal to turn competing priorities into clear tradeoffs and timely decisions. Lead Executive Business Reviews and escalate when executive intervention is needed.

• Manage supplier relationships, forecasts and on-time delivery, using objective performance measures to improve supplier performance.

• Build the function. Create supply chain tools, processes and policies (e.g., Supplier Code of Conduct). Define, recruit, hire and develop a supply chain team as needs arise.

AI-Enabled Supply Chain: Why It Matters Here
AI is central to how this team works. A small team can only build a supply chain that scales to commercial volume if it uses AI to do work that would otherwise take many more people. In this role you will:

• Build and update should-cost models faster, and benchmark supplier quotes against commodity and market data.

• Use AI to map sub-tier supply networks, monitor supplier risk signals (financials, tariffs, geopolitical events) and flag exposure early.

• Use AI to speed up RFQ analysis, contract review and redlining, so you can focus your judgment on the clauses and terms that matter.

• Build your own lightweight tools, dashboards and automations instead of waiting for IT or adding headcount.

• Help set the standard for how the wider supply chain team adopts AI.

We’re looking for someone who already uses AI tools in their daily work and has real examples of how it changed their speed, the quality of their analysis, or their results.

Key Qualifications

• 5+ years of supply chain management experience, covering strategic and tactical supply, supplier development and executive escalations.

• Experience in semiconductor, solar, energy storage or related hardware supply chains.

• Technical credibility with engineers: you understand drawings, tolerances and manufacturing processes well enough to challenge a spec and diagnose problems on a supplier’s floor.

• Proven record of major cost reductions achieved by working with suppliers and engineering, with before-and-after numbers.

• Experience building should-cost models and using them to change sourcing or design decisions.

• Experience scaling at least one supplier from low volume to production.

• Hands-on use of AI tools (e.g., LLMs, AI-assisted analytics, automation) in supply chain work.

• Strong analytical skills, including statistical concepts and data analysis, and working knowledge of MRP/ERP systems.

• Love for negotiating costs and contracts.

• Ability to explain complex tradeoffs to executives clearly and briefly.

• Bachelor’s degree in engineering, supply chain, business or a related discipline.

• Low ego, team-first, and fun to work with.

• Ability to work onsite at our Sunnyvale facility.

Additional Qualifications Desired

• Global perspective: international sourcing, customs, shipping and working across cultures.

• Familiarity with domestic-content requirements and tariff mitigation strategies.

Work Location:  Onsite - San Jose, CA

Salary Range:  $170,000 USD - $190,000 USD

Salary Basis:  Annual

This job posting contains the salary range that Antora Energy believes it would be willing to pay for the posted job. The actual salary offered will be determined within the posted range based on a candidate's experience, credentials, and expertise as they pertain to the requirements of the position.

In addition to a competitive base salary, Antora Energy’s Total Rewards program includes a premium health benefits package with life and disability insurance, a 401K plan, a flexible spending account, industry leading paid time off policy, providing a flexible and inclusive holiday observance, as well as paid volunteer time off.

#Li-AV

WHAT IS BOX?

Box (NYSE:BOX) is the leader in Intelligent Content Management. Our platform enables organizations to fuel collaboration, manage the entire content lifecycle, secure critical content, and transform business workflows with enterprise AI. We help companies thrive in the new AI-first era of business. Founded in 2005, Box simplifies work for leading global organizations, including JLL, Morgan Stanley, and Nationwide. Box is headquartered in Redwood City, CA, with offices across the United States, Europe, and Asia.

By joining Box, you will have the unique opportunity to continue driving our platform forward. Content powers how we work. It’s the billions of files and information flowing across teams, departments, and key business processes every single day: contracts, invoices, employee records, financials, product specs, marketing assets, and more. Our mission is to bring intelligence to the world of content management and empower our customers to completely transform workflows across their organizations. With the combination of AI and enterprise content, the opportunity has never been greater to transform how the world works together and at Box you will be on the front lines of this massive shift.

WHAT MAKES US DIFFERENT

We operate with a founder-like mindset: we move fast, take ownership, and hold ourselves to a high bar. We are genuinely customer-obsessed, and we bring that same curiosity and care to how we work with each other. If you want to work somewhere that challenges you, trusts you, and gives you the opportunity to do work that actually moves the needle, Box is that place.

WHY BOX NEEDS YOU

Every enterprise is sitting on a goldmine they can't access. Millions of documents, contracts, presentations, images, and emails, the institutional knowledge that defines how a company operates, are locked in legacy systems, invisible to the AI models and agents that could transform how work gets done. Box is the platform that changes that.Box has seen a major evolution since pioneering cloud storage solutions. Today, we are building the secure, intelligent content layer that connects enterprise knowledge to AI powering any model, any agent, and any workflow, while maintaining the governance, compliance, and control that the world's largest organizations demand. AI is only as powerful as the information it can securely access, and that is exactly what Box provides.The enterprises that win the AI era will be the ones that can securely connect their models to the right knowledge, at the right time, with the right controls. Box is that foundation, and we've been building toward this moment for over 20 years.

We are seeking high-caliber sales professionals to drive new customer acquisition and expand relationships across our largest enterprise accounts As an Enterprise Account Executive, you’ll be bringing in new logos as well as growing and expanding existing customers within our largest accounts. You won't be selling a point solution, you'll be helping all lines of business rethink the role of their most valuable asset, their content.

• Proven ability to translate complex platform capabilities into clear business value, communicating emerging technology effectively to diverse audiences, from technical practitioners to senior leadership.

• Display curiosity about AI, eager to learn, and passionate about helping organizations navigate major technological advancements.

Box lives its values, with community and in-person collaboration being a core part of our culture. Boxers are expected to work from their assigned office a minimum of 3 days per week. jobs.title: Process Engineer, MSAT, Drug Substance
jobs.description:
Amylyx has an audacious mission to usher in a new era for treating diseases with high unmet needs. Where others see challenges, we see opportunities that we pursue with urgency, rigorous science, and unwavering commitment to the communities we serve. We are a clinical-stage company currently focused on post-bariatric hypoglycemia (PBH), Wolfram syndrome, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).

Our mission is powered by our people. Our core values – be audacious, be curious, be authentic, be engaged, and be accountable – creating a culture of caring. Amylyx has assembled an experienced team ready to take action because the communities we serve have no time to wait. If you share our passion and are determined to tackle some of medicine’s toughest problems, we encourage you to read the opportunity below and apply.

The Opportunity

The Principal Process Engineer, MSAT Drug Substance, will serve as the global process owner and technical subject matter expert for avexitide, a GLP-1 antagonist peptide drug substance, and partner closely with Quality, QC, CMC, and External Manufacturing teams to ensure reliable, compliant, and efficient operational execution. The role is accountable for drug substance technology transfer, process validation, continued process verification, investigations, change control, and process lifecycle management while building collaborative, trust-based relationships across internal and external stakeholders. This role reports to the Director, Manufacturing Sciences and Technology.

Responsibilities

Global Process Ownership and CMC Representation:

• Serve as the global process owner for assigned products ensuring comparability across manufacturing locations.

• Provide technical authorship and review for regulatory submissions (BLA, NDA, MAA), validation reports, and responses to regulatory agency questions.

• Represent MSAT on CMC teams as the product drug substance owner and process SME.

• Assess technical and regulatory impact of potential changes to global process.

• Author annual product reviews/assessments to satisfy global health authority requirements.

• Lead process transfers to new manufacturing sites, or larger-scale facilities as required.

• Partner with technical development to evaluate and implement new process technology as required.

Process Validation:

• Lead drug substance technology transfer activities between clinical, validation, and commercial manufacturing sites.

• Define critical process parameters (CPPs), critical quality attributes (CQAs), and in-process controls for peptide drug substance unit operations.

• Develop and execute process validation strategies, including PPQ planning, statistical sampling plans, and acceptance criteria aligned with regulatory guidance.

• Support new drug substance introductions and commercial launches by ensuring peptide manufacturing processes are validated, scalable, robust, and inspection-ready.

Manufacturing Support:

• Provide technical leadership and day-to-day process engineering support for clinical and commercial drug substance manufacturing at external CDMOs.

• Serve as the process engineering SME during manufacturing operations, providing onsite support when required.

• Lead investigations, perform rigorous root cause analysis and develop scientifically sound CAPAs, ensuring alignment with regulatory expectations and industry best practices.

• Assess and author technical risk assessments and change controls to support manufacturing changes, investigations, and regulatory filings.

• Ensure strict compliance with cGMPs, global regulatory requirements, and internal quality systems for drug substance manufacturing.

• Review and provide technical input into master batch records, campaign readiness plans, process descriptions, and manufacturing documentation to ensure process requirements are accurately translated into GMP execution.

Data Analysis & Continued Process Verification:

• Lead continued process verification (CPV) and routine data trending for manufacturing unit operations, in-process controls, and critical process parameters.

• Develop and maintain data repositories, dashboards, and meaningful KPIs to assess process capability, performance, and trends.

• Identify early signals of process drift, yield loss, impurity shifts, raw material variability, or scale-dependent performance risks and proactively drive corrective or preventive actions.

• Prepare and present quarterly CPV summaries and technical assessments for internal management reviews.

Continuous Improvement:

• Identify and execute continuous improvement initiatives focused on process robustness, impurity control, yield, cycle time, capacity, and operational efficiency.

• Apply Quality by Design (QbD), Design of Experiments (DoE), statistical process control (SPC), and risk-based decision making to optimize drug substance manufacturing processes.

• Collaborate with CDMOs to implement best practices, new technologies, or process enhancements where appropriate.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in chemical engineering or a related field with 10+ years of relevant experience, or Master’s degree with 8+ years of relevant experience.

• Experience with peptide or biologic drug substance late-phase/commercial manufacturing is required including relevant downstream operations such as chromatography purification, ultrafiltration or diafiltration, and lyophilization.

• Experience with liquid phase, hybrid, tag-assisted synthesis, or green chemistry peptide manufacturing is a plus.

• Comprehensive understanding of cGMP principles and regulatory requirements, including process, equipment, and facility validation.

• Familiarity with modeling and optimization tools (e.g., MATLAB, JMP) is a plus.

• Detail-oriented with strong problem-solving skills and ability to identify subtle trends in data.

• Excellent communication and teamwork skills.

• Demonstrated ability to lead technical discussions with external partners, influence cross-functional decisions without direct authority, and communicate complex process risks clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

• Ability to travel to domestic and international CMOs up to 20%.

Work Location and Conditions

• At Amylyx, we proudly support remote work opportunities within the United States. However, due to business considerations candidates must be able to attend meetings at our office in Cambridge, MA on a regular basis. Preference will be given to candidates who reside in the New England region and can be in person on an as needed basis.

• When working remotly, you must have access to a work setting which enables meeting all requirements of the role (including privacy, reliable internet access, phone, ability to video conference, etc.) at your remote location.

Compensation

The pay range posted below represents our good faith estimate of compensation for this role, based on market data and internal benchmarks. The final offer may vary depending on a candidate’s experience, skills, and qualifications, as well as considerations of internal equity.

Base salary is one component of Amylyx’s total rewards package. In addition to competitive base pay, eligible employees may receive annual performance-based bonuses and equity awards, providing an opportunity to share in the company’s long-term success. Amylyx also offers a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the health, well-being, and financial security of our employees.

Estimated Pay Range

$171,000—$192,000 USD

Amylyx’s management team is dedicated to this policy with respect to recruitment, hiring, placement, promotion, transfer, training, compensation, benefits, employee activities, access to facilities and programs, and general treatment during employment. Accommodations are available for candidates who require them in our selection process. If you need an accommodation, please let your Amylyx Talent Acquisition contact know.

jobs.title: Exposure Management Engineer - Mid-Atlantic region (Remote)
jobs.description:
GuidePoint Security provides trusted cybersecurity expertise, solutions and services that help organizations make better decisions and minimize risk. By taking a three-tiered, holistic approach for evaluating security posture and ecosystems, GuidePoint enables some of the nation’s top organizations, such as Fortune 500 companies and U.S. government agencies, to identify threats, optimize resources and integrate best-fit solutions that mitigate risk.

General Description

We are looking for a skilled Exposure Management Engineer to support GuidePoint Security's Mid-Atlantic Exposure Management practice, with a primary focus on deploying, configuring, and operating the Axonius Asset Cloud to power risk-based vulnerability management and cyber asset management for our clients. This role will engage in the development of unified asset inventories, risk-based prioritization models, and automated remediation workflows in Axonius while providing “Wow Them” service to clients and/or internal customers or co-workers.

The Exposure Management Engineer will be required to demonstrate strong asset management, integration, and risk-based vulnerability management skills, lead by influence, and strong business/financial acumen to drive the use of progressive exposure management programs — built on Axonius — that will align the delivery of business objectives and priorities.

About the Mid-Atlantic Exposure Management Practice

The Mid-Atlantic Exposure Management Practice is responsible for helping clients see everything they own and fix what matters most. We build unified, real-time asset inventories and risk-based exposure programs — with the Axonius Asset Cloud at the center — that turn fragmented data from hundreds of security and IT tools into a single, trusted asset model and a prioritized, business-aware remediation backlog.

Our team of exposure management engineers, Axonius platform specialists, and automation developers focuses on cyber asset attack surface management (CAASM), risk-based vulnerability management (RBVM), and exposure prioritization. We partner with client security, IT, infrastructure, and cloud teams to eliminate blind spots, de-duplicate findings across tools, assign asset ownership, and drive measurable risk reduction.

Key focus areas of the practice:

• Deploying and configuring the Axonius Asset Cloud — data connections, asset correlation, and coverage gap analysis

• Configuring risk-based vulnerability management in Axonius — de-duplication, asset criticality, exploitability, and business-context prioritization

• Automating enforcement, ticketing, and remediation workflows using the Axonius query and enforcement engine

Roles and Responsibilities:

Axonius Platform Engineering

• Deploy, configure, and maintain the Axonius Asset Cloud (Cyber Asset Attack Surface Management / exposure platform) across complex hybrid, multi-cloud, and on-premises client environments.

• Design and build data connections (adapters) to onboard data from security, IT, identity, cloud, endpoint, and network sources — EDR, vulnerability scanners, MDM, IdP, CMDB, cloud providers, NGFW, and case management tools — via API.

• Configure and tune the Axonius asset correlation engine so that data from disparate sources resolves into unified, de-duplicated asset records.

• Perform daily operational support, monitoring, and maintenance of the Axonius platform, including adapter health, data freshness, and system performance.

• Work with third parties and client tool owners to ensure the correct data is onboarded, credentialed, and refreshed on the right cadence.

Platform Operations

• Operate and maintain security platforms including vulnerability management, CAASM, and CNAPP tools

• Monitor security findings and support prioritization and remediation workflows

• Assist in platform tuning, configuration optimization, and integration with client environments

• Support onboarding of new assets, applications, and cloud environments into security platforms

Exposure Management Operations

• Review exposure findings and assist with prioritization and remediation tracking

• Help manage remediation workflows with client engineering teams

• Generate operational dashboards and reporting for security leadership

• Assist in maintaining asset inventory coverage and scanning accuracy

Risk-Based Vulnerability Management (Axonius) Configuration

• Configure risk-based vulnerability management (RBVM) in Axonius so that vulnerabilities are prioritized by real-world risk — business impact, exposure, and exploitability — rather than by CVSS score alone.

• Ingest and consolidate vulnerability findings from multiple scanners (e.g., Tenable, Qualys, Rapid7) into Axonius, and configure de-duplication so a single vulnerability reported by different tools is represented once.

• Build and maintain asset criticality ratings and business-context tags in Axonius so prioritization reflects the importance of each asset to the business.

• Configure enrichment of findings with threat intelligence and exploitability signals (e.g., known-exploited, active-in-the-wild) to surface the vulnerabilities attackers are most likely to use.

• Design saved queries and dynamic asset/vulnerability views that isolate high-risk, exposed, mission-critical findings and filter out low-risk noise and items already within SLA.

• Configure risk scoring, severity mapping, and prioritization logic that combine CVSS, exposure (internet-facing vs. isolated), exploit status, asset criticality, and existing mitigating controls.

• Build Axonius Enforcement Center actions to automate remediation workflows — create and route tickets to the correct owner in ServiceNow/Jira, notify teams, and track SLA and patch-window adherence.

• Configure escalation (“fire alarm”) logic and SLA-based rules for critical and zero-day vulnerabilities that require faster-than-standard remediation.

• Build dashboards and reporting that show remediation progress, SLA compliance, risk reduction over time, and coverage — tailored for both operational teams and security leadership.

• Continuously tune prioritization models and reduce alert fatigue so client teams focus effort on the findings that actually reduce risk.

Asset Management (Axonius) Configuration

• Configure Axonius data connections (adapters) across security, IT, cloud, identity, endpoint, and network sources to build a comprehensive, real-time inventory of all assets — devices, users, cloud resources, SaaS, and software.

• Tune the asset correlation and de-duplication engine so records from disparate sources merge into a single trusted asset model the entire team can rely on.

• Configure coverage and gap analysis to automatically surface unmanaged, unknown, or non-compliant assets — e.g., devices missing EDR, endpoints missing an agent, or assets absent from the CMDB.

• Build and maintain asset categorization, tagging, and business-context enrichment (owner, environment, criticality, data sensitivity, location) to power downstream prioritization and ownership.

• Configure asset ownership assignment so every finding maps to an accountable owner, closing the “who owns this?” gap that stalls remediation.

• Establish and maintain data hygiene — adapter scheduling, credential management, field mapping, and data freshness — to keep the inventory accurate and current.

• Configure enforcement actions that keep the inventory and other systems in sync — e.g., push corrected/enriched asset data back into the CMDB, open tickets for coverage gaps, or trigger onboarding of missing agents.

• Build saved queries, dashboards, and reports that give clients continuous visibility into asset inventory, coverage, and policy gaps (comparable to building a unified inventory of tens of thousands of assets).

• Compile and reconcile asset inventories from disparate data sources, applying knowledge of network, cloud, and endpoint technologies commonly used in enterprise environments.

• Partner with SIEM, automation, and security operations teams to leverage Axonius asset data for detections, automation, and exposure analysis.

CNAPP & Cloud Security Support

• Assist with the operation and optimization of CNAPP platforms (e.g., Wiz, Prisma Cloud, Orca)

• Support cloud posture monitoring and exposure analysis

• Assist with investigation of cloud misconfigurations, identity exposures, and attack paths

• Work with senior engineers to onboard new cloud environments

Automation & Integrations

• Develop scripts and automation to improve security workflows

• Build integrations between security tools and ticketing systems

• Automate reporting, vulnerability triage, and remediation tracking

• Use APIs and automation frameworks to reduce manual operational effort

• Use the Axonius Query Language, REST API, and Enforcement Center to automate asset queries, enrichment, ticketing, and remediation actions.

Client Engagement

• Participate in regular operational cadence meetings with clients

• Provide updates on platform findings and remediation progress

• Assist senior engineers in troubleshooting security platform issues

• Contribute to documentation and operational playbooks

Required Experience:

• 3+ years of experience in cybersecurity engineering

• Exposure management or risk-based vulnerability management experience

• Hands-on experience with the Axonius Asset Cloud (or comparable CAASM / asset intelligence platform) — configuring adapters, correlation, queries, and enforcement actions.

• Experience building and maintaining unified asset inventories from disparate security and IT data sources.

• Experience configuring asset criticality, ownership, and business context to drive risk-based prioritization.

• Familiarity with vulnerability management, exposure management, or CNAPP platforms such as Tenable, Qualys, Rapid7, Wiz, Axonius, or similar tools

• Scripting experience (Python, PowerShell, or similar)

• Experience working with APIs or automating workflows

• Understanding of security fundamentals: vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, identity and access control, security monitoring

• Strong communication skills and ability to work with engineering teams

• Embraces emerging technologies, including AI tools, to work smarter, solve problems, and drive better business outcomes.

Preferred Experience:

• Experience with CNAPP platforms such as: Wiz, Prisma Cloud, Orca, Lacework

• Experience with cloud platforms: AWS, Azure, GCP

• Familiarity with container security and Kubernetes

• Experience integrating security tools with ticketing platforms (Jira, ServiceNow)

• Direct engineering experience with Axonius adapters, correlation tuning, and the Enforcement Center.

• Experience with cyber asset management (CAASM), asset discovery, and network enumeration tooling.

• Experience in Linux environments and API-based data retrieval from security/infrastructure tools (EDR, IdP, NGFW, cloud providers).

• Experience using AI-assisted tools (LLMs, copilots, or agent frameworks) to accelerate scripting, analysis, and security operations workflows

Travel Requirements:

• Up to 10% travel

Physical Requirements:

• Sedentary work

• Substantial movement of the wrists, hands, and/or fingers for a minimum of 8 hours a day

• Required to have close visual acuity to view computer terminal and/or extensive reading for a minimum of 8 hours a day

Note: Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa for this role.

We use Greenhouse Software as our applicant tracking system and Zoom Scheduler for HR screen request scheduling. At times, your email may block our communication with you. Please be sure to check your SPAM folder so that you don't miss updates on your application.

Why GuidePoint?

GuidePoint Security is a rapidly growing, profitable, privately-held value added reseller that focuses exclusively on Information Security. Since its inception in 2011, GuidePoint has grown to over 1,300 employees, established strategic partnerships with leading security vendors, and serves as a trusted advisor to more than 6,200 customers.

Firmly-defined core values drive all aspects of the business, which have been paramount to the company’s success and establishment of an enjoyable workplace atmosphere. At GuidePoint, your colleagues are knowledgeable, skilled, and experienced and will seek to collaborate and provide mentorship and guidance at every opportunity.

This is a unique and rare opportunity to grow your career along with one of the fastest growing companies in the nation.

Some added perks….

• Remote workforce primarily (U.S. based only, some travel may be required for certain positions, working on-site may be required for Federal positions)

• Group Medical Insurance options: Zero Deductible PPO Plan (GuidePoint pays 90% of the premium for employees and 70% for family plans (spouse/children/family) or High Deductible Health Plan with HSA (GuidePoint pays 100% of the employees premiums and 75% for family plans (spouse/children/family). If you choose the High Deductible / HSA plan, GPS will contribute in 4 equal quarterly installments: ($850 per EE annually / $1750 per family annually (includes spouse/children/family options)

• Group Dental Insurance: GuidePoint pays 100% of the premium for employees and 75% of family plans

• 12 corporate holidays and a Flexible Time Off (FTO) program

jobs.title: Operations Manager - Roofing
jobs.description:
The Operations Manager is responsible for day-to-day roofing service delivery across the portfolio, keeping roofs, gutters, and building envelopes watertight, safe, and protective of customer property. The role owns leak and repair work from dispatch through closeout, holds contractors to defined service levels, cost controls, and quality standards, and serves as the primary technical authority on roofing repairs, storm response, and escalations.

Key Responsibilities

• Lead day-to-day roofing service delivery across the portfolio, including work order dispatch, prioritization, execution, backlog management, and closeout within established service levels.
• Own recovery of units taken offline for roof leaks, coordinating repair, verification, and return to rentable condition in partnership with field operations.
• Serve as the technical subject matter expert for roofing repairs, validating leak diagnoses, scopes of work, proposals, change orders, and pricing.
• Review and approve roofing quotes, change orders, and invoices within delegated authority while ensuring scope accuracy, cost control, and alignment with pricing standards.
• Own roofing escalations and emergency response, including active leaks, after-hours triage, and urgent concerns from field leaders, AHJs, and company leadership.
• Lead storm and catastrophe response, including post-event roof assessments, damage documentation, contractor mobilization, and proper classification of storm-related work.
• Manage contractor performance across the national vendor network, including response times, leak resolution, quality of work, documentation, safety, and invoicing accuracy.
• Maintain qualified roofing contractor coverage across all markets, including vendor rankings, onboarding of new service providers, and coverage for newly acquired properties.
• Track and report on service performance, including work order aging, repeat leaks, time to stop active leaks, repair spend, and unrentable units, and lead monthly performance reviews with divisional operations leaders.
• Partner with the Leadership to share leak trends, service performance, and field intelligence while retaining ownership of day-to-day service delivery, contractor performance, and escalation management.

• 7+ years of experience in commercial roofing, field operations, or facilities management supporting a national or multi-region portfolio, including time as a service manager or in a similar leadership role.
• Experience leading roofing service technicians or crews, or managing contractor crews across a national footprint.
• Proven ability to manage a high volume of work orders in a fast-paced environment, including surges after storm events.
• Experience managing large-scale roofing projects, such as roof replacements or multi-site repair programs, from scope through completion.
• Hands-on knowledge of commercial roof systems, including TPO, EPDM, modified bitumen, and metal.
• Experience diagnosing leaks and assessing storm damage.
• Ability to review scopes of work, proposals, and change orders for technical accuracy and pricing.
• Strong analytical skills, with the ability to turn work order, spend, and performance data into clear findings, trends, and action plans.
• Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office, including Excel, plus experience with Power BI or similar reporting tools and a CMMS or work order management platform.
• Strong organizational and communication skills, with sound, data-driven decision-making.
• Associate’s degree or equivalent experience in Construction, Engineering, or a related field preferred.
• HAAG certification preferred.
• Willingness to travel as needed, including after storm events, and support after-hours escalations.

Workplace

• One of our values pillars is to work as One Team and we believe that there is no replacement for in-person collaboration but understand the value of some flexibility. Public Storage teammates are expected to work in the office five days each week with the option to take up to three flexible remote days per month.

POSITION TITLE: Semiconductor Manufacturing Technician Instructional Assistant

LOCATION: Phoenix, Arizona

DURATION: Permanent role, 40/hours a week

WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR

Per Scholas is seeking a Semiconductor Manufacturing Instructional Assistant to become a member of our Training Team. The ideal candidate is a detail-oriented, problem-solving individual with strong technical and instructional skills, demonstrates the ability to adapt quickly to a dynamic environment, and maintains a strong sense of accountability.

To succeed in this role, candidates must be business-minded within our mission focus and excel in instructional delivery that meets clients’ and learners’ high expectations.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Support instructor-led training that prepares students for entry-level to mid-level careers in Semiconductor Manufacturing. Responsibilities include daily instruction, assessment administration, attendance, one-on-one tutoring, daily evaluation and monitoring of individual student progress, addressing student violations with students in a consistent manner, and more.

• Assist in evaluating learner performance during hands-on and simulated fab exercises, including zero-energy verifications, cleanroom gowning, manual/automated wafer transfer, and defect inspection under optical microscopy.

• Provide students with access to relevant resources for outside learning on technologies and study aids relevant to the curriculum.

• Work closely with the team to identify student needs, provide the necessary support, establish individualized plans for student achievement, and participate in regular student-status meetings.

• Maintain and update Salesforce and/or our LMS with student grades, certification scores, and progress notes.

• Support and maintain the training curricula, syllabi, lesson plans, and other classroom materials.

• Assist in the evaluation of student troubleshooting performance using scenario-based diagnostics (e.g., P&ID reading, OCAP execution) and structured performance checklists.

• Dedicate capacity (e.g., 10% of non-instructional time) to professional development, technical upskilling, curriculum modernization, and contributing to the product's retrospective/evaluation cycle.

• Work closely with the instructional and curriculum development teams to provide feedback on lab effectiveness, learner pain points, and content clarity.

WHAT YOU’LL BRING TO US

Instructional Skill Sets

• 1-3 years of teaching or training experience.

• Strong technical background; able to grasp and convey highly technical subject matter.

• Ability to respond clearly to live digital conversations via a digital engagement platform such as Zoom or an in-person training environment.

• Strong communication skills.

Required Skill Sets

• Foundational knowledge of semiconductor operations, including cleanroom contamination controls (ISO Class 5/6), wafer processing fundamentals (FEOL/BEOL), and general industrial hazard safety.

• Commitment to ongoing professional development, applicable certifications (such as Lean Six Sigma Yellow Belt or OSHA 10), and coursework to stay current with rapidly evolving technology trends and advancements.

Preferred Skill Sets

• Experience with MES simulators, ADC software, and interpretation of control charts.

• Prior cleanroom working experience.

Professional Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree (or equivalent practical/industry experience)

• Strong technical aptitude (Google Sheets/Excel, Slides/PowerPoint, Salesforce, Slack, Zoom, etc.), project management, and organizational skills with detailed follow-through abilities

• Excellent written communication, presentation, and customer service skills

• Solid understanding of business needs

• Strong evaluation and data management skills

• Prior knowledge or background in semiconductor manufacturing, hardware, or engineering.

Personal Characteristics

• You thrive in a creative, inventive, fast-paced startup environment with people who are passionate about their work and mission.

• You are data-driven, result-oriented, and a forward-looking catalyst for social change.

• You have a collaborative and flexible work style. You’re excited to work cross-functionally with other departments and independently.

• You are a life-long learner.

• You are an effective communicator with strong oral and written skills.

• You are tech-savvy and learn new tools quickly.

• You are detail-oriented, with exceptional organizational management skills.

• You have strong public speaking and interpersonal skills. You are a motivator who is personable, approachable, and socially engaging. You can cultivate relationships and build rapport quickly and authentically with people from various professional and cultural backgrounds.

• You are adept at managing your time and balancing multiple projects and tasks.

• You stand behind our mission, believing that individuals from any community should have access to well-paying career positions and that talent should be recognized and recruited from diverse sources.

Compensation

For this role specifically, we are targeting $60,320.00 as the salary

Benefits & Perks

Per Scholas offers a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your health, financial well-being, and overall quality of life!

Holidays & PTO: Full-Time Per Scholas team members enjoy over 40 days of paid time off each year through a mix of holidays, vacation, and sick/personal time! All employees are eligible for Holiday pay upon hire (a total of 22 holidays annually, including a week off for Independence day and a week before the New Year). Full-Time Benefits Eligible employees also receive 80 Wellness Hours to use for Sick, Safe, or Personal reasons and accrue Vacation at a rate of 8 hours at the beginning of every month, supporting rest, recharge, and work-life balance. Vacation accruals increase with tenure. Part-time employees are afforded time off on a prorated basis and in accordance with local requirements.

Comprehensive Medical Coverage: Benefit eligible employees can choose from multiple medical plans through Cigna or Kaiser Permanente (where available), with options to fit your needs. Eligible employees also have access to a Health Reimbursement Account (HRA) that reimburses eligible out-of-pocket expenses, up to $4,000 for individuals and $8,000 for families.

Dental and Vision Insurance: Eligible employees can select from two dental plan options and a vision plan. Employees who waive medical coverage receive employer paid dental and vision premiums.

Retirement Savings: 401(k) plan with a current 100% employer match on contributions up to 6%, eligible employees are offered entry and full vesting after 90 days with the company.

Employee Assistance Program (EAP): Free, confidential, 24/7 access to counseling, legal support, and financial resources for employees and their household members

Parental Leave: Eligible employees are offered up to 6 weeks of 100% paid parental leave to support employees as they welcome a new child and bond with their family.

Additional Benefits & Perks: Eligible employees have access to employer-paid life and AD&D Insurance, as well as employer-paid short-term disability coverage, with the option to elect additional life coverage and long-term disability insurance. Flexible Spending accounts are available for healthcare, dependent care, and commuting expenses. Per Scholas also offers a range of voluntary benefits, including: Accident, Critical Illness, Hospital Indemnity, Legal Services, and Pet Insurance. Additional resources include healthcare concierge support, financial wellness tools, and employee discount programs.

jobs.title: Clinical Services Responder
jobs.description:
Career Opportunity: Clinical Services Responder in the Tri-State of Kentucky and Surrounding Regions

Are you looking for an opportunity to make a meaningful, life-changing impact through organ donation? In this role, you will use your clinical expertise to evaluate potential donors, coordinate critical care and support, guide hospital professionals through time-sensitive decisions, and help maximize opportunities for successful donation. This position is ideal for a compassionate, detail-oriented healthcare professional who thrives in fast-paced, sensitive, and highly collaborative environments.

As a Clinical Services Responder, you will respond to referred potential organ donors, review medical records and clinical information, determine donation suitability under organizational and regulatory guidelines, and provide timely information to donor-hospital professionals. You will also document required donor information, assess family and hospital support needs, identify the legal next-of-kin, and assist with specimen collection and labeling requirements. This position reports to the Manager of Recovery Services and works across hospital clinical settings.

We are committed to supporting the professional growth and development of our team members, with opportunities to expand skills, take on additional responsibilities, and advance within the organization. In this role, you will be expected to consistently perform your work safely, ethically, and in accordance with organizational policies, professional standards, and applicable laws and regulations. Your commitment to safety, integrity, and compassionate care will be essential to supporting donors, their families, healthcare partners, and our mission.

Responsibilities:

• Respond to potential organ donor referrals and evaluate clinical suitability using Life Connection of Ohio, CMS, OPTN/UNOS, AOPO, and CDC guidelines.

• Identify clinical triggers that support timely hospital referrals of potential donors.

• Review medical records, including present and past medical history, malignancies, surgeries, treatments, laboratory results, diagnostics, and procedural records.

• Recognize organ-specific behavioral risk factors and understand legal and hospital requirements for death declaration and organ donation.

• Assess family dynamics, available hospital support, and cultural, religious, emotional, and informational needs.

• Identify the patient’s legal next-of-kin in accordance with state law and the Uniform Anatomical Gift Act.

• Support required blood, culture, and tissue-typing specimen collection and labeling procedures.

• Maintain accurate, complete, and confidential donor records in compliance with organizational and regulatory requirements.

• Maintain current knowledge of donation standards and regulatory changes and communicate relevant updates to staff and leadership.

Qualifications:

• High school diploma or GED and healthcare experience required.

• Associate degree in nursing, respiratory care, paramedic medicine, biological sciences, or a related field preferred.

• Relevant credentials may include LPN, STNA, Paramedic, EMT, or Medical Assistant.

• One to two years of hospital experience required.

• BLS, ACLS, and PALS certifications preferred.

• Strong attention to detail, time management, professional communication, and interpersonal skills.

jobs.title: Electrical Design Engineer
jobs.description:
A New Paradigm For Space Operations.

Who We Are:

Space Kinetic is a dual-use space technology startup building a new architecture for space operations, one that brings the advantages of proliferated drone technology (low-cost, operationally flexible, attainable, distributed) to space missions while reducing the ecosystem's reliance on consumable fuel. In a world where many companies are focused on incrementally improving the status quo,  we are focused on creating something entirely different – an architecture underpinned by new first principles to meet the opportunities and challenges of the third space age head-on.  Our goal is to move away from one-to-one space architectures – where each satellite in a constellation has one (or a small # of) primary payloads attached to the bus -- and unlock a ‘one-to-many’ system, where each satellite has a large number of payloads which can be deployed from their host spacecraft at high velocities without firing a thruster.

This is not a role for someone looking for a traditional 40-hour work week. Space Kinetic is building ambitious, first-of-its-kind technology, and that requires urgency, ownership, and a high level of commitment to changing the foundational assumptions for everything we do in space.

What You’ll Do:

As a mid-level Electrical Design Engineer, you will independently design, develop, integrate, and test the electrical systems for Space Kinetics’ core technology. Working alongside a multidisciplinary engineering and manufacturing team, you will help mature electrical architectures, develop circuit designs and PCB assemblies, build and test prototypes, and troubleshoot complex hardware challenges. You will own individual design tasks and lead electrical subsystem development, driving solutions from initial concept through hardware integration and qualification as we advance toward flight readiness.

Job Responsibilities:

Responsibilities will vary based on experience and role level, and will include:

• Independently design, develop, and release electrical hardware for spacecraft, satellite payloads, and space systems.

• Design, develop, and test electrical circuits, PCBs, and prototype hardware specifically for spacecraft, satellite, or payload and space system

• Refine electrical architectures, schematics, and subsystem designs.

• Perform component selection, circuit analysis, and electrical trade studies.

• Support PCB layout, fabrication, assembly, and vendor coordination.

• Develop and integrate motor drives, power electronics, sensors, and embedded control interfaces.

• Integrate electrical systems with mechanical assemblies and vehicle hardware.

• Conduct hardware bring-up, troubleshooting, debugging, and performance testing.

• Develop electrical documentation, including BOMs, wiring diagrams, ICDs, and test procedures.

• Oversee and mentor junior-level design components

• Participate in design reviews and cross-functional engineering activities.

• Support prototype maturation, qualification, and progression toward flight readiness.

What It Takes:

• Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering or a closely related STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematic) field.

• 3–7+ years of experience designing, building, and testing complex electrical hardware.

• Experience with three-phase motor drives, field-oriented control (FOC), and bidirectional power electronics.

• Proficiency in circuit design, schematic capture, PCB development, and component selection.

• Familiarity with Altium, OrCAD, KiCad, MATLAB/Simulink, or similar engineering tools.

• Familiarity with aerospace environmental requirements, including EMI/EMC, thermal, vibration, and shock testing.

• Experience taking electrical systems from concept through prototype development and integration.

• Ability to independently own electrical design tasks and drive technical challenges to resolution.

• Experience with design-for-manufacturing, design-for-test, and engineering documentation.

• Strong cross-functional collaboration and technical communication skills.

• Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. government security clearance.

What We’d Love:

• Master’s Degree in Electrical Engineering or related technical field.

• Experience developing hardware for aerospace, defense, robotics, or other demanding applications.

• Knowledge of embedded systems, microcontrollers, sensors, motor controls, and power electronics.

• Experience with CubeSat, small satellite, or other flight-hardware development.

• Experience with high-voltage or high-current systems.

• Familiarity with environmental qualification and functional testing.

• Experience coordinating with external PCB fabrication and assembly vendors.

• Ability to thrive in a fast-paced startup environment with evolving technical requirements.

Our vision is unique, and so is the team we’re building. So, if your background doesn’t fully meet these qualifications, we still want your application.

Where You’ll Be:

• The position is onsite at our headquarters in El Segundo, CA. Domestic travel may be required (up to ~10% of the year).

What We Offer:

• Equity-Based Compensation

• 401(k) retirement plan with a 3.5% company match

• Highly Competitive PTO

• Paid company holidays + winter break

• Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance

• Unique Performance-based bonus opportunities

ITAR Requirements:
To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about ITAR here

In this role, you’ll be joining a team of passionate professionals who are dedicated wholeheartedly to our mission.

You’ll build relationships with clinical partners in your local community and provide much-needed resources to thousands of people struggling with their mental health.
