jobs.title: Director of Special Education Academics
jobs.description:
The KIPP Texas Director of Special Education Academics plays a critical role in advancing the KTX mission by ensuring that students with disabilities receive high-quality, rigorous, and inclusive academic instruction aligned to grade-level standards. This role centers on strengthening instructional design, curriculum implementation, progress monitoring, and academic outcomes for students served through Special Education.

The Director of Special Education Academics is responsible for leading and supporting the academic components of Special Education services across KIPP Texas.  This includes oversight of instructional practices, curriculum alignment, progress monitoring, and academic interventions for students receiving Special Education services.  The Director ensures instructional coherence between general education and Special Education and partners with schools to improve outcomes in literacy, mathematics, and other content areas.

General Role Description

• Strategy | Lead with a strategic vision and courage to ensure that KTX school and regional teams implement the Special Education Strategic Plan and provide comprehensive improvement of school performance using a collaborative approach to clear and specific performance targets aligned to the Special Education Strategic Plan and execute, monitor, edit strategic plans, annual goals and quarterly benchmarking for departmental improvement.

• Team Leadership | Supervise and coach a core team of special education specialists. This position will be responsible for monitoring their performance, conducting evaluations and improvement plans to ensure full compliance with all requirements and deadlines.
• Communication | Ensures KTX special education teams provide excellent communication, customer service and well-coordinated support.

• Legal Framework & Compliance | Maintain strong knowledge of IDEA, Texas Special Education regulations, Section 504, and instructional requirements related to IEP implementation. Ensure instructional practices align with legal requirements and support meaningful access to the general education curriculum.

ROLE RESPONSIBILITIES:

Academic Leadership and Collaboration

• Provide academic leadership for Special Education instructional programs, ensuring alignment to KTX curriculum, assessments, and instructional priorities.
• Partner with Academic Programs leadership to establish goals, analyze data, and drive continuous improvement for students with disabilities.
• Collaborate with campus leaders to address instructional challenges, identify root causes, and implement targeted academic solutions.
• Prepare and present academic updates, trends, and recommendations to KTX leadership and key stakeholders.

Instructional Program Design and Oversight

• Design, refine, and oversee instructional frameworks for Special Education, including inclusive practices, co-teaching, intervention models, and progress monitoring systems.
• Support campuses in aligning IEP academic goals to grade-level standards and KTX curriculum expectations.
• Monitor implementation of IEP instructional components, accommodations, and modifications to ensure fidelity and instructional rigor.
• Analyze student performance data to inform instructional adjustments and targeted supports.

Systems, Data, and Continuous Improvement

• Develop systems to monitor academic outcomes for students with disabilities across schools and regions.
• Support the effective use of progress monitoring tools and data to drive instructional decision-making.
• Partner with MTSS Director to ensure alignment between general education interventions and Special Education services.

Professional Development and Capacity Building

• Design and deliver professional development focused on Special Education academics, including instructional strategies, curriculum access, accommodations, and progress monitoring.
• Build the instructional capacity of campus leaders, teachers, and Special Education staff to support inclusive, high-quality instruction.
• Collaborate with Special Populations leadership to ensure training aligns with legal requirements and KTX instructional priorities.

Compliance Support Related to Instruction

• Support campuses in implementing IEPs with fidelity to instructional requirements and timelines.
• Collaborate with compliance-focused leaders to address instructional components of TEA complaints, corrective actions, and audits.
• Ensure academic practices support compliance while prioritizing student learning and growth.

Community Engagement and Communication

• Partner with families, campus leaders, and regional teams to support understanding of Special Education academic programming.
• Serve as an academic resource for addressing instructional concerns related to students with disabilities.
• Communicate clearly and proactively to ensure alignment, transparency, and trust among stakeholders.

Other Duties:

Perform all other tasks and duties as assigned by the Managing Director of Special Populations

QUALIFICATIONS:

• Master’s Degree Required, Mid Management/Principal Certification Preferred.
• EC-12 Special Education Certification Required and EC-4 or 4-8 Generalist or Content Certification Preferred.
• Minimum 2-3 years of leadership experience as a school administrator and/or systems level leadership with demonstrated results.
• Experience in developing, analyzing and implementing Federal, State and Local Special Education regulations, policies and procedures.

COMPETENCY AND SKILLS:

• Demonstrated proficient knowledge of computer operations such as Microsoft Office, Google Suite, and Outlook email.

Physical Requirements:

• The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
• The person in this position needs to be able to move about inside and outside the school throughout the workday.
• The candidate is expected to attend conferences, meetings and training sessions both virtually and in person within the Region.

Additional Requirements:

• Reliable transportation is needed for travel between campuses
• Ability to maintain emotional control under stress.
• Work with frequent interruptions.

Work Environment:

Hybrid work - This role will spend significant time in KIPP Texas schools with hybrid work options when not in classrooms.

Travel Requirements:

Moderate travel: Regular travel to school sites, regional offices or external locations for professional learning, meetings and other work related activities. Travel frequency may increase based on time of year. Travel time will range between 20% - 60% depending on the candidate’s location.

What We Bring to the Table:

jobs.description:
About Valar Atomics

At Valar Atomics, we're redefining what's possible in energy. Our mission is to make clean, high-temperature nuclear power scalable—unlocking abundant energy for industry, hydrogen, and next-generation manufacturing. We are a team of builders, engineers, and operators who believe nuclear energy should be fast to deploy, factory-made, and built for the real world. Our first pilot plant in Orangeville, Utah will demonstrate how advanced nuclear systems and fuel fabrication can power the future. Joining Valar Atomics means becoming part of a company where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level.

The Team

As part of the Engineering organization, Power Conversion develops the technologies that efficiently transform reactor-generated heat into usable electrical power. The team focuses on maximizing system performance, reliability, and commercial viability.

The Role

Valar Atomics is seeking a Lead, Turbomachinery Analsysis to join the Turbomachinery Team and advance power generation capability. In this role, you’ll be responsible for the analysis behind Valar’s supercritical CO2 power cycle. You’ll lead a team of 4-5 analysts to achieve the performance and reliability targets of the rotating turbomachinery. As an early hire in turbomachinery, you will be able to directly influence design decisions on the system architecture.

Key Responsibilities

• Lead group of 4-5 turbomachinery analysts in the development of Valar’s first supercritical CO2 power cycle

• Own all aspects of achieving cycle performance goals

• Lead team in conducting detailed analysis to inform and validate Valar’s SCO2 turbomachinery design

• Drive the architecture of future SCO2 cycles

Basic Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Mechanical or Aerospace Engineering

• Deep, proven expertise in a core turbomachinery analysis discipline: Aerodynamics, Performance, Operability, Secondary Flow, Rotordynamics, or Structures

• Working knowledge of many turbomachinery analysis disciplines

• Excellent judgement in trading risk for expediency

• Demonstrated success in leading groups of engineers on large technical projects

• 10+ years of experience working on turbomachinery

Preferred Skills and Experience

• Master's degree in Mechanical or Aerospace Engineering

• Experience with turbomachinery mechanical design

• Experience with supercritical C02

What We Offer

• Competitive base salary

• Equity ownership in a rapidly growing advanced energy company

• Comprehensive medical benefits

• Unlimited PTO

• Free daily lunch and dinner provided onsite

• Generous PPE stipend

• High-impact startup environment with significant ownership and autonomy

• Opportunities for rapid career growth and internal advancement

• Direct collaboration with experienced operators, engineers, and industry leaders

• The opportunity to help build and scale transformative energy technology from the ground up

Equal Employment Opportunity Statement

Valar Atomics is an equal opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected status under applicable law.

We are committed to providing a workplace free of discrimination and harassment and will provide reasonable accommodation as required by law.

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States as a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident (green card holder).

Salary

$200,000—$295,000 USD

jobs.description:
About Us

Fanatics is a leading global sports platform redefining how fans connect with the teams, players and moments they love. Our businesses — Fanatics Commerce, Fanatics Collectibles, Fanatics Betting & Gaming, Fanatics Events, Fanatics Advertising, Fanatics Markets and Fanatics Studios — maximize the presence and reach for hundreds of partners globally and create a one-stop experience that allows fans to buy, bet, collect, and earn, while engaging with sports in deeper, more immersive ways. Together, they form a powerful, integrated ecosystem — connected by the Fanatics ONE loyalty program and FanCash, the currency of sport — delivering personalized experiences to over 100 million fans worldwide. Fanatics holds partnerships with over 900 sports properties, from professional leagues and players’ associations to teams, colleges and retail partners; over 7,000 athletes and celebrities; and over 2,000 retail locations, including all Lids stores. Backed by a team of more than 22,000 employees, Fanatics is committed to relentlessly enhancing the fan experience.

About the Team

Launched in 2021, Fanatics Betting and Gaming is the online and retail sports betting subsidiary of Fanatics, a global digital sports platform. The Fanatics Sportsbook is available to 95% of the addressable online sports bettor market in the U.S. Fanatics Casino is currently available online in Michigan, New Jersey, Pennsylvania and West Virginia. Fanatics Betting and Gaming operates twenty-two retail sports betting locations, including the only sportsbook inside an NFL stadium at Northwest Stadium. Fanatics Betting and Gaming is headquartered in New York with offices in Denver, Leeds and Dublin.

Overview

As a Learning Facilitator on FBG's Operations Learning team, you will deliver onboarding for new Customer Experience Agents across our general and specialized support teams, while supporting continued learning as our business grows into new products and markets.Reporting directly to the Sr. Manager of Operations Learning, you will play an integral role within the Learning, Operations and Customer Experience teams.

You will bring to life training programs designed by our Operations Learning Managers, serving as the voice of the classroom and the link between new hires and the team. You will prepare, organize, and deliver new-hire training while giving new team members the time, resources, feedback, and support they need to understand how we work, where they fit within the organization, and how they can grow their careers at FBG.

The ideal candidate is organized, personable, and confident leading a training class while maintaining engagement and adapting to the needs of the group. They are reliable, proactive, receptive to feedback, and comfortable adjusting plans in real time. They can work independently, manage competing priorities, and take strong ownership of their work. Experience in Human Resources, Learning and Development, or Customer Service is preferred.

Responsibilities

• Deliver structured training sessions for new Customer Experience Agents, both in person and virtually, in partnership with Operations Learning Managers.

• Lead training classes while maintaining learner attention, participation, and engagement.

• Manage classroom dynamics and adjust facilitation methods, pacing, or activities in real time based on learner needs and feedback.

• Manage program communications, training schedules, and daily priorities to ensure new hires and key stakeholders have the information they need to be successful.

• Monitor agent performance throughout training and provide timely coaching, learning interventions, and feedback as needed.

• Maintain clear and accurate notes documenting agent performance, strengths, skill level, and development opportunities.

• Communicate agent readiness and areas of opportunity to the Operations Learning team, Customer Experience leaders, and other relevant stakeholders.

• Mentor new agents by answering questions, providing feedback, and reverse shadowing them during practical training activities.

• Confidently facilitate virtual training through Zoom, including creating and managing breakout rooms, sharing screens, troubleshooting common issues, removing participants when necessary, promoting participants to host or co-host, and teaching learners how to use meeting features such as raising their hand.

• Partner with Operations Learning Managers and other stakeholders to ensure training content remains accurate, relevant, and engaging.

• Support Operations Learning Managers with training builds, content updates, and program data gathering as needed.

• Stay up to date on current casework, case navigation, and case management by working closely with agents on the production floor.

• While not facilitating onboarding sessions, partner with other key Operations leaders to identify areas of training and upskilling needs, build training, and deliver said training to the business

• Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

• 3+ years of experience in Human Resources, Learning and Development, Customer Service, or a related field.

• A Bachelor’s Degree in a related field is considered an asset but is not required.

• Ability to obtain and maintain gaming licensure in all jurisdictions where FBG operates or plans to operate, which may include background checks, fingerprinting, and periodic renewals

• Excellent presentation, facilitation, and communication skills, with experience in public speaking, classroom leadership, or delivering training.

• Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to adapt communication style based on the customer, situation, and channel.

• Strong time-management skills, with the ability to manage a training schedule, meet deadlines, and balance multiple priorities effectively.

• Develop and maintain broad knowledge across the Fanatics ecosystem to confidently address a wide range of customer needs and connect experiences across products and services.

• Identify learning trends within each new-hire class, such as recurring questions and knowledge gaps, and flag differences between trained processes and current floor practice to Operations Learning Managers.

• Ability to execute structured training sessions with defined objectives and activities.

• Strong observation and documentation skills, with the ability to assess agent performance, recognize learning patterns across a class, and clearly communicate strengths, skill levels, and development opportunities.

• Experience using Zoom or a similar virtual meeting platform to facilitate training and manage participants.

• Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to collaborate effectively as part of a team and across departments.

• Comfortable receiving feedback, adapting quickly, and changing plans in real time when learner or business needs shift.

• Ability to work independently, take initiative, and follow through with a strong sense of ownership.

• Ability to troubleshoot basic technology issues and partner effectively with IT or other support teams when additional assistance is needed.

• Curiosity and a proactive approach to learning, problem-solving, and building better solutions in support of a world-class customer experience.

• Passion for learning and development, with a desire to continue building facilitation and instructional skills.

• Willingness to travel regularly to events, Fanatics offices, offsites, and team meetings.

• Ability to thrive in an entrepreneurial, high-growth environment where priorities evolve regularly and decisions are made quickly.

• Team-first mentality, with a willingness to do what it takes to get the job done and a desire to continuously improve.

Depending on the role, your interview and onboarding experience may include in-person components, such as onsite interviews or Launching into Better: LIVE—a multi-day cultural immersion in New York City for full-time, non-seasonal hires. These sessions are designed to build connection and bring our culture to life, though specific travel and participation requirements will be confirmed based on your role and location. Your recruiter will provide clear guidance at each stage of the process.

For information about our benefits, please visit https://benefitsatfanatics.com/

jobs.title: Operations Readiness Lead, PV & BESS
jobs.description:
We’re a team of friends bound together by a mission to preserve our planet for future generations through innovative energy solutions and modern infrastructure. Intersect develops, constructs, and operates the most ambitious power and data center infrastructure in the country by co-locating industrial demand with dedicated gas and renewable power generation.
 
Intersect was acquired by Google in March 2026 and operates as an independent subsidiary. We are developing and constructing multiple gigawatts of energy and data center projects in the U.S., enabling more data center and generation capacity to come online faster. We’re on an aggressive growth trajectory and looking for people hungry to tackle the largest energy challenges on the planet.
 
Location & Team Gatherings
Intersect has been a fully flexible workplace since its founding in 2016.  We’ve been very intentional about the way we do things. We are not work-from-home, hybrid, or in-office - we are any and all of those options! Deepening social connections and offering shared experiences is a cornerstone of the way we work. We connect as a team at our Team Week experiences four times a year and at our recently established Hub locations - SF Bay Area, NYC Metro Area, NY; Denver, CO; Austin, TX; Calgary, AB; and Toronto, ON.


Operations Readiness Lead, PV & BESS
 
About this role
As an Operations Readiness Lead, PV & BESS on Intersect's Operations team, you'll ensure our utility-scale solar, battery storage, substation, and transmission facilities are built for safe, reliable, long-term operation well before they leave construction. Bringing an operator's lens to early design and equipment decisions, you will guide projects from engineering review through commissioning and final handover into commercial operations.
 
In close partnership with Engineering, Development, Construction, Asset Management, and external EPCs and OEMs, you will verify testing milestones, close critical deficiencies, and establish operational infrastructure—from EMS/SCADA interfaces to CMMS readiness and safety protocols. Your work directly protects asset performance and builds long-run value across our clean energy fleet. This role is planned to start in December 2026.
 
Team overview
This team plays a critical role in advancing Intersect's mission to accelerate the clean energy transition. The Operations team bridges development, engineering, and construction with long-term asset stewardship to ensure our utility-scale power infrastructure operates safely and at peak reliability. Joining this team means shaping how multi-hundred-megawatt solar and storage projects transition into commercial service, giving you the opportunity to influence fleet-wide standards and grow alongside dedicated industry experts.
 
What you'll do
Influence Early Design and Equipment Selection
Critique PV, BESS, substation, and transmission engineering drawings and specifications early in the lifecycle to embed operability, maintainability, and safety.
Deliver operational feedback on major equipment selections, including modules, trackers, inverters, main power transformers, battery enclosures, PCS, EMS/SCADA, and fire protection systems.
 
Drive Commissioning Verification and Quality Assurance
Partner with E&C, commissioning, and testing teams to monitor construction progress and escalate risks impacting operational readiness.
Witness and evaluate Factory Acceptance Tests (FAT), Site Acceptance Tests (SAT), and commissioning milestones while driving rigorous punch-list and deficiency closure.
Direct and manage comprehensive quality inspections across all solar facility assets.
 
Lead Operations Handover and System Readiness
Define and verify commercial handover deliverables, encompassing O&M procedures, spare parts inventories, specialized tooling, site training, CMMS configuration, and as-built documentation.
Align EMS/SCADA, substation controls, and grid/market interface requirements across Operations and Asset Management.
 
Institutionalize Continuous Improvement Across the Fleet
Capture construction, commissioning, and early-operations lessons learned and codify them into updated technical standards for future clean energy projects.
Manage multiple concurrent project integrations, keeping cross-functional leadership aligned on readiness status, technical risks, and mitigation plans.
 
What you'll bring
Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related engineering field, or equivalent practical experience.
5+ years of hands-on experience with utility-scale solar PV, BESS, substation, and transmission systems across engineering, construction, commissioning, or operations
PMP certification preferred.
Proven track record bridging construction and operations on large-scale power projects, including managing FAT/SAT verification, commissioning documentation, and commercial handover.
Strong working knowledge of PV and BESS electrical architectures, PCS, transformers, EMS/SCADA integration, and CMMS implementation.
Familiarity with applicable electrical and BESS safety codes and standards (such as NEC, IEEE, NERC, NFPA 855, and UL 9540A), including thermal runaway mitigation and fire protection design.
Proficiency in reading and redlining complex electrical and mechanical engineering drawings and technical specifications.
Self-directed, detail-oriented approach with the communication skills to align EPCs, vendors, and internal teams in a fast-paced environment.
Commitment to operational excellence, safety, and collaborative problem-solving, aligned with Intersect's values of Equity, Humility, Authenticity, Long-run Value, and People Come First.

jobs.title: Finance Business Intelligence & Analytics Analyst
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are seeking a hands-on Finance Business Intelligence & Analytics Analyst to join our Strategic Financial Operations and Finance Data Systems team. In this role, you will build and deliver financial reporting and analytics for Finance and Accounting across Oracle Fusion and Databricks. You’ll work from requirements gathering through design, development, and iterative delivery of mission-critical reporting solutions. You will also take on special projects that help Finance and Accounting teams solve operational problems with data. You’ll be instrumental in turning complex financial needs into robust, scalable, and automated reporting that supports Anduril’s rapid growth and strategic decision-making. This role sits between Finance and Accounting and our Analytics Engineering team.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Design, build, and deploy financial reporting solutions within Finance and Accounting, partnering with Finance and Accounting stakeholders from requirements through delivery

• Build complex financial reports and datasets, ensuring data integrity, accuracy, and efficiency, and serve as a reporting subject matter expert for Oracle Fusion ERP, Oracle EPM, Databricks, and other platforms

• Build Finance and Accounting reporting, datasets, and dashboards in Databricks (SQL, AI/BI dashboards), working with Analytics Engineering to define requirements for curated finance and supply chain data models

• Reconcile Databricks reporting to Oracle source data (subledger to GL, report to report) so the data warehouse is trusted as a source of truth

• Support Finance master data management (MDM) processes and structures across core financial systems, partnering with Corporate Technology to keep critical financial dimensions for reporting accurate, consistent, and intact

• Integrate disparate financial data sources into a cohesive, reliable, and auditable Finance and Accounting reporting ecosystem, using curated data in the Databricks lakehouse in partnership with Analytics Engineering

• Deliver special projects that solve operational problems and support Finance and Accounting data transformation

• Proactively identify, champion, and deliver opportunities for process automation and reporting enhancements, and apply engineering best practices (version control, auditability, scalability, comprehensive testing) to all deliverables

• Collaborate with cross-functional teams, such as Corporate Technology, to create reporting solutions that scale with the business

• Serve as a technical reporting resource for Finance and Accounting stakeholders: translate complex financial requirements into technical reporting specifications, and explain technical solutions and their implications in business-friendly terms

• Ensure all financial reporting solutions comply with relevant regulations and internal control frameworks by implementing rigorous validation, reconciliation, and audit trails

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• 5+ years of extensive, hands-on experience owning and leading finance and accounting systems reporting, with a proven track record of personally designing, building, and implementing reporting solutions from concept to production in a high-growth, technically advanced organization

• Ability to own projects end-to-end with minimal oversight

• Strong hands-on proficiency in reporting design and development within Oracle Fusion ERP (BI Publisher, OTBI), including a deep understanding of its data model

• Mastery of SQL, including Oracle SQL and Spark SQL / Databricks SQL, for complex data modeling, advanced querying, data manipulation, and performance optimization across diverse database environments

• Hands-on experience with a cloud data warehouse or lakehouse (Databricks preferred; Snowflake, Oracle, BigQuery, or Redshift acceptable), including querying large datasets and an understanding of dimensional modeling (facts, dimensions, grain)

• Understanding of finance and accounting principles

• Proven experience in Finance Master Data Management (MDM), including data modeling, data governance, and data quality initiatives, particularly within Oracle ERP (Fusion) and Oracle EPM environments

• Exceptional analytical and problem-solving skills, with a proven ability to break highly ambiguous and complex financial challenges into clear, actionable technical reporting solutions and then personally build and implement them

• A strong aptitude for engineering best practices, such as Git-based version control, modular design, automation, testing, and reconciliation discipline

• Outstanding verbal and written communication skills, with a proven ability to gather requirements from diverse stakeholders, present technical solutions, and influence adoption across the organization

• Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Oracle EPM Planning experience

• Palantir Foundry experience

• Python for data manipulation and automation, or for building lightweight applications (e.g., Databricks Apps, Streamlit)

• Workiva experience

• Accounting or finance degree, or a background in cost accounting, GL close, or subledger reconciliation

• Consulting or implementation-partner experience in finance systems or analytics

US Salary Range

$147,000—$196,000 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

• Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

• What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

jobs.title: Account Manager
jobs.description:
About Us

Riskified empowers businesses to unleash ecommerce growth by taking risk off the table. Many of the world’s biggest brands and publicly traded companies selling online rely on Riskified for guaranteed protection against chargebacks, to fight fraud and policy abuse at scale, and to improve customer retention. Developed and managed by the largest team of ecommerce risk analysts, data scientists and researchers, Riskified’s AI-powered fraud and risk intelligence platform analyzes the individual behind each interaction to provide real-time decisions and robust identity-based insights. We thrive in a collaborative work setting, alongside great people, to build and enhance products that matter. Abundant opportunities to create and contribute provide us with a sense of purpose that extends beyond ourselves, leaving a lasting impact. These sentiments capture why we choose Riskified every day.

About the Role

At Riskified, we succeed when our merchants succeed. As such, you'll be the merchant’s representative within Riskified, helping them to maximize the value they receive from our service. You will be expected to manage and prioritize their needs to ensure they're happy and profitable. Your clients will include Fortune 500 companies, big-box retailers, startups, travel merchants, and more. You'll collaborate daily with various Riskified teams, including Product, Analytics, Data Science and Development.

What you'll be doing

• Own a portfolio of merchants as their primary point of contact, from onboarding through renewal and expansion

• Monitor portfolio health at scale (approval rates, chargeback rates, SLA performance and order volume) using dashboards and AI tools, and act on risks and opportunities before merchants raise them

• Build and run AI-powered workflows for account research, business review prep, follow-ups and routine merchant questions, then share what works so the whole team benefits

• Design repeatable, one-to-many programs, such as automated health check-ins, templated business reviews, webinars and lifecycle campaigns, so every merchant gets consistent value

• Decide which tasks should be automated and which deserve a person's time, and go deeper with the merchants who have the most growth potential or risk

• Use usage and performance data to prioritize your book, and identify and lead upsell and cross-sell opportunities

• Onboard new merchants quickly through a standardized, scalable process

• Work with Product, Analytics, Data Science and Development to turn patterns across your portfolio into product feedback and process improvements

Qualifications

• 2–4+ years of experience in a client-facing role such as account management or customer success, ideally managing a large portfolio of mid-market or SMB customers

• Hands-on experience building automations (CRM workflows, no-code tools, scripts or AI agents); SQL is a plus

This is an incentive-based role and a significant portion of compensation is based on performance against objectives. The OTE range for this position is $187,000- 204,000. This range is applicable to candidates who will perform the job either wholly, or in part, within New York City. Actual salary will be based on qualifications, competencies, and location. If you feel this range is not attractive, we encourage you to let us know through the application process.

Base salary is just one part of the pay package at Riskified. All full-time regular employees receive a bonus target and are eligible to receive stock-based awards. Also, our value proposition goes way beyond compensation: our perks and benefits package, culture, community, and learning and development programs are just some of the elements we provide to bring value to our employees. We invite you to apply at www.riskified.com to learn more about what we have to offer.

Life at Riskified

We are a fast-growing and dynamic tech company with 750+ team members globally. We value collaboration and innovative thinking. We’re looking for bright, driven, and passionate people to grow with us.

Some of our NYC Benefits & Perks:

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Validation Engineering
jobs.description:
Forge Your Future with Us:

At Forge Biologics, we believe in turning bold ideas into life-changing realities. Our mission is simple yet powerful: to enable access to life-changing gene therapies and help bring them from ideas into reality. We partner with scientists, physicians, biotech and pharma innovators, and patient communities — all united by one goal: improving lives. If you’re driven by purpose and excited to make a tangible impact, this is where your journey begins.

Our team works out of The Hearth, a state-of-the-art, 200,000-square-foot cGMP facility in Columbus, Ohio. Here, you won’t just watch innovation happen — you’ll be part of it. Whether you’re scaling AAV manufacturing, collaborating on cutting-edge therapies, or supporting complex technical projects, you’ll play a key role in bringing hope to patients with genetic diseases.

What sets Forge apart is our culture of H.O.P.E. We are hardworking, showing up each day with determination and grit. We are open, creating a space where ideas flow freely, and every voice is valued. We are purpose-driven, with every task directly tied to changing lives. And we are engaged, energized by the challenges we face and the milestones we achieve together.

At Forge, your growth matters. We’re committed to helping you expand your skills, take on new challenges, and develop your career through mentorship, hands-on learning, and opportunities for advancement. Our people are our greatest investment, and we’re proud to see team members grow with us.

If you’re ready to use your talent to help deliver hope to patients around the world, join us — and be part of something bigger than yourself.

About The Role:

Forge Biologics is seeking a Senior Manager, Validation to provide functional leadership for site Commissioning, Qualification, and Validation (CQV) programs. This role is accountable for translating site and business priorities into science and risk-based validation strategies, directing execution across GMP systems and processes, and advancing the effectiveness and maturity of the validation function. The Senior Manager will exercise independent judgment in establishing priorities, allocating resources, resolving complex technical challenges, and aligning cross-functional stakeholders while ensuring that systems and processes remain fit for intended use and compliant throughout their lifecycle. The position combines strategic program leadership, people development, and targeted hands-on technical contribution when business needs require.

Responsibilities:

• Own the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of the site Validation Master Plan (VMP), establishing priorities, lifecycle expectations, and program standards aligned with site strategy and regulatory requirements.

• Lead the site Commissioning, Qualification, and Validation (CQV) program for GMP equipment, facilities, utilities, systems, and applicable manufacturing processes, providing oversight of execution, technical quality, and delivery.

• Provide functional oversight for validation of GMP processes, including Aseptic Process Simulation (APS), Process Performance Qualification (PPQ), Cleaning, Sterilization/Decontamination, Filter Validation, Mixing, and Shipping, as applicable.

• Establish and direct science- and risk-based validation approaches, ensuring qualification and validation scope, critical controls, acceptance criteria, and continued verification are appropriate throughout the lifecycle.

• Set functional priorities and independently allocate validation personnel and contractor resources across competing operational and project demands; evaluate capacity, tradeoffs, and delivery commitments with business and project owners.

• Lead validation planning for complex or high-impact projects, partnering with Project Management, Operations, Quality/Regulatory, Development, and technical functions to align scope, schedules, resources, dependencies, and risk mitigation.

• Exercise delegated technical approval authority for validation lifecycle deliverables, including impact and risk assessments, user requirements, design qualification, protocols, reports, and related project documentation.

• Provide direction and technical escalation support for complex validation issues, deviations, and changes; make timely, risk-based decisions and escalate matters with material compliance, safety, or business implications.

• Own the assessment of changes affecting the validated state of GMP systems and processes and ensure appropriate ongoing lifecycle controls, requalification, and revalidation strategies.

• Drive validation process improvements, standardization, and scalable ways of working, including updates to site policies, procedures, templates, and digital validation practices.

• Define, monitor, and use meaningful program metrics to assess compliance, execution quality, schedule performance, capacity, and opportunities for continuous improvement; communicate trends and corrective priorities to senior leadership.

• Lead, coach, and develop validation team members through clear performance expectations, regular feedback, technical mentorship, development planning, and succession/capability building.

• Provide oversight of assigned CQV quality events, including deviations, change controls, corrective and preventive actions, and continuous improvement activities, ensuring effective and timely resolution.

• Champion data integrity, applicable company procedures, and electronic records/electronic signatures controls, including 21 CFR Part 11 requirements, in validation planning and execution.

• Serve as a senior validation subject matter expert and functional representative in internal and external audits, client interactions, and regulatory inspections; lead preparation and response for validation-related matters.

• Advise senior leadership on validation risks, capacity constraints, capability gaps, and investment or improvement needs, recommending practical solutions aligned with business priorities.

• Perform or directly support critical verification testing, technical assessments, and validation documentation selectively when project complexity, escalations, or business-critical demand warrants hands-on involvement.

Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Biology, Life Sciences, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent professional experience.

• 10+ years of progressive experience in validation, CQV, or a related technical function within an FDA-regulated pharmaceutical or biotechnology environment.

• Demonstrated experience managing technical personnel and leading complex validation programs or multiple concurrent GMP projects.

• Proven ability to establish functional priorities, allocate resources, exercise technical judgment, and drive results across competing business needs.

• Advanced knowledge of GMP manufacturing systems, processes, validation lifecycle management, and science- and risk-based qualification principles.

• Strong knowledge of applicable regulatory requirements and industry guidance, including FDA cGMP, EU GMP Annex 1 and Annex 15, ISPE, ICH, PDA, and relevant ISO standards.

• Experience applying cGMP requirements in clinical and commercial manufacturing environments, including aseptic processing, contamination control, and cleanroom operations.

• Experience overseeing validation-related deviations, change controls, investigations, and remediation or continuous improvement activities.

• Experience with quality management systems, electronic validation documentation, and applicable data integrity requirements.

• Demonstrated effectiveness influencing cross-functional leaders, resolving complex technical or delivery issues, and communicating recommendations to senior management.

• Strong people leadership, coaching, analytical, and problem-solving skills, with accountability for team performance and development.

Preferred Skills:

• Broad validation leadership experience spanning GMP equipment, facilities, utilities, and manufacturing processes.

• Experience developing or maturing a site Validation Master Plan, program governance, or scalable CQV standards.

• Experience applying cGMP principles in preclinical and early-phase clinical manufacturing.

• Cell and gene therapy industry experience.

• Experience in small to mid-sized biotechnology organizations with evolving programs and competing priorities.

• Experience supporting domestic and international regulatory inspections and client audits.

• Experience with digital validation management systems and implementing process improvements.

• Experience developing and implementing Contamination Control Strategies (CCS).

This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change, or new ones may be assigned.

Work Environment and Physical Demands

This position works in both a laboratory environment and typical office environment where the physical work demands will vary depending on the specific tasks and duties required of the job. The employee will be stationary (standing/sitting) for extended periods of time. Employees regularly wear personal protective equipment based on the task being performed. Must be able to work in a confined space, such as a clean room or laboratory environment. Ability to identify small details within the field of vision, distinguish between different colors, and accurately identify objects within a specific area.

Forge Biologics is an equal opportunity employer dedicated to building an inclusive and diverse workforce. Forge Biologics, provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.

We’ve Got You Covered:

At Forge Biologics, we believe our people deserve to be taken care of – in and out of the workplace. We’ve built a comprehensive compensation and benefits package designed to help you thrive, grow, and feel valued every step of the way:

Health from day one

• Health, dental and vision insurance start your first day – with 90% of premiums covered for you and your family.

Time to recharge

• A competitive paid time off plan – because rest fuels innovation.

• 12 weeks of fully paid parental leave so you can focus on family when it matters most.

Rewarding your impact

• Annual bonus opportunities for all full-time team members.

• 401(k) with company match to help you plan for the future.

• Special employee discounts, including childcare and dependent care savings.

Your wellness, supported

• Employer-paid short and long-term disability coverage to protect your peace of mind.

Fuel for your workday

Grow with us

• Ongoing professional development resources, training, and mentorship programs to help you build your care and grow within Forge.

jobs.title: DFT Engineer (Contractor)
jobs.description:
Tenstorrent is leading the industry on cutting-edge AI technology, revolutionizing performance expectations, ease of use, and cost efficiency. With AI redefining the computing paradigm, solutions must evolve to unify innovations in software models, compilers, platforms, networking, and semiconductors. Our diverse team of technologists have developed a high performance RISC-V CPU from scratch, and share a passion for AI and a deep desire to build the best AI platform possible. We value collaboration, curiosity, and a commitment to solving hard problems. We are growing our team and looking for contributors of all seniorities.

Tenstorrent is looking for a person ready to take up the challenge of working in a high-profile project where we design and integrate multiple chiplets into a System-in-package, in collaboration with external stakeholders. You will work with Tenstorrent worldwide experts and leaders in the USA, Japan and other countries, and help us make our IP even better. In this role, you will be responsible for DFT implementation using industry standard tools for high-speed CPU core design.

This role is remote based out of the United States.

We welcome candidates at various experience levels for this role. During the interview process, candidates will be assessed for the appropriate level, and offers will align with that level, which may differ from the one in this posting.

Who you are

• You have a Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or Computer Science, along with 10+ years of relevant DFT experience.

• You have hands-on experience with industry-standard DFT tools such as Synopsys and Siemens, as well as scripting in TCL and Python.

• You bring expertise in DFT planning, SoC-level silicon debug, formal verification, and signoff of inserted DFT logic.

• You are a strong cross-functional collaborator who can assess risk, communicate resource needs, and deliver in a complex technical environment.

What we need

• Build and execute chip-level DFT strategies for high-speed CPU core designs and multi-chiplet System-in-Package programs.

• Implement and verify DFT features including scan chains, memory BIST, and JTAG to support manufacturing test and silicon debug.

• Partner with RTL, physical design, and verification teams to ensure testability throughout the design flow.

• Script, automate, and analyze DFT flows using industry-standard EDA tools, including ATPG and fault coverage reporting.

What you will learn

• How to develop DFT strategies for advanced multi-chiplet and System-in-Package designs.

• How Tenstorrent approaches testability, silicon bring-up, and manufacturing readiness for high-performance CPU programs.

• How to work across global teams and external stakeholders on complex silicon development efforts.

• How to scale DFT execution through automation, deeper cross-functional collaboration, and continuous IP improvement.

Compensation for all engineers at Tenstorrent ranges from $100k - $500k including base and variable compensation targets. Experience, skills, education, background and location all impact the actual offer made.

Tenstorrent offers a highly competitive compensation package and benefits, and we are an equal opportunity employer.

This offer of employment is contingent upon the applicant being eligible to access U.S. export-controlled technology.  Due to U.S. export laws, including those codified in the U.S. Export Administration Regulations (EAR), the Company is required to ensure compliance with these laws when transferring technology to nationals of certain countries (such as EAR Country Groups D:1, E1, and E2).   These requirements apply to persons located in the U.S. and all countries outside the U.S.  As the position offered will have direct and/or indirect access to information, systems, or technologies subject to these laws, the offer may be contingent upon your citizenship/permanent residency status or ability to obtain prior license approval from the U.S. Commerce Department or applicable federal agency.  If employment is not possible due to U.S. export laws, any offer of employment will be rescinded.

jobs.title: People Operations & Workplace Specialist
jobs.description:
ABOUT 9AMHEALTH

9amHealth is an AI-enabled virtual specialty care platform focused on managing high-cost chronic conditions at scale. The company partners with employers, health plans, and pharmacy benefit managers to deliver comprehensive, cost-effective medical care for individuals living with obesity, diabetes, hypertension, and dyslipidemia. Members receive access to specialized clinicians, including endocrinologists, obesity medicine specialists, and clinical pharmacists, at-home lab testing, prescription medications, and lifestyle support.

9amHealth was founded in 2021 and is backed by leading healthcare investors like Define Ventures, SemperVirens, 7Wire Ventures, and The Cigna Group Ventures.



What It Is

Our Encinitas office is where our team comes together, and it needs someone to own it. We’re looking for an organized, proactive People Operations & Workplace Specialist who takes pride in running a welcoming, well-run workplace and making sure employees have the support and resources they need to do their best work.

Your first 90 days are about the office: stabilizing it, running it, and building the simple systems that keep it running well. From there, you’ll start supporting new hire orientations and become a trusted first stop for employee questions, so new hires feel welcomed and every employee knows where to go for help. You’ll report to our Senior Manager, People Operations, and work closely with them as we build out the People team’s programs.

This is a hands-on role for someone with strong follow-through who can run programs reliably and improve them over time. Someone who likes to build will thrive here, and as the company grows, so can the scope of this role. You’ll handle routine needs independently and flag significant costs, risks, or decisions that need approval.

This full-time role requires ~3 days onsite each week in Encinitas, including Tuesday–Thursday. The onsite schedule may shift to support visiting teams and office needs. Candidates must live within a reasonable commute of the office.



What You’ll Do

First 90 days: the office

 - Run the office day to day: Keep supplies, shared spaces, workstations, and meeting rooms functional, welcoming, and safe. Be the go-to person for unexpected facilities issues, and escalate significant spend or risk.

 - Own facilities and vendors: Identify maintenance needs, get quotes, and arrange repairs. Manage cleaners, vendors, and the property manager so they have clear direction and deliver what we need. Track issues through resolution.

 - Build the office’s operating system: Create simple, documented processes and schedules for cleaning, supplies, maintenance, and vendor access, with clear owners and escalation paths.

 - Support the onsite experience: Coordinate space, meeting rooms, lunches, and logistics for team gatherings and visiting teams.

 - Support the Co-CEO: Coordinate scheduling, book flights and hotels, and manage travel logistics and calendar updates.

Next: employee support + onboarding

 - Be a trusted first stop: Serve as an initial point of contact for routine employee questions and operational requests, providing timely assistance and directing more complex or sensitive matters to the appropriate People team partner.

 - Help build our employee support system: Partner with the People Operations team to implement and maintain a structured employee support and request process. Bring ideas, adapt as we learn, and own the day-to-day once it’s running: triage requests, follow up, close the loop, and flag recurring issues.

 - Partner on onboarding: Help run new hire orientations and I-9 verification alongside the People team, partner with Talent, IT, and hiring managers as needed, and grow into more of the onboarding workflow over time.

 - Improve as you go: Use our systems and workflows, including Asana, gather new hire feedback, and flag friction points and ideas for improvement.



What You’ll Need

 - Bachelor’s degree preferred, not required

 - 3+ years in a startup or fast-paced environment, with hands-on experience in at least two of these: people operations, onboarding, employee support, or office/workplace operations

 - A strong executor who adapts quickly and brings ideas when helping stand up something new

 - Demonstrated experience independently managing office or workplace operations, including facilities, vendor relationships, supplies, and onsite logistics

 - You’ve built simple, documented processes from scratch and run programs or request queues with consistent follow-through

 - Strong vendor management and practical problem-solving without a detailed playbook

 - Good judgment about what to handle, recommend, or escalate, and discretion with sensitive employee information

 - Detail-oriented with scheduling and travel, and comfortable with shifting priorities and new systems

 - A warm, welcoming presence: you make people feel cared for, especially on their first day, and you want to be onsite and visible for the team

 - Excited to grow in People Ops



Nice to Have

 - Rippling or ticketing tool experience a plus


WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT AT 9AMHEALTH

At 9amHealth, you'll join the exciting environment of a startup with the stability of highly experienced founders that have successfully built a business from scratch. We foster a collaborative learning mindset and a passion for improvement. You'll work with a brand-new product alongside a small, flexible team of people eager to shape technology, infrastructure, and culture.

Our team members are spread across the globe, with physical sites in San Diego, California, and Vienna, Austria, but we value your culture regardless of where you work.

Additionally, we provide a professional development budget and support continuing education, empowering our team to grow alongside the company. Team members have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact on chronic disease management and patient outcomes while contributing to a collaborative, mission driven culture focused on improving healthcare accessibility and affordability.

Full-Time/W2 Positions Only: We offer a comprehensive benefits package, including health, dental, and vision insurance, along with flexible PTO and work from home options. 



OUR COMMITMENT TO DIVERSITY AND INCLUSION

Diabetes disproportionately impacts BIPOC (black, indigenous, and people of color) https://9am.health/en/journal/how-diabetes-affects-bipoc-communities communities. We are committed to creating a workforce that reflects our patients and creating a positive healthcare experience for them. We welcome applications from people of color, LGBTQ+ individuals, people with disabilities, members of ethnic minorities, and foreign born residents.

jobs.title: Photonics Test and Characterization Engineer
jobs.description:
PsiQuantum's mission is to build the first useful quantum computers: machines capable of delivering the breakthroughs the field has long promised. Since our founding in 2016, our singular focus has been to build and deploy million-qubit, fault-tolerant quantum systems.

Quantum computers harness the laws of quantum mechanics to solve problems that even the most advanced supercomputers or AI systems will never reach. Their impact will span energy, pharmaceuticals, finance, agriculture, transportation, materials, and other foundational industries.

Our architecture and approach is based on silicon photonics. By leveraging the advanced semiconductor manufacturing industry, including partners like GlobalFoundries, we use the same high-volume processes that already produce billions of chips for telecom and consumer electronics. Photonics offers natural advantages for scale: photons don't feel heat, are immune to electromagnetic interference, and integrate with existing cryogenic cooling and standard fiber-optic infrastructure.

That approach has since been tested at the highest level of scrutiny the U.S. government applies to emerging technology, and it has held up. In 2025, PsiQuantum closed a $1 billion funding round that valued the company at $7 billion. In 2026, the U.S. Department of Commerce signed a $100 million Letter of Intent under the CHIPS and Science Act, followed by a $125 million agreement with DARPA under Stage C of its Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, PsiQuantum's most valuable U.S. government agreement to date. This year, we also broke ground on our utility-scale quantum computer in Brisbane, Australia, and continued building out our Chicago site. Victor Peng, our CEO, and co-founder Jeremy O'Brien, now Executive Chairman, lead a team and board that reflects how seriously the world is taking this build, joined this year by Intel's Lip-Bu Tan and Atomico's Niklas Zennström.

PsiQuantum also develops the algorithms and software needed to make these systems commercially valuable. Our application, software, and industry teams work directly with leading Fortune 500 companies, including Airbus, Lockheed Martin, Mercedes-Benz, Boehringer Ingelheim, and Mitsubishi Chemical, to prepare quantum solutions for real-world impact.

Quantum computing is not an extension of classical computing. It represents a fundamental shift, and a path to mastering challenges that cannot be solved any other way. The potential is enormous, and we now have the funding, the government validation, and the sites under construction to make it real.

Job Summary:

We are seeking a Photonics Test and Characterization Engineer to characterize and validate optical switching circuits and subsystems. You will build automated experiments, evaluate photonic performance, and investigate issues that inform improvements to our devices, assemblies, and control algorithms.

This hands-on role is suited to a recent PhD graduate with a strong experimental background in optics or photonics. You will work closely with the photonics team to turn measurements into a clear understanding of subsystem behavior.

Responsibilities:

• Design, execute and automate experiments to measure insertion loss, crosstalk, optical return loss, switching repeatability, and other relevant photonic metrics.

• Characterize performance across operating conditions, including wavelength, polarization, and temperature where applicable.

• Build, troubleshoot, and automate optical test setups using Python for instrument control, data acquisition, and analysis.

• Work closely with firmware teams to develop and validate switching, calibration, and control algorithms in the lab. Provide software scripts and code prototypes for firmware implementation, then perform functional, regression, and stress testing to verify the implemented behavior.

• Develop diagnostic experiments to investigate unexpected behavior, distinguish measurement artifacts from device effects, and support root-cause analysis.

• Support screening and validation of new subassemblies and design revisions.

• Document test methods and results, and communicate findings to photonics, controls, and hardware engineers.

Experience/Qualifications:

• PhD in Photonics, Optics, Physics, Electrical Engineering, or a related field. Prior industry experience is desirable but not required.

• Hands-on experience building and troubleshooting optical experiments.

• Strong understanding of optical measurement principles, calibration, repeatability, and data analysis.

• Proficiency in Python, with experience automating experimental setups.

• Ability to design thoughtful experiments and communicate technical findings clearly.

Preferred qualifications

• Familiarity with photonic integrated circuits, Mach–Zehnder interferometers, phase shifters, or optical modulators.

• Experience with fiber-based measurements, optical switching, polarization control, or packaged photonic devices.

jobs.title: Facilities Manager
jobs.description:
Spacecraft represent the most pressing unmet need across the entire aerospace industry. As more launch vehicles come online and the cost to orbit decreases, more companies launching payloads to space continue to emerge.

For the first time in history, this influx of payload companies combined with reduced launch costs has resulted in a massive increase in need for commercial spacecraft platforms, known as satellite buses. These buses hold the payloads of our customers and are flown on launch vehicles.

Apex manufactures these satellite buses at scale using a combination of software, vertical integration, and hardware that is designed for manufacturing. Our spacecraft enable the future of society: ranging from earth observation to communications and more.

We’d love for you to join us on our mission of providing humankind access to the galaxy beyond our planet. 




ABOUT THE ROLE

As Apex continues to expand its satellite manufacturing footprint, we are seeking a Facilities Manager to lead the day-to-day operations, maintenance programs, vendors, and team that keep our engineering, laboratory, and manufacturing environments safe, compliant, and efficient. This role owns the facilities team and programs, enabling Facilities leadership to focus on strategy, capital planning, and risk management.

The ideal candidate is a hybrid leader who thrives in fast-paced, high-growth manufacturing environments, able to build and run programs and a team while staying close enough to the work to step in when it matters.




RESPONSIBILITIES:

Team Leadership & People Management (Approximately 20%)

 - Hire, develop, schedule, and manage the facilities team (Leads, Technicians, Associates / Specialists, and in-house janitorial).

 - Set priorities, assign work, and hold the team and vendors accountable to quality, safety, and timeliness standards.

 - Coach and develop staff; conduct performance reviews and manage performance issues through to resolution.

 - Build cross-training and coverage plans so critical functions are sustained across shifts and sites.

 - Foster a culture of safety, service, and continuous improvement.



Facilities Operations & Maintenance Programs (Approximately 25%)

 - Own preventive, predictive, and corrective maintenance programs for HVAC, electrical, plumbing, fire/life safety, compressed air, and building systems.

 - Ensure rapid response and resolution for facilities issues impacting production, safety, or employee experience.

 - Maintain critical spares and consumables to address common and anticipated needs and minimize downtime.

 - Direct maintenance of light-industrial, lab, and production-support equipment in coordination with Manufacturing and Engineering.

 - Step in hands-on to troubleshoot or execute during escalations, emergencies, or peak demand.



Vendor, Contract & Budget Management (Approximately 20%)

 - Manage on-site vendors and service providers (janitorial, security, HVAC, fire safety, waste, landscaping, utilities, etc.).

 - Track vendor performance against SLAs; drive service quality, cost control, and accountability.

 - Lead contract renewals, RFPs, and vendor onboarding; negotiate scope and pricing in coordination with leadership.

 - Prepare and manage the facilities operating budget and forecasts; monitor expenditures, validate invoices, and maintain financial controls.

 - Identify and drive cost-reduction and value-engineering opportunities across services, repairs, and utilities.



Projects, Build-Outs & Space Planning (Approximately 20%)

 - Lead site-level facilities projects from intake through close-out: scope, budget, schedule, contractor coordination, and documentation.

 - Support build-outs, renovations, equipment installs, and infrastructure upgrades; coordinate with senior leadership on larger capital initiatives.

 - Lead space planning: capacity assessments, layouts, equipment placement, moves, parking, and access control.

 - Coordinate project timing to minimize disruption to manufacturing and site operations; give advance notice and full reporting on impacts.

 - Track project schedules, budgets, and deliverables to ensure on-time, on-budget execution.



Compliance, Safety & Risk (Approximately 10%)

 - Own facilities compliance with building codes, lease requirements, and permitted-use conditions (HVAC servicing, fire inspections, etc.).

 - Partner with EHS to execute OSHA and safety programs: inspections, corrective actions, lock-out/tag-out, and incident follow-up.

 - Maintain readiness for audits, inspections, and insurance requirements through accurate documentation and reporting.

 - Lead facilities response to emergencies, outages, and business-continuity events; maintain and exercise response plans.

 - Maintain HAZMAT, waste, and environmental compliance as applicable to the sites.



Systems, Reporting & Continuous Improvement (Approximately 5%)

 - Maintain facilities documentation, drawings, asset records, logs, and compliance records; keep an accurate site plan.

 - Use a CMMS / IWMS to manage assets, work orders, and preventive-maintenance schedules.

 - Track and report on work orders, costs, uptime, and service performance; use data to inform decisions and priorities.

 - Identify and drive improvements in efficiency, reliability, sustainability, and employee experience across facilities.
   
   


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

 - All applicants must be a U.S. Person due to export control requirements.

 - Bachelor's degree in Facilities Management, Engineering, Construction Management, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.

 - Minimum of 5 years of progressive facilities management experience, preferably in aerospace, defense, manufacturing, or high-tech environments.

 - Demonstrated experience managing people, vendors, budgets, and facilities programs in an industrial or manufacturing setting.

 - Strong working knowledge of building systems (HVAC, electrical, plumbing, fire/life safety) plus building codes, OSHA/EHS requirements, and facilities best practices.

 - Proficiency in Microsoft Office, SharePoint, and CMMS / facilities workflow systems.

 - Proven ability to manage multiple priorities, projects, and stakeholders in a fast-paced environment.

 - Strong organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills.




PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

 - Experience supporting aerospace or regulated / mission-critical manufacturing environments.

 - Experience leading facility build-outs, expansions, or new-site launches.

 - Working knowledge of NFPA, NEC, and applicable building and fire codes.

 - Certified Facility Manager (CFM), FMP, or equivalent credential.

 - Experience managing budgets, forecasts, and vendor contracts with financial controls.

 - Experience generating operational dashboards or reporting metrics.




PHYSICAL & WORK ENVIRONMENT REQUIREMENTS

 - Ability to work across office, laboratory, warehouse, and manufacturing environments.

 - Ability to walk active production floors and navigate construction areas safely.

 - Ability to frequently sit, stand, and walk for extended periods.

 - Ability to bend, stoop, squat, kneel, crawl, twist, and reach, including in confined or restricted spaces.

 - Ability to climb and work safely from ladders, aerial lifts, and rooftops, and at elevated heights.

 - Ability to safely operate hand tools, power tools, and facilities equipment.

 - Ability to lift, carry, push, or pull up to 30 pounds occasionally.

 - Ability to perform repetitive hand and finger movements and use a computer for extended periods for documentation and administrative tasks.

 - Ability to use required PPE in designated production areas.

 - Ability to respond to facilities emergencies outside of normal business hours as needed.



#LI-HC1


WHY JOIN APEX?

Apex believes in creating a work environment that you look forward to embracing every day. Our employees love working at Apex, and we want you to love it too. We're a fast-growing startup that has raised more than $500M in funding, and we invest heavily in our people from day one.




WHAT WE OFFER FOR FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES:

 - Shared upside: Receive equity in Apex, letting you benefit from the work you create

 - Cash bonus eligibility: share in Apex’s success with eligibility for a performance-based cash bonus on top of your salary, rewarding the impact you make

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: 

Compensation ranges are set by role, level, location, and alignment with market data. A candidate's specific level and base pay are determined case by case and may vary with job-related skills, education, experience, technical capabilities, and internal equity. Beyond base salary, full-time hires are also eligible for long-term incentives in the form of stock options, along with medical, dental, and vision coverage and a 401(k) retirement plan.




ITAR REQUIREMENTS

Apex's work is governed by U.S. export control laws, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). To be eligible for this role, applicants must either (1) qualify as a U.S. Person, meaning a U.S. citizen or national, a lawful permanent resident (green card holder), a refugee admitted under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or an individual granted asylum under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or (2) be able to obtain the required export authorizations from the U.S. Department of State, the U.S. Department of Commerce, or another applicable U.S. government agency. Required Qualifications:

• Demonstrated, at least 3 years of hands-on experience repairing and troubleshooting mechanical or electronic weighing systems; this is not an entry-level calibration position.

• Strong mechanical aptitude and the ability to diagnose electrical or electronic issues, read technical instructions, and use common test tools.

• Ability to work independently at industrial and laboratory customer sites, prioritize service tasks, and resolve equipment issues.

• Clear communication skills, professional customer service, and accurate technical documentation.

• Valid driver’s license and ability to travel routinely throughout Northeast Ohio and nearby service areas.

• Ability to lift and transport equipment up to 50 pounds and perform work involving standing, bending, kneeling, or climbing, with or without reasonable accommodation.

Experience That Stands Out:

• Experience troubleshooting load cells, weight indicators, circuit boards, electrical connections, and scale control systems.

• Service experience with a variety of commercial or industrial scale types, including larger-capacity weighing systems.

• Familiarity with calibration and traceability requirements under ISO/IEC 17025 or other documented quality systems.

• Experience with calibration or service management software, including IndySoft; technical training, related certification, or military metrology training.
