jobs.title: Mechanical Engineer - Lethality (Maritime)
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril's Lethality team designs, builds, tests, and delivers the warheads and energetic subsystems that enable our autonomous defense systems to accomplish their missions. Our engineers work across the full hardware development lifecycle, translating mission requirements into mechanical designs, validating performance through testing, and partnering with manufacturing teams to bring those designs into production.

Within Lethality, our maritime engineering team develops warhead systems for platforms operating on and beneath the water. These systems must perform reliably in demanding environments, where pressure, corrosion, shock, and long-term storage introduce complex engineering challenges.

We're a small, growing team where engineers have meaningful ownership of the hardware they design and direct visibility into how it performs. You'll work alongside experienced warhead designers, structural analysts, explosives specialists, and manufacturing partners, solving technical challenges that don't always have established solutions.

Our approach is hands-on and iterative. Engineers don't simply deliver drawings and move on. They work across design, fabrication, and testing, using real hardware performance to guide engineering decisions and continuously improve the product.

ABOUT THE JOB

We're looking for a Mechanical Engineer to develop the mechanical components and subsystems of maritime warheads, from initial requirements and detailed design through fabrication, testing, and production readiness.

You'll take ownership of critical mechanical hardware, applying engineering fundamentals to solve structural, environmental, and manufacturing challenges. You'll create detailed designs, evaluate technical trade-offs, work with manufacturing partners, and use test results to improve hardware performance. Depending on the program and your experience, you may own the design of a complete mechanical subsystem or take responsibility for critical components within a larger warhead development effort, working alongside senior engineers on system-level decisions.

We're interested in engineers who have demonstrated ownership of mechanical hardware and know how to turn engineering concepts into physical, tested products. Experience in aerospace, robotics, automotive, marine systems, research, or other hardware-intensive environments can provide a strong foundation.

You'll have the opportunity to develop specialized expertise in maritime engineering, energetic systems, and warhead development while contributing directly to hardware that moves from engineering design into real-world testing.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Own mechanical hardware design. Develop mechanical components and subsystems from engineering requirements through detailed CAD models, manufacturing drawings, design reviews, and hardware validation.

• Solve complex mechanical engineering challenges. Apply structural analysis, materials engineering, tolerance analysis, and engineering judgment to evaluate design trade-offs and improve performance, reliability, and manufacturability.

• Design for demanding environments. Develop hardware that can withstand maritime operating conditions, including pressure, corrosion, mechanical shock, and long-term storage requirements.

• Turn designs into physical hardware. Work closely with prototype fabrication teams, suppliers, and manufacturing partners to produce, evaluate, and refine mechanical components and assemblies.

• Validate designs through testing. Contribute to test planning, instrumentation, hardware preparation, and data analysis. Use test results to investigate failures, validate performance, and inform subsequent design decisions. Testing may include component, system-level, and underwater explosion (UNDEX) evaluations.

• Develop specialized warhead engineering expertise. Collaborate with experienced warhead designers and energetic materials specialists to understand system architecture, component interfaces, and how mechanical design decisions influence overall performance and safety.

• Partner across engineering disciplines. Work with vehicle integration teams, structural analysts, test engineers, and explosives specialists to translate system requirements into practical mechanical solutions.

• Support manufacturing and production readiness. Collaborate with critical subcontractors and manufacturing partners to resolve technical issues, address nonconformances, and improve the repeatability and quality of manufactured hardware.

• Document and communicate engineering decisions. Develop specifications, drawings, test procedures, assembly instructions, and technical reports that support the design, manufacture, integration, and validation of hardware.

• Participate in technical reviews and customer interactions. Present engineering decisions, explain trade-offs, incorporate feedback, and contribute to technical discussions with internal stakeholders and external partners.

• Support hands-on testing and integration. Participate in hardware assembly, test preparation, and evaluation activities in accordance with established safety procedures and applicable qualifications.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, ocean engineering, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent relevant education and hands-on engineering experience.

• 5+ years of relevant mechanical engineering experience, including direct ownership of at least one mechanical component, assembly, or subsystem through a complete design, build, and test cycle.

• Demonstrated ownership of at least one mechanical component, assembly, or subsystem through a complete design, build, and test cycle, including direct responsibility for engineering decisions and design deliverables.

• Proficiency with 3D CAD software (such as NX, SolidWorks, or equivalent), including experience creating fabrication-ready models and engineering drawings with appropriate geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T).

• Ability to apply mechanical engineering fundamentals, including structural analysis, material selection, failure mechanisms, and tolerance analysis, to evaluate design trade-offs and resolve technical challenges.

• Hands-on experience contributing to at least one hardware test cycle, including test planning, instrumentation or setup, data analysis, and using results to inform design or validation decisions.

• Experience producing engineering documentation, including design specifications, manufacturing drawings, test procedures, or technical reports.

• Demonstrated ability to independently investigate engineering challenges, evaluate solutions, and advance designs with limited direction and technical review at key milestones.

• Experience collaborating across engineering, manufacturing, and test teams to communicate technical decisions, resolve issues, and incorporate constructive feedback.

• Interest in applying mechanical engineering expertise to maritime defense systems, warhead development, and complex hardware challenges.

• Ability to travel up to 25% during periods of increased testing activity.

• Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. government security clearance at the level required for the position.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Experience designing, developing, or testing mechanical hardware for subsea, surface, or other demanding marine environments, including pressure housings, sealing systems, corrosion protection, or shock-resistant structures.

• Experience with warheads, munitions, energetic materials, explosive testing, or underwater explosion (UNDEX) environments. Relevant university research, laboratory projects, and experimental testing experience are valued.

• Experience transitioning mechanical hardware from prototype development into production, including collaborating with manufacturers, suppliers, or subcontractors to improve repeatability and manufacturability.

• Experience performing structural simulations or finite element analysis (FEA) to evaluate mechanical performance and guide design decisions.

• Experience working directly with customers or external technical stakeholders to translate requirements into hardware designs and evaluate engineering trade-offs.

• Familiarity with defense environmental qualification standards, such as MIL-STD-810, or relevant weapons safety and design review processes.

• Experience delivering hardware in rapid development environments, including research laboratories, robotics, motorsport, hardware startups, defense contractors, or multidisciplinary engineering teams.

• Current or previously held U.S. government security clearance.

US Salary Range

$132,000—$222,000 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

• No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

• Please always verify communications: Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address. Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

• Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

• What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.

By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. jobs.title: Hospice STNA Float
jobs.description:
Reports To: Director of Clinical Services

Schedules available: Wednesday - Sunday 9a-6p  OR  Saturday - Wednesday 9a-6p
This position is a full-time floating role covering needs across bedside presence and visit overlaps. Assignment will change daily.

About Luminary Hospice:

At Luminary Hospice, we are a mission-driven organization that empowers our team members to shape our culture in order to allow them to provide the highest quality support to patients and families throughout their entire end-of-life journey.

Our mission is to deliver personalized care that radiates compassion and preserves dignity for all that we are honored to serve on their end-of-life journey. We are centered on caring for the whole person – with expert medical care, pain management as well as emotional and spiritual support along with resources, information, and emotional support for families and caregivers.

About the role:

The hospice aide is a paraprofessional member of the interdisciplinary group who works under the supervision of a registered nurse and performs various services for a patient as necessary to meet the patient's personal needs and to promote comfort. The hospice aide is responsible for observing the patient, reporting these observations, and documenting observations and care performed.

The hospice aide will be assigned in a manner that promotes quality, continuity, and safety of a patient's care.

Job Responsibilities:

1. Performing personal care needs after given a patient's assignment and attending to his/her requests promptly.  If unable to perform a certain task, report to the Case Manager immediately.

2. Providing patient and family with positive communication techniques, within the realm of ethical and respectful care, including confidentiality.

3. Meeting the safety needs of the patient and using equipment safely and properly (foot stools, side rails, O2, etc.)

4. Giving personal care including baths, back rubs, oral hygiene, shampoos, and changing bed linen as often as assigned.

5. Assisting in dressing and undressing patients as assigned.

6. Planning and preparing nutritious meals, including shopping, as assigned.

7. Assisting in feeding the patient as assigned.

8. Taking and recording oral, rectal, and auxiliary temperatures, pulse, respiration, and blood pressure when ordered with appropriate completed/demonstrated skills competency.

9. Providing proper care and observation of the patient's skin to prevent the breakdown of tissue over bony prominence.

10. Assessing and reporting on the patient's condition and significant changes to the Case Manager. Also aware of the caregiver or other individuals living with the patient and interpersonal issues.

11. Assist in ambulation and exercise as instructed by the hospice nurse or therapist.

12. Provide a normal range of motion and transfers/positioning as directed.

13. Assistance with self-administered medications as allowed by state regulations, such as “reminders.”

14. Offering and assisting with bedpans and urinals.  Assisting as assigned with light laundry needs.

15. Performing range of motion and other simple procedures as an extensional therapy service as ordered with appropriate completed/demonstrated skills competency.

16. Providing respite for patient's/family/caregiver when on-site, as appropriate.

17. Keeping the patient's living area clean and orderly, as assigned.

18. Adhering to the organization's documentation and care procedures and standards of personal and professional conduct.

19. Participates in quality assessment performance improvement teams and activities.

20. Respectful of patient and family/caregiver environment and patient's personal needs.

The above statements are only meant to be a representative summary of the major duties and responsibilities performed by incumbents of this job.  The incumbents may be requested to perform job-related tasks other than those stated in this description.

Job Qualifications:

1. Active STNA or CNA (state will dictate) Certification in the state performing job duties.

2. Meets the training requirements of the State.

3. Completed a minimum of 75 hours of classroom and supervised practical training.  Sixteen hours of classroom must be completed before a mandatory 16 hours of practical training.

4. At least 18 years of age.

5. Ability to read and follow written instructions and document care given.

6. Understands hospice philosophy and is comfortable providing specialized care to the terminally ill.

7. Satisfactory references from previous employers.

8. Is self-directing with the ability to work with little direct supervision.  Secure with issues of death/dying. Provides a calm manner when in a patient’s home.

9. Has empathy for the needs of the ill, injured, frail, and the impaired.

10. Possess and maintain current CPR certification.

11. Demonstrates tact, patience, and good personal hygiene.

12. Licensed driver with an automobile that is insured in accordance with organization requirements and is in good working order.

13. Complete a probationary period.  This probationary period is to ensure the aide is competent in the above qualifications and is documented by the supervisor and the employee.

Physical Demands:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to sit or stand. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds.

Equal Employment Opportunity:

Luminary Hospice is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace. We do not discriminate against any applicant or employee based on race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. We are committed to providing a work environment free from discrimination and harassment, where all individuals are treated with respect and dignity. All employment decisions at Luminary Hospice are based on business needs, job requirements, and individual qualifications.

Compensation and Benefits:

Luminary Hospice offers a competitive compensation package, along with a comprehensive benefits package that includes health, dental, and vision insurance, retirement savings options, and more. Our benefits are designed to support your health, well-being, and long-term financial goals.

jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

SR. COMMERCIAL COUNSEL, SUPPLY CHAIN

As a Sr. Commercial Counsel on the SpaceX Legal Team, you will enable SpaceX’s procurement of critical goods and services by providing legal review and solutions-based counseling to Supply Chain, Purchasing, Facilities and other cross-functional partners on complex legal and business issues in the United States and internationally.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Draft, negotiate, and review a range of commercial contracts, including purchase orders/agreements, service agreements, license agreements, long-term supply agreements, non-disclosure agreements, and other agreements related to the acquisition of goods and services

• Identify and mitigate legal risk by implementing appropriate processes, trainings, and controls for the supported SpaceX teams

• Provide legal analyses of applicable laws, regulations, and industry practices, particularly related to the procurement of goods and services

• Work closely with Supply Chain, Purchasing, and Facilities Teams to provide legal counseling throughout all stages of the procurement lifecycle, including RFPs, RFQs, purchase agreements, license agreements and dispute resolution

• Manage SpaceX’s form Purchase Order and Standard Terms and Conditions

• Support continuous improvements of forms, policies, and processes to streamline and simplify procurements, including using AI and other technologies to improve efficiency and efficacy

• Work cross functionally with business teams across the company to analyze legal risks, devise creative solutions, and develop strong, trusted advisor relationships

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• JD or foreign equivalent from an accredited law school

• 8+ years of legal experience

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Experience at a well-regarded law firm

• Experience as an in-house lawyer, ideally within the tech and/or manufacturing sectors and with direct contact with Supply Chain, Purchasing, and Facilities Teams

• Experience providing legal advice related to commercial procurement transactions, including international transactions, and ideally with Fortune 1000 companies

• Experience managing legal issues for a high-growth multinational company

• Experience building and maintaining relationships with clients in various geographies and comfortable advising all levels of management

• Ability to communicate effectively with business stakeholders

• Knowledge of applicable regulatory issues

• Comfortable with and responsive to rapid developments and changes in direction as well as working with technologies and products and in practice areas without significant precedence

• The ideal candidate is diligent and proactive and has demonstrated excellent legal and business judgment, technical acumen, communication skills, and strategic thinking, along with the ability to work independently and cross-functionally

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Must be admitted to the bar, in good standing, in at least one U.S. State

• This position is based in Washington, DC—though other SpaceX offices will be considered—and requires being onsite at a SpaceX office; remote work will not be considered

• Must be able to work extended hours and weekends, as needed

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Pay Range:

Level 3: $235,000.00 - $305,000.00

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. In addition, the Aftercare Coordinator is responsible for assisting the clinical program in meeting standards for Northpoint patients to access Northpoint care continuum.  The Aftercare Coordinator will work under the direction of clinical leadership, counseling staff, and the multidisciplinary team to coordinate care for all patients in our care. The Aftercare Coordinator will complete all documentation associated with these duties in a professional and timely manner.

ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES AND DUTIES INCLUDE:

• Orient patients to the Northpoint care continuum, remaining fully knowledgeable of all Northpoint levels of care, service types, service locations, service times, etc.

• Maintain ongoing staffings and meetings with Northpoint leadership to remain keenly aware of programmatic changes and features

• Facilitate educational sessions to Northpoint patients on the Northpoint continuum of care

• Maintain contact with all discharging Northpoint patients within an alotted amount of time post-discharge to ensure patients have followed up with discharge plans

• Host community events to educate partners on the Northpoint continuum of care, in collaboration with Northpoint Business Development

• Maintain accurate data and reporting regarding patient access within the Northpoint continuum of care and present data succinctly to stakeholders

• Interact routinely with patients, observe behaviors and communicate significant observations to clinical staff

• Maintain ongoing collaboration with the Admissions and Assessment departments to ensure prompt re-admission for patients identified for re-admission through aftercare coordination

• Provide timely and professional updates of progress and admission status to referring entities as directed

• Document information regarding patient care and behavior as required in the policies and procedures

• Utilize de-escalation skills when exposed to volatile patients to maintain personal safety while also ensuring safety for the patients and other individuals on the unit

• Participate in maintenance of a clean, orderly and safe environment, and report needs for repairs and maintenance to appropriate staff

• Assist nursing and counseling staff in responding to emergency situations

• Conduct and assist with activity groups as assigned, and document timlely according to policies and procedures

• Assist patients with scheduling community appointments

• Provide facilitation and co-facilitation of approved group sessions

• Create and assist in updating treatment plans

• Create educational curriculum as directed

• Provide resourcing for crisis intervention (safety plans, contacting support, risk assessments, etc)

• Assist patients in maintaining attendance to the program

Shift: This is a part time weekend role, Saturday and Sunday 4:00pm-12:00am.

About the Team

Since 2017, Avride has been building expertise in autonomous technologies to create solutions that address current needs and anticipate future demands.  We are a U.S.-based autonomous vehicle startup headquartered in Austin, Texas with additional R&D hubs around the world. Our company develops and operates both autonomous cars and delivery robots that share technologies and mutually benefit from each other’s advancements — a unique approach in the industry.

About the Role

Avride is preparing to launch a fleet of autonomous delivery robots at multiple campuses across the U.S. and we are hiring a motivated, entry-level Robot Service Technician Assistant to support this exciting deployment. In this role, you will support the daily operations, maintenance, and preparations of our delivery robots. This part-time and weekend-based role is the perfect starting point for individuals looking to build a career in robotics and electro-mechanical assembly. You will ensure our fleet is ready for deployment while learning foundational skills needed to advance in our rapidly growing industry.

This position is employed through our staffing partner and offers weekly pay.

What You’ll Do

• Prepare robots for the shift: Ensure all hardware and software are ready for daily deployment.

• Put robots/batteries on chargers for the night: Manage power cycles to ensure maximum fleet readiness.

• Clean robots: Maintain physical appearance and protect sensitive external hardware.

• Perform mechanical repairs: Assist with and execute basic repairs on the robot fleet.

• Perform service campaigns: Help implement widespread hardware or software updates across the fleet.

• Assist remote support coordinators: Act as the hands-on field contact for the remote tracking team.

• Perform calibrations and wheel alignment: Ensure sensors and chassis components are properly tuned for safe navigation.

• Keep workshop clean and tidy: Maintain a safe, organized, and efficient workspace for the entire technical team.

What You’ll Need

• Comfortable working in varied field environments.

• Ability to lift and move items over 50 pounds safely.

• Strong attention to detail and a logical approach to problem-solving.

• Team-oriented mindset with strong communication and collaboration skills.

Nice to Have

• General computer literacy.

• Introductory background or interest in electric vehicle (EV) service, automotive repair, or electronics.

jobs.title: Head of Talent
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

Our vision is to become the marketplace for everything expensive, specialized, and difficult to move. We’re building the infrastructure that powers the procurement and disposition of assets across America’s essential industries, automating everything from discovery and payments to freight, warranty, and financing. Today, Garage operates in cities and towns across all 50 states and has surpassed $100M+ in annualized transaction volume on the platform.

Our mission is to save local governments and essential services businesses time and money. We started with fire departments two years ago and have since expanded into EMS and heavy-duty, launching new verticals while growing revenue >10x last year.

If you move fast, hold a high bar, and want meaningful ownership in building a category-defining company, Garage is the place to do it.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As the Head of Talent, you will own and build the recruiting function behind Garage’s next stage of growth. You'll partner closely with the CEO and leadership team to attract exceptional talent across engineering, growth, marketing, operations, and corporate functions, helping us scale rapidly without compromising on our talent bar.

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who is equally excited about closing exceptional candidates as they are about building a world-class recruiting organization. You'll set the talent acquisition strategy, own high-priority searches, build scalable recruiting systems, and ultimately grow and lead the team responsible for bringing Garage's next generation of talent on board.

 - Own Garage's end-to-end talent acquisition strategy, partnering directly with the Chief of Staff and functional leaders on hiring priorities, headcount planning, and execution.

 - Lead full-cycle recruiting for critical and senior-level roles, personally sourcing, assessing, and closing exceptional candidates.

 - Build and lead Garage's internal recruiting function, hiring and developing a high-performing team as the company scales.

 - Design scalable recruiting processes, systems, and infrastructure that enable rapid hiring while maintaining an exceptionally high talent bar.

 - Establish and track recruiting KPIs, leveraging data to improve funnel performance, hiring velocity, candidate quality, and overall recruiting effectiveness.

 - Build Garage's employer brand and create a differentiated candidate experience that attracts the best talent in a competitive market.




WHO YOU ARE

 - Builder mentality. Excited to build a recruiting function from the ground up, with the ability to operate strategically while remaining deeply hands-on.

 - Exceptional talent judgment. Has an instinct for identifying outstanding people and a relentless commitment to raising the talent bar.

 - Strong operator. Highly analytical, organized, and process-oriented, with the ability to translate ambitious hiring goals into clear plans and measurable results.

 - Compelling recruiter and closer. Knows how to engage top talent, build meaningful relationships, and get exceptional candidates excited about joining Garage.

 - High ownership and bias toward action. Thrives in fast-paced, ambiguous environments, moves with urgency, and takes personal accountability for outcomes.

 - Trusted leadership partner. Able to influence executives, challenge assumptions, and provide thoughtful guidance on hiring decisions and organizational growth.




WHAT YOU'LL NEED

 - 8+ years of recruiting experience, including experience owning talent acquisition strategy and leading recruiting teams.

 - Experience building or scaling recruiting at a high-growth, venture-backed startup, ideally through periods of significant headcount expansion.

 - Proven track record of recruiting and closing exceptional talent across multiple functions, including technical and GTM roles.

 - Experience partnering directly with founders and senior executives on hiring strategy, workforce planning, and critical searches.

 - Strong understanding of the NYC talent market, with an established network and experience recruiting for in-office teams.

 - Deep familiarity with modern recruiting tools, sourcing platforms, and applicant tracking systems such as Ashby.



Our Values

 - Take Big Swings. We are here to transform an overlooked industry—not make small improvements around the edges. We set ambitious goals, take calculated risks, and push through setbacks. We never trade lasting impact for short-term comfort.

 - Customers Come First. Our customers operate in an industry burdened by slow, expensive, and outdated processes. We attack the problems that cost them the most and measure our success by the time and money we give back to them.

 - Play For the Front of the Jersey. We put the mission ahead of ourselves. We challenge each other directly, support each other relentlessly, and step up whenever the team needs us. We win together, and we have fun doing it.

 - All Gas, No Ego. Building something that matters takes relentless effort. We move fast, take ownership, and see hard problems through. When we fall short, we own it, learn quickly, and come back stronger.



Why Join Garage?

 - Do work that matters. Our platform helps people buy the assets that local communities rely on to keep their communities safe, clean, and operating every day.

 - Help shape the company. Join as one of our first 50 employees and work directly alongside the founders.

 - Make an outsized impact. You’ll join a talent-dense, high-performance team where every person moves the company forward.

 - Build from a strong foundation. We’ve raised $18M, including a $13.5M Series A, from Y Combinator, Initialized Capital, Infinity Ventures, FJ Labs, and other leading investors.



What we offer

 - Competitive salary and stock options

 - 100% medical, dental and vision insurance coverage

 - Unlimited PTO (in addition to company observed holidays)

 - Daily lunch & dinner (for employees based in NYC)

 - $100/month wellness stipend

 - 401(k) w/ employer match

 - Pre-tax commuter benefits

 - Annual team offsite

 - Relocation assistance
   
   

We realize applying for jobs can feel daunting at times. We don’t expect you to check all the qualification boxes and encourage you to apply if you have experience in some of the areas.

Equal Opportunity

As an equal-opportunity employer, we are committed to building an inclusive environment where you can be you. We work hard to evaluate all employees and job applicants consistently, without regard to race, color, religion, gender, natural origin, age, disability, pregnancy, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected class.

jobs.title: Assistant Teacher (Float) (Part-time): Denton, TX
jobs.description:
As a part-time Assistant Teacher (Float) at Bezos Academy (internally titled Assistant Teacher I), you share our passion for early childhood education and commitment to creating nurturing, high-quality learning environments for all children. While exact responsibilities will vary from school to school, you may assist in classrooms, serve and supervise mealtimes, and support the overall operations of the school. Drawing on your organizational skills, professionalism, and commitment to children, you will support high quality, tuition-free, Montessori-inspired programs that enable every child to thrive in our growing network of preschools in under-resourced communities.

LOCATION

We are actively hiring for a part-time Assistant Teacher (Float) to support our preschool in Denton (1820 Frame Street Denton, TX 76209).

SCHEDULES, BENEFITS, AND COMPENSATION

• School schedules vary depending on community needs but generally range from 8am-5:30pm, with teachers staggered across these hours with varying start and end times. Your specific schedule will be determined with your school leader when considering all staff, classroom, and community needs, but are currently expected to be 1:00pm-5:00pm.

• This role includes paid care (sick) time, accrued based on hours worked, and a 401(k) plan with a 4% employer contribution match.

• The full compensation range for this position is $23-$26 per hour. The starting pay for all new employees is $23 per hour.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

• Age 18 with high school diploma or GED

• Ability to pass background checks, clear tuberculosis screenings, and (upon hire) successfully complete trainings required by the state of Texas to supervise children independently

• Ability to independently supervise, communicate effectively with, and care for young children safely, including ability to lift a minimum of 40 lbs

• Access to reliable transportation to and from work and ability to consistently attend work as scheduled to ensure proper staff-to-child classroom ratios and support smooth school operations

• Must have a valid Food Handler’s Permit or be willing to obtain one upon hire

• Ability to complete 20 hours of onboarding by your seventh day of employment

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Prior experience supporting or teaching children ages 3–5 in a Montessori or early childhood classroom setting

• Experience working effectively across lines of difference and fostering an inclusive, welcoming environment for all children and families

• Strong communication and organizational skills, with the ability to manage daily operational tasks such as classroom setup, safety checks, and basic clerical responsibilities

• Demonstrated reliability and flexibility in supporting school operations, including meal service, playground supervision, assisting with classroom coverage as needed, and lead after-school activities

RESPONSIBILITIES

*NOTE: The combination of responsibilities may vary based on the needs of the school site, students, and prior experiences of the Assistant Teacher.

Instructional

• Serve as a floating assistant teacher, providing support wherever and however the school most needs it each day

• As needed, independently supervise children throughout the day in classrooms and a variety of other situations, including but not limited to arrival/departure, transitions, outside time, rest/nap time, and (if offered) extended hours

• Assist in maintaining accurate child and family records

• Complete Montessori basics training and credentialing/licensing requirements within seven days of hire

Operational

• Support Bezos Academy classrooms by following regulations and guidelines in the day-to-day operation of the classroom and school (e.g. cleaning/preparing materials, meal prep and cleanup, nap time transitions, laundry, bathroom supervision, etc.)

• Support school leadership and teachers to foster a nurturing, safe, and stimulating, non-competitive school environment

• Support children’s increasing independence with daily living skills (i.e., washing hands, using the bathroom, eating meals and snacks, cleaning up, etc.)

• Maintain licensing and credentialing requirements and complete required ongoing professional development trainings in a timely manner

• Attend staff meetings and family events as schedule allows

• Assume postures at low levels (e.g., kneeling, stooping, bending, and sitting on the floor) as needed to communicate effectively with children

• Provide support to nearby Bezos Academy schools, as needed, at the direction of your Head of School or District School Leader

Other

• Attend staff meetings and family events as schedule allows

Bezos Academy is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All applicants receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, protected veteran status, or disability status.

Bezos Academy participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with employee Form I-9 Information to confirm authorization to work in the U.S. Bezos Academy only uses E-Verify once a candidate has accepted a job offer and completed the Form I-9. If E-Verify cannot confirm that an employee is authorized to work, Bezos Academy will give the employee written instructions and an opportunity to contact the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) or Social Security Administration (SSA) so the employee can begin to resolve the issue before any adverse employment action is taken. For more information about your right to work, please see the Notice of Right to Work.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. If you are in need of an accommodation to participate in the application process, please reach out to talent@bezosacademy.org. We will work with you to ensure you have a fair opportunity to apply for our open positions.

If you are a current Bezos Academy employee, please use the internal job board to apply.

jobs.title: Proposal Lead (Specialist III)
jobs.description:
Interested in an opportunity to be part of a dynamic team of proposal managers focused on winning US Federal work around the world? AECOM is hiring an experienced Proposal Lead (Specialist III) to work within our Governments Marketing team.

In this role, you will be responsible for leading key proposals and presentations, providing support and guidance from pre-RFP positioning and capture through to interview stage, as required, and leading proposal teams who support Amtrak and various Federal civilian clients.

The ideal candidate will bring experience with US Federal proposals, and have strong proposal writing and leadership skills, as well as a sharp compliance focus, pre-positioning and capture experience, and creative design ideas.

This will be a hybrid position including a combination of both remote and in-office work schedules, that can be based in, but not limited to: Des Moines, IA.

Job Responsibilities will include, but not be limited to:

General

• As a Proposal Lead and writer, collaborate with business line teams on identified priority pursuits, including pre-positioning, capture, responses to requests for qualifications (RFQ) and requests for proposals (RFP), as well as shortlist interviews.
• Reports to the Federal Civilian Marketing Team Lead within our Governments Marketing group.

Proposal Management and Development

• Lead medium to large, complex pursuits from capture through to interview stage, as required, which may include multiple disciplines/geographies.
• Participate in workshops/sessions to support the capture manager in development of the win strategy.
• Lead and contribute to the writing of proposal sections to include cover letters, executive summaries, past performance sections, management approaches, and resumes/staffing sections.
• Develop and manage annotated outlines, proposal schedules, compliance lists, and content plans, and provide conceptual leadership for document design.
• Participate actively in Go/No-Go, positioning activities, capture strategies and greenlight analyses.
• Drive compliance by providing leadership and direction to proposal teams, as required.
• Use approved AI tools to streamline proposal workflows, including outlines, compliance matrices, and first drafts, while following AECOM data-handling and confidentiality guidelines.
• Facilitate color reviews for assigned pursuits, and apply lessons learned to add value to proposal and win plan.
• May serve as an independent reviewer for priority pursuits led by others.
• Support debriefs and gathering of client feedback on assigned proposals to ensure and demonstrate continuous improvements.
• Manage proposal close-out activities, including maintaining files for all recent Amtrak submittals and project descriptions.
• May lead or participate in special projects involving various business line staff, as directed.

Minimum Requirements

• Bachelor's degree, preferably in Journalism, English, Communications, Marketing or a related field and 4+ years of related proposal experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education.
• 4+ years of Amtrak and/or Federal proposal experience.
• Evidence of successful leadership of multi-disciplinary or multi-geography proposals valued >$10 million.
• Working knowledge of and interest in the A/E industry, including AECOM’s Federal clients, projects, people, credentials, and competitors as well as knowledge of Amtrak, rail, and Federal transportation pursuits.
• A thorough understanding of effective proposal and presentation best practices and tools, including how to convey messages, themes, discriminators, and responses to evaluation criteria clearly and effectively.
• Demonstrated experience applying industry best practices and procedures to support positioning, client or business development processes.
• Strong proposal writing and editing skills, including grammar and style.
• A strong working knowledge of desktop publishing software (e.g., Adobe Creative Suite), graphics programs (e.g., InDesign, Adobe Acrobat, Photoshop), word processing programs (e.g., Microsoft Word), spreadsheet management (Excel), and presentation software (e.g., PowerPoint).
• A working knowledge of collaborative tools such as Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, etc.
• Experience applying AI tools (e.g., Microsoft 365 Copilot) within the proposal workflow, such as drafting and refining content, extracting requirements, checking compliance, and supporting reviews, with sound judgment on accuracy, confidentiality, and appropriate use of client or sensitive information.

jobs.title: Strategic Finance Lead
jobs.description:
👋 WELCOME TO GLIDE!

 

At Glide we’re reimagining the banking experience for the modern world. Our embedded fintech platform empowers legacy financial institutions, like community banks and credit unions, to pioneer novel digital experiences for their customers.

You’ll be joining an all-star team with engineering, product, and growth experience from Stripe, Google, and Amazon. We’re looking for a talented Strategic Finance Lead to build our finance function and help shape our next stage of growth. We’re bringing a new perspective to the decades-old financial world, and we’re hoping you can help us do that!

 


YOUR NORTH STAR

Build the financial backbone of Glide’s next stage of growth. Create an AI-native finance function that anticipates what the business needs, allocates capital against our biggest opportunities, and gives every leader the clarity to act decisively. Make finance a competitive advantage, with intelligent systems running day-to-day operations and your insights shaping where Glide goes next.

 


YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Model Glide’s path to profitable growth. Build the models that guide our biggest investment decisions, stress-test growth and hiring scenarios, and chart a path to durable profitability with a clear view of cash flow, runway, and capital needs.

 - Automate financial data and forecasting. Design the systems and automations that connect our financial data, keep forecasts current, and surface opportunities and risks early. Give leaders timely insight they can act on as the business scales.

 - Build the budget and hiring plan. Own the company-wide budget and hiring plan, partner with leaders to prioritize investments, and direct resources toward the teams and initiatives with the greatest potential impact.

 - Turn board reporting into actionable recommendations. Own our monthly board reporting and financial narrative. Translate performance, variances, and updated forecasts into clear recommendations on where to accelerate, where to adjust, and what comes next.

 - Automate billing from contract to cash. Use AI to orchestrate the journey from signed contract to cash in the bank, automating invoicing, collections, reconciliation, and revenue schedules so revenue can scale with minimal manual intervention.

 - Win strong vendor deals. Negotiate vendor partnerships that improve our economics and preserve flexibility, securing better pricing, commitments, renewal terms, and payment structures as Glide grows.

 - Own revenue recognition and cost allocation. Establish and defend the accounting assumptions behind our performance, including salary allocation to COGS and the timing of revenue and expense recognition, so leaders can confidently act on the numbers.

 - Deliver a fast, accurate monthly close. Partner with our CPA to deliver accurate books, resolve accounting questions, and continuously improve the processes that keep our financial foundation strong.

 


NEED-TO-HAVES:

 - Roughly 5–8 years of experience, with meaningful hands-on finance ownership at a B2B SaaS, fintech infrastructure, or usage-based software startup.

 - Strong expertise with complex billing patterns, including personally owning both billing and financial planning.

 - Experience as a Strategic Finance Manager, Finance Lead, or hands-on second-in-command to a CFO, with ownership of both planning and financial operations. Candidates with Head of Finance experience should be excited to do hands-on individual contributor work.

 - Strong accounting judgment alongside modeling and commercial skills. Consulting, accounting/advisory, Big Four, or investment banking experience should be followed by meaningful hands-on startup finance experience.

 - Experience building processes and working independently in a small team.

 - A track record of sustained ownership and impact in previous roles, with the commitment to build and grow with a company over time.

 - Based in New York City, or willing to relocate, and able to work in person at our office three days per week.

 - Authorized to work in the United States without current or future visa sponsorship. Glide does not provide visa sponsorship for this role.

 


NICE-TO-HAVES:

 - Experience at companies that serve enterprise customers, especially in fintech.

 - Founding or first finance hire experience at a startup.

 - Experience building department-level budgets and P&Ls so each leader can manage resource planning.

 - Ability to prepare monthly books internally over time. Our CPA handles this today.

 


PERKS AND BENEFITS:





💸 COMPETITIVE COMPENSATION:

You’ll receive an annual base salary of $140,000–$180,000 and an equity package of 0.025%–0.075% for joining us at Glide.

 


❤️ WELLBEING CREDITS (FOR US EMPLOYEES)

Besides stellar health, dental, and vision insurance, we offer a generous health and wellness stipend, so you can stay healthy and active.

 


🥗 LUNCH ON US (FOR US EMPLOYEES)

We love food. Every member of the Glide team gets free lunch, every day. No one goes hungry around here :)

 


💻 BEST TOOLS

We want you to be happy at work. You'll get a full equipment upgrade - from a top-of-the-line computer to your preference on keyboard, mouse, and accessories.

jobs.description:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

SPACE SYSTEMS

At Rocket Lab, we’re not just launching rockets — we're building the future of space. Our Space Systems team builds everything from complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space, like solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, radios, and more.

Our Space Systems team has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. The team has built spacecraft, payloads, and components for missions to the Moon and Mars, working with partners including NASA, the Space Development Agency, and the U.S. Space Force. Whether it’s a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or the vertically integrated components that help them get to space — our world class Space Systems team is empowering some of the boldest and most ambitious space missions

TECHNICIAN I-III, OPS SUPPORT - EQUIPMENT MAINTENANCE (EES)

Based at Rocket Lab’s site in Albuquerque, New Mexico the Technician I-III, Ops Support - Equipment Maintenance (EES) is responsible for the maintenance, upkeep and troubleshooting of assigned semiconductor and composites manufacturing equipment to ensure that the equipment is running safely and efficiently to meet production objectives. You will support the Operations Manager and operations organization, with deliverables required for internal leadership, board of directors, and investors.

(Please note: this position can be hired at the Ops. Support Technician I, Ops. Support Technician II, Ops. Support Technician III level)

WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO:

• Service, maintain and troubleshoot equipment and manufacturing tools related to the function and operation of an aerospace composites and semiconductor plant and facility including gasses, chemicals, compressed air, water and waste streams.

• Troubleshoot and repair of manufacturing and support equipment and systems.

• Works with engineers and managers to resolve issues or plan for acquiring/installing new equipment or systems.

• Locate and order parts and materials.

• Assumes leadership role in training and support of new technicians.

• Maintain facility data collection requirements and procedures.

• Identifies nonconformance when they occur and participates in finding the solution to the non-conformance.

• Deploys the Quality Management System as it applies to the scope of work.

• Supports Facilities shut down and projects off shift as scheduled by department management.

• Serve as member of Emergency Response Team.

YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS AS A TECHNICIAN I, OPS. SUPPORT:

• Experience troubleshooting, repairing and performing maintenance on semiconductor and solar photovoltaic manufacturing equipment.

• Experience with installing and relocating semiconductor and manufacturing equipment

• Pneumatic, hydraulic, mechanical and electrical experience

• High school diploma or GED

• Experience using a respirator

YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS AS A TECHNICIAN II, OPS. SUPPORT:

• 2+ years of experience troubleshooting, repairing and performing maintenance on semiconductor and solar photovoltaic manufacturing equipment.

• Experience with installing and relocating semiconductor and manufacturing equipment

• Pneumatic, hydraulic, mechanical and electrical experience

• High school diploma

• Experience using a respirator

YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS AS A TECHNICIAN III, OPS. SUPPORT:

• 5+ years of experience troubleshooting, repairing and performing maintenance on semiconductor and solar photovoltaic manufacturing equipment.

• Experience with installing and relocating semiconductor and manufacturing equipment

• Pneumatic, hydraulic, mechanical and electrical experience

• High school diploma

• Experience using a respirator

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Stand and walk for entire shift (8+ hours) on various work surfaces

• Climb ladders and work at elevated height small spaces, awkward positions, and tight areas as needed

• Perform repetitive motions including bending, twisting, reaching, grasping, pushing, pulling, and stooping

• Use hands with precision to handle, control, and operate tools, instruments, and equipment

• Lift, carry, push, and pull materials and equipment up to 25 lbs.

• Work in varied environments including production floors, equipment areas, and field locations with exposure to noise, temperature variations, and moving machinery

• Flexibility to work extended hours, weekends, and varied shifts as operational needs require

#RL1

WHAT TO EXPECT

We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way.

Important information:

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), Rocket Lab Employees must be a U.S. citizen, lawful U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State and/or the U.S. Department of Commerce, as applicable. Rocket Lab provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. Applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation for the application/interview process for a job in the United States should contact Giulia Johnson at g.biow@rocketlabusa.com.This dedicated resource is intended solely to assist job seekers with disabilities whose disability prevents them from being able to apply/interview. Only messages left for this purpose will be considered. A response to your request may take up to two business days.

FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN NEW ZEALAND OFFICES ONLY:

For security reasons, background checks will be undertaken prior to any employment offers being made to an applicant.  These checks will include nationality checks as it is a requirement of this position that you be eligible to access equipment and data regulated by the United States' International Traffic in Arms Regulations.

jobs.title: Vice President, Technology and Product (Remote)
jobs.description:
Position Overview

We are seeking an experienced VP of Product and Technology to build and launch our next generation of physician engagement products and services. This is a builder role at the intersection of product and engineering. You believe time spent understanding physicians and pharma clients is equally important as the time spent working with engineers. You will develop fresh ideas for how pharma brands can reach physicians and be useful to them, and you will be measured on impact, not output.

Reporting to the Chief Commercial Officer, you will oversee all technology initiatives, manage product and engineering teams, and architect scalable solutions that enhance our ability to deliver timely, relevant experiences to healthcare professionals in the US. You will enable the team to take advantage of the speed and agility of agentic code development to prototype and pivot fast and collaborate with other teams to find optimal solutions through working prototypes, not wireframes and powerpoints.

The ideal candidate is a technologist who has led product, design, and engineering as one integrated team under a single reporting line. You are credible with engineers on architecture, data infrastructure, and AI, and you own the full process from discovery and design through development, release, and iteration. You have built engagement products that people return to by choice: interactive formats, habit loops, community, and personalization. You have taken a product from 0 to 1, and you have set up and run a forward-deployed engineering (FDE) model across a range of business stakeholders.

Product Leadership and Experimentation

• Own the MDLinx product vision and roadmap across physician-facing experiences and pharma engagement products, leading product, design, and engineering as one team.
• Bring new ideas for how pharma brands can reach and help physicians, and for experiences physicians return to by choice.
• Build a culture of rapid experimentation: go from idea to working prototype in days, put it in front of physicians and clients, learn, and redeploy. With AI-native development, building is cheap. The scarce resource is sharp product judgment about what to test next.
• Spend regular time with physicians and pharma clients and let what you learn in the field shape what the team builds next.
• Run a forward-deployed engineering (FDE) model in which engineers work directly with internal business stakeholders and clients. Client engagements become live prototypes, and what proves valuable becomes a platform capability.
• Scale what works, retire what doesn’t, and quickly move people and code to the next bet.

Engineering Leadership

• Lead application development and data engineering, directly and through team leads.
• Keep teams small, fast, and focused on outcomes. Buy or reuse wherever something isn’t a differentiator.
• Make AI-native development the default way the team works. Ship AI capabilities (personalization, recommendation, content intelligence) as core parts of the product.
• Build a platform designed for speed, so teams can launch, test, and roll back experiments without destabilizing core products.
• Run MDLinx product and technology with a high degree of autonomy, within M3 USA engineering standards and in line with the M3 USA technology plan.

Engagement and Data

• Instrument every experience to generate signal, giving us a continuous read on physician knowledge, attitudes, and behavior.
• Own the MDLinx first-party data strategy with the data engineering team, serving both product and commercial needs.

AI and Content Intelligence

• Lead generative AI for content creation, summarization, curation, and medical literature analysis.
• Build recommendation and real-time personalization engines, plus predictive models for content affinity and engagement propensity.

Platform, Data, and Architecture

• Own technical direction and architecture, using a modular, composable platform built for rapid deployment and experimentation.
• Architect the infrastructure to capture, unify, and activate physician behavioral signals, including unified physician profiles, for both product and commercial use.

Experience

• 12+ years in product and engineering, including 5+ years leading product, design, and engineering as one integrated team, with managers reporting to you.
• A product you took from 0 to 1, from first idea through first paying customers, as a founder, early employee, or leader of a new venture inside a larger company, with specific, measurable results.
• Engagement products with proven retention: interactive, community, or personalized experiences, with evidence of how they changed return visits and depth of engagement.
• A forward-deployed engineering (FDE) model, or a comparable embedded model, that you set up and ran, with engineers working directly alongside clients and business stakeholders.

Technical Depth

• Architecture: you have made and owned the architecture decisions for a high-traffic production platform with high availability requirements, on modern cloud and event-driven infrastructure (AWS preferred).
• AI-native development: your teams build with AI coding agents as standard practice, and you can show the effect on cycle time and output.
• Production AI: LLM applications, recommendation systems, and real-time personalization shipped to users, not only piloted.
• First-party data: event instrumentation, identity resolution, unified profiles, and activation through a customer data platform, designed privacy-first.
• Experimentation and measurement: A/B testing, feature flags, and rollback infrastructure, plus the statistical judgment to separate real signal from noise. You know the difference between engagement metrics and insight into what users know and believe.

How You Lead

• You keep teams small and fast, ship in days rather than quarters, and hold the team to results that matter to physicians and clients.
• You make sharp calls on what to test next and act quickly on the evidence: scale, retire, or redeploy.
• You treat Editorial, Sales, and Marketing as co-builders, and you explain technical tradeoffs clearly to engineers, physicians, pharma clients, and executives.
• You operate with autonomy inside a larger organization, moving at startup speed within M3 USA standards.

Benefits:

A career opportunity with M3USA offers competitive wages, and benefits such as:

• Health and Dental
• Life, Accident and Disability Insurance
• Prescription Plan
• Flexible Spending Account
• 401k Plan and Match
• Paid Holidays and Vacation
• Sick Days and Personal Day

*M3 reserves the right to change this job description to meet the business needs of the organization

jobs.description:
ABOUT PER SCHOLAS:

For 30 years, Per Scholas has been on a mission to drive mobility and opportunity in the ever-advancing technology landscape by unlocking the untapped potential of individuals, uplifting communities, and meeting the needs of employers through rigorous tech training. By teaming up with dynamic employer partners, ranging from Fortune 500 companies to innovative startups, we're forging inclusive tech talent pipelines, fulfilling an ever-increasing need for skilled talent. With national remote training and campuses in 20+ cities and counting, Per Scholas offers no-cost training programs in the most sought-after tech skills, spanning Cloud, Cybersecurity, Data Engineering, IT Support, Software Engineering, and more. To date, 30,000+ individuals have been trained through Per Scholas, propelling their professional trajectories into high-growth tech careers with salaries three times higher than their pre-training earnings. Learn more by visiting PerScholas.org and follow us on LinkedIn, X, Facebook, Instagram, and YouTube.

Per Scholas candidates must reside in one of the following states, provided the position does not carry a specific office location requirement: AZ, CA, CO, FL, GA, IL, IN, KS, MD, MA, MI, MO, NC, NJ, NY, OH, PA, TX, WA, WI.

Position Title: Instructional Assistant (IT Support)

Location: Bronx, NY

Reports To: Director, Technical Instruction

WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR:

We are currently seeking an Information Technology Support Instructional Assistant to join our organization. This person will join our Curriculum & Adult Learning organization.

Per Scholas is seeking a dynamic, team-oriented individual to serve as an Instructor Assistant within the Buffalo Training Department. The Instructional Assistant (IA) will play an important role in our organization’s mission, as they train Per Scholas students to be outstanding entry and mid-level technicians. They will be responsible for the following:

Overall Focus:

Candidates should be able to provide effective support in the classroom and be eager to grow their technical knowledge. In particular, they should be able to:

• Assist the lead instructor both in and out of class in the teaching and administration of the class.

• Display knowledge and/or interest in the following areas: information technology, software and hardware support, network administration, technology education

What You’ll Do:

Out-of-Class Tasks and Responsibilities:

• Assist and/or collaborate with the instructor to:

• Grade and/or review assessments, class projects, and other materials

• Enter student grades into Learning Management Systems software and grading templates

• Update Salesforce data as necessary

• Review curriculum materials and assessments weekly and report to the instructor and curriculum development team any proofreading or subject-matter errors

• Assist instructor with the preparation of daily agenda for students

• Schedule time with the instructor and students to discuss class challenges

• Monitor learner attendance, certifications’ progress, etc.

• Manage learner common areas and tech supply inventory

• Attend weekly team meetings and be prepared to provide classroom and learner updates.

In-Class Tasks and Responsibilities:

• Monitor class as it is in progress - checking that overall functionality (audio, video, screen appearance, etc.) is working as needed

• Serve as class timekeeper, monitor breaks and other scheduling information

• Monitor students during test-taking and break-out group activities

• Manage and monitor assigned study groups

• Provide tutoring to underperforming learners

• Manage cleanliness of classroom and tech equipment

• Note challenges presented during class, including (but not limited to) students who:

• Seem disengaged or uninvolved with class activities

• Are speaking more than other students (dominating) or are typically quiet

Professional Qualifications

• CompTIA A+ Certification

• Ability to teach in a highly interactive and hands-on style

• Passion for teaching others

• Flexibility to adapt to changes in schedule

• Interest in being part of a culture of continuous improvement

• Team oriented

• Highly responsive communicator

• Excellent verbal communication skills

• Teaching Experience is a plus

• Qualified candidates must be able to comfortably and frequently lift 50lbs

Personal Characteristics

• You thrive in a creative, inventive, fast-paced startup environment with people who are passionate about their work and mission

• You are data-driven, result-oriented and a forward-looking catalyst for social change

• You have a collaborative and flexible work style. You’re excited to work cross-functionally with other departments and independently

• You have a passion for teaching others and being part of a culture of continuous improvement

• You are an effective communicator with strong oral and written skills

• You are strong at managing your time and you can balance multiple projects and tasks

• You stand behind our mission, believing that individuals from any community should have access to well-paying career positions, and that talent should be recognized and recruited from many diverse sources

For this role specifically, we are targeting an hourly rate of $23/hourly. The difference in salary is typically determined by several factors, including alignment with qualifications and level of experience.

Benefits & Perks

Per Scholas offers a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your health, financial well-being, and overall quality of life!

Holidays & PTO: Full-Time Per Scholas team members enjoy over 40 days of paid time off each year through a mix of holidays, vacation, and sick/personal time! All employees are eligible for Holiday pay upon hire (a total of 22 holidays annually, including a week off for Independence day and a week before the New Year). Full-Time Benefits Eligible employees also receive 80 Wellness Hours to use for Sick, Safe, or Personal reasons and accrue Vacation at a rate of 8 hours at the beginning of every month, supporting rest, recharge, and work-life balance. Vacation accruals increase with tenure. Part-time employees are afforded time off on a prorated basis and in accordance with local requirements.

Eligible employees also have access to a Health Reimbursement Account (HRA) that reimburses eligible out-of-pocket expenses, up to $4,000 for individuals and $8,000 for families.

Dental and Vision Insurance: Eligible employees can select from two dental plan options and a vision plan. Employees who waive medical coverage receive employer paid dental and vision premiums.

Retirement Savings: 401(k) plan with a current 100% employer match on contributions up to 6%, eligible employees are offered entry and full vesting after 90 days with the company.

Employee Assistance Program (EAP): Free, confidential, 24/7 access to counseling, legal support, and financial resources for employees and their household members

Parental Leave: Eligible employees are offered up to 6 weeks of 100% paid parental leave to support employees as they welcome a new child and bond with their family.

Additional Benefits & Perks: Eligible employees have access to employer-paid life and AD&D Insurance, as well as employer-paid short-term disability coverage, with the option to elect additional life coverage and long-term disability insurance. Flexible Spending accounts are available for healthcare, dependent care, and commuting expenses. Per Scholas also offers a range of voluntary benefits, including: Accident, Critical Illness, Hospital Indemnity, Legal Services, and Pet Insurance. Additional resources include healthcare concierge support, financial wellness tools, and employee discount programs.

QUESTIONS?

We start every day on a mission to empower professionals with the most trusted, innovative technology to deliver world-class outcomes for their clients and exceptional financial results for their business. They count on our purpose-built solutions to simplify operations, ensure compliance, and fuel profitable growth, so they can focus on their clients and do more of the work that matters.

What you'll do:

• Partner with Product, Support, Sales, Engineering, Marketing, and Legal and Compliance to smooth handoffs and turn customer feedback into improvements, and keep the C-suite informed with regular updates.

About you:

• Proven results improving retention and GRR and reducing churn.

• Executive presence, with clear writing and presenting that earn trust from C-level and cross-functional partners.

• A systems mindset and sharp attention to detail, with the ability to juggle competing priorities with clarity and urgency.

• Demonstrated experience leveraging AI tools and technologies to improve workflows, enhance decision-making, or drive innovation.
